News.title: Britain to pay higher Trump tariffs than EU
News.content:
Britain will pay higher tariffs than the EU after Donald Trump’s latest global trade onslaught.

Bosses in Britain have warned they will lose any competitive advantage over the bloc after the US President announced higher import taxes on goods from 60 trading partners.

The US administration imposed 10pc tariffs on both Britain and the EU to replace levies which expired overnight following a Supreme Court ruling earlier this year.

Britain must pay the import taxes on top of so-called Most Favoured Nation tariffs imposed on all members of the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

However, from Friday, the EU’s tariffs are inclusive of the WTO levies. The average WTO tariff rate is between 2.4pc to 3.5pc for non-agricultural food products.

William Bain, head of trade policy at the BCC, said: “There will be concerns about the loss of the UK’s competitive advantage over the EU and other countries which have secured a more favourable deal in other goods sectors.”

A government spokesman said: “There is no negative ‌change ‌to ⁠the tariff rate facing UK businesses as a result of this ⁠announcement.”

“Our agreement with the US remains in place, and today we see ​an improvement to our ‌trading terms with zero tariffs on whisky and medical technology.”

Jonathan Reynolds, the Business Secretary, said Scottish whisky distilleries would get a “boost” from the new tariff regime, which removes levies on scotch under a deal first announced during the King’s state visit to the US in April.

On Friday, Trump also threatened new tariffs on the European Union in response to billions worth of fines imposed on US tech giants by competition regulators.

In a post on his social media platform Truth Social, Trump said: “The United States of America is not a “PIGGYBANK” for Europe, nor will we allow it to be!”

The US president said he expected to impose “substantial tariffs” on the EU after the European Commission fined Google €890m (£760m) on Thursday.

UK and European stock markets shrugged off the latest tariffs, with the FTSE 100 up 0.9pc.

However, Wall Street was more mixed. The S&P 500 was roughly flat, while the Nasdaq Composite was down 1.1pc. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 0.3pc near the end of Friday’s trading session.

It followed dramatic falls in Asia overnight, with Japan’s Nikkei falling 2.7pc and South Korea’s Kospi down 5.7pc.

News.title: Mason Mount offering Michael Carrick a midfield solution which could have legs
News.content:
It is not uncommon to hear football club executives talking about the importance of the “money being on the pitch”.

In other words, managers having their best players fit and available most if not all of the time. Quality at the top level is essential but so is robustness. They go hand in hand.

Unfortunately for Manchester United, the money has not been on the pitch down the years nearly as much as the club would want or expect.

Bruno Fernandes stands out for what he does with the ball primarily, but also because he plays almost every minute of every game and, while his sheer indefatigability is extreme, United know they need more of his ilk.

This is why the forthcoming season is such a big one for Mason Mount. His quality has seldom been in doubt. The problem is he has rarely been on the pitch long or consistently enough to show it.

Indeed, the one-time England midfielder has started just 25 Premier League matches since his £60m move from Chelsea three years ago and that perennial unavailability is one of the reasons doubts were being cast about his Old Trafford future going into this summer.

Yet Michael Carrick was keen to keep Mount, United have rebuffed inquiries around him and intriguingly the 27-year-old could yet have an impact on what the club do during the remaining six weeks of the transfer window.

For the second time in the space of six days, Mount was deployed in a deeper midfield role alongside new £48m, signing Andrey Santos for Friday’s resounding 5-0 victory over Norwegian side Rosenborg in Trondheim, just as he had done against Wrexham last weekend.

News.title: Eleanor Cardwell: ‘Comfortable sportswear should not be expensive’
News.content:
What sports shoes do you recommend?

Robert, South West

The sports shoes that I’m currently wearing are from Puma. They’re very comfortable and have support. I actually wear a basketball shoe at the minute to have more support up the ankle.

A lot of the girls wear Asics as well, which I know is the netball shoe. I’ve worn Puma for the last four years, so I would recommend them.

But honestly, whatever works best for you, you have to try them out. Whatever is best for your instep and whatever is comfiest. And if you need more ankle support, you can put some ankle braces on.

How has playing for Manchester Thunder helped you develop as a player?

Jason, London

Manchester has massively helped me develop as a player. I’ve been playing here since 2012. As a young girl, it created me as a person, to be honest with you. It’s such a family environment that I think a lot of my values come from this club. So my family values, being connected, creating energy – all those things come rooted from this club, which is incredible.

I think whatever step you are in your career, whether you’re a young athlete or senior, they help you develop. Even now I’m 31, they’re still helping me learn new things on the court. The coaches are incredible, and I’m constantly learning and being inspired by them every single week.

Do players retire from elite netball quite young?

Helen, South West

I think it depends on the athlete. Some can retire at 40, and that’s because their bodies are so conditioned, and they might not have had any major injuries in their career. They’re able to continue to push themselves all the way until 40.

But I’d say the average is probably mid-30s. Now the Super League has become professional, the younger athletes are getting better training from a younger age. We want to keep pushing ourselves to play as long as possible.

How can netball get more coverage when women’s football is constantly pushed?

Sarah, South West

I think netball needs to have more sponsors to get more media coverage. Bigger sponsors.

Players need to put their personalities more out there on social media, so brands will want to work with us. Everyone’s got amazing personalities in netball. They [brands] should want to be a part of the netball players’ stories and the netball teams.

But it’s about getting as much exposure as possible, and making sure that everyone is going on YouTube or BBC, so more people are able to learn about the sport.

I loved netball at school. How do I get involved now in my 60s?

Sue, Yorkshire

Netball is for everyone. I personally love going to walking netball sessions and taking them through classes. You can go to the England Netball website and find out where you can play locally.

There’s also Back to Netball, depending on your ability and what you want to get out of it. Personally, I think walking netball is so much fun. The women who are in those sessions are a huge laugh, and I know when I retire, I’m going to be joining a group, for sure.

Apart from netball, what other hobbies do you have? How do they help you relieve the pressure of competition?

George, London

I feel like over the past few years I’ve really got into some new hobbies. I love reading. I love fantasy reading, like Throne of Glass. I love BookTok, so I’ve really got into that.

I’m also very crafty. I like making things – I’ve made little crochet bees for all the girls, and I like drawing, and painting occasionally – just wholesome activities to take me away from netball life. As soon as I zone in on an activity, I’m locked in and I have to complete it.

Sports.title: Chelsea flop Benoit Badiashile lined up for Napoli transfer as Blues close in on Lacroix signing
Sports.content:
NAPOLI are interested in signing Chelsea defender Benoît Badiashile following an injury to Alessandro Buongiorno.

Massimiliano Allegri‘s side are closely monitoring the French centre-back as they look to bolster their backline ahead of the new season, with the Italian club planning to offer him a three-year contract.



Badiashile is keen on continuing his career in Serie A, though he is also attracting interest from unnamed Premier League clubs.

Chelsea are open to selling Badiashile as part of a major defensive overhaul under Xabi Alonso.



The Blues had initially explored using the 25-year-old in a potential swap deal with Crystal Palace for Maxence Lacroix.

However, Palace have now made it clear that Axel Disasi is their primary preference to be included in any agreement for Lacroix.



Talks are ongoing between Palace and Disasi’s representatives, and the move is expected to become official once personal terms are finalised.

Should any unexpected complications arise with Disasi, Palace could re-open discussions for Badiashile.

But the French defender remains strongly drawn to the option of moving to Italy with Napoli.

Allegri, who replaced former Chelsea boss Antonio Conte in Naples this summer, is eager to strengthen his defence before the start of the 2026/27 campaign as he looks to return the club to the top of Italian football.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Chelsea signed Badiashile from Monaco in a £35million deal in 2023, handing the defender a seven-and-a-half-year contract after identifying him as one of Europe’s brightest young centre-backs.

The move came after Badiashile broke into the France senior side while still at Monaco, earning two international caps in 2022 before the Blues swooped for his signature.

Since arriving at Stamford Bridge, the Frenchman has made 71 appearances in all competitions but has struggled to establish himself as a first-team regular.

Napoli know exactly how important a solid defence can be as they won the Serie A title in the 2024/25 season with the league’s best defensive record – conceding just 27 goals.



Last season, however, they finished runners-up to Inter Milan after shipping 36 goals across the campaign, meaning it is now an area Allegri is determined to tighten up.

With Chelsea closing in on the signing of Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace, Badiashile appears increasingly likely to move on in search of regular football, with Napoli emerging as one of the strongest contenders for his signature.

Sports.title: ‘F*** you and them’ – Jermaine Jenas delivers bizarre message to critics as axed BBC host dances topless over pancakes
Sports.content:
JERMAINE JENAS delivered a stinging message to his critics as he bizarrely danced topless in front of pancakes.

Former England and Tottenham star Jenas was axed from his role on Match of the Day in August 2024 after he sent inappropriate messages to two women.



He had been a regular on the BBC show and Radio 5 Live, before his wife, Ellie Penfold, also announced they had split up after 16 years together months after the complaints emerged.

Jenas spoke said he had “lost everything” following a “tough two-year period,” in a candid interview on ITV‘s Good Morning Britain show.



He also expressed his deepest regrets over his workplace conduct but added he believed he had been “punished heavily” over his mistakes.

Earlier this month, he was seen frolicking in the sea with new girlfriend, Anne Leplaideur, with the pair having gone public on their relationship last year.



But in an unorthodox Instagram post on Saturday, Jenas hit back at his critics by posting a defiant message alongside a video of himself dancing while spinning a plate of white chocolate pancakes.

Jenas also added the caption: “I no longer care how the story gets told…

“F*** you and them… Respectfully.”

The post text added: “My post workout white chocolate pancakes on a Saturday morning are legendary have a great weekend people.”

It prompted a reply from Rio Ferdinand, who cheekily said: “Okaaaaay… these tunes don’t fit the caption ffs.”

The comment was echoed by fellow ex-England international Shaun Wright-Phillips, who posted a pair of laughing emojis.

But Jenas then clapped back at Ferdinand by saying: “You don’t even know about these tunes so relax.”

He then brutally joked: “There’s never been a better combo for for a lip balm deal.. I’m still waiting to see it.”

Meanwhile, Jermaine Pennant had a playful dig about Jenas needing “them pancakes to try and out drive me,” with the former TV star declaring it was “absolute lies” in response.

Sports.title: Arsenal win 3-0 in secret behind-closed-doors friendly as Christos Tzolis bags assist on debut
Sports.content:
ARSENAL signing Christos Tzolis shone bright during the club’s first pre-season friendly against MK Dons with an assist, just two days after his arrival.

The Gunners, who were without all of their World Cup stars, dominated the Dons with a 3-0 victory earlier today in a secret behind-closed-doors encounter at the club’s Sobha Realty Training Centre.



Tzolis, 24, stood out on his unofficial debut as he started for Mikel Arteta’s side down the left wing.

The winger created the North Londoners’ opener as he set up Reiss Nelson after just ten minutes.



That was after the Greece international teed up Nelson, 26, for the opener inside the box only one minute into the game but the latter’s effort was blocked by MK Dons goalkeeper Craig MacGillvary.

The ex-Club Brugge star, who joined the Premier League champions after a £35million deal that saw him signing a five-year contract, dominated the left wing throughout the entirety of the first half.

Tzolis formed an impressive pairing with left-back Riccardo Calafiori down the flank.

That led to Arsenal‘s second just six minutes before half-time with Ethan Nwaneri on target.

Arteta shook things up significantly in the second half as he fielded a very youthful side.

The Spanish tactician made eight changes, with only Kepa Arrizabalaga, Marli Salmon and Louie Copley remaining on the pitch.

Arsenal completed their win with their first big chance of the second half when a fine chipped ball over the top from Demiane Agustien found Ceadach O’Neill who hit the back of the net.

Tzolis’ fellow summer signing Islan Meslier also made his unofficial debut when he replaced Kepa between the sticks on 59 minutes.

Sports.title: Hilarious moment Erling Haaland leads Man City team-mate Donnarumma’s suited wedding guests in Viking Row
Sports.content:
ERLING HAALAND had fans in stitches as he led a Viking Row in the strangest of locations.

Haaland and his Norway team-mates helped popularise the viral ‘row’ celebration during the World Cup.



The sensation involves a single leader thumping a drum twice to set a rhythm, before a crowd of people sat in lines mimicked a rowing motion while chanting “Row!”

The unique trend captured the hearts of fans in the US, with the Norway players quickly joining in on their own version on the pitch led by Martin Odegaard after knocking out Brazil.



And now Haaland has debuted his skill on the drums as he led a rendition at the wedding of his Manchester City team-mate Gianluigi Donnarumma.

The Italian goalkeeper tied the knot with his glamorous partner Alessia Elefante at a lavish event in their home country.

And Haaland, who turned 26 on Tuesday, clearly brought his signature energy to the event.

He got up on stage and beat the drum as dozens of party guests sat on the floor and rowed in time with him.

He even laughed out loud and had to stop to give one participant instructions on how to do the viral celebration.

Fans loved the hilarious interaction from the big Norwegian.

One supporter wrote: “Guy with zero haters.”

Another gushed: “I am laughing omgggg. This looks like a fun wedding.”

And a third joked: “This guy is sensational LMAOOOOOOO.”

Haaland was in attendance alongside his stunning partner Isabel Haugseng Johansen.



Some of Italy‘s biggest footballing names were also on the scene.

Sandro Tonali, Nicolo Barella and even Paolo Maldini graced the ceremony as Donnarumma said ‘I do’ to his childhood sweetheart, who had their first son in 2024.

Sports.title: ‘Do not just fail to turn up’ – Woking blast Jermain Defoe in lengthy statement after ex-England star’s shock sacking
Sports.content:
WOKING have issued a damning statement following the departure of Jermain Defoe as manager.

The former England star left the National League club on Thursday after just four months in charge.



Defoe managed a total of six league games after being named as the replacement for Neal Ardley in March, winning two of those games to see the club finish 10th in the league.

However, the 43-year-old released a statement on social media saying it had become “impossible for me to continue in the position,” adding the experience had been “eye-opening”.



But Woking have now hit back in a statement of their own, insisting the former Tottenham and Sunderland ace was supported by the higher-ups at the club and going so far as to slam Defoe for “not turning up” to a meeting.

A statement from Woking director of football, Jody Brown, said: “I do not intend to discuss internal matters more than necessary or attribute blame. I’ve seen the speculation.



“Instead, I want to make clear that the club was fully committed to supporting Jermain in every sense throughout his time in the role.

“All player recruitment, staffing decisions and football matters were heavily influenced by Jermain, and he was given the necessary operational and board support.

“In any organisation there are processes to follow. Just days before his departure, the club were delighted to finalise the signing of an excellent player identified by Jermain, again illustrating the support the club had given right up until his final day.”

Brown continued: “However, in recent weeks there had been feedback from across the club, including players, staff and other departments, regarding growing concerns.



“To better understand the situation, I asked Jermain and Paul for a brief report outlining the squad’s current depth, recruitment targets and any operational challenges, so we could provide the support required and accelerate preparations for the season.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“That report was requested on more than one occasion but was never received.

“A meeting was subsequently scheduled involving the directors, manager, assistant manager and Head of Operations to review preparations for the season.

“Neither Jermain nor his assistant attended that meeting or that day’s training session.

“Throughout his tenure, Jermain had never communicated any serious concerns directly to me, so I am not going to speculate on his reasons.



“Every football club faces challenges. Players want more game time, improved contracts or transfers.

“The media team might want better equipment, the medical department more interns, the strength and conditioning staff larger gym space, and the car park attendants may want more coffee.

“But people do not just fail to turn up.”

Brown concluded the lengthy statement by saying it highlighted lessons around communication for himself and the club, before wishing Defoe and his staff success in the future.

In his own statement, Defoe confirmed a mutual exit agreement before saying he was unable to continue in the role due to unspecified circumstances.



He said: “I can confirm that I have mutually agreed to leave my position as manager of Woking FC. Unfortunately, circumstances have ultimately made it impossible for me to continue in the position.

“I am extremely proud of the work undertaken during my time at the club and genuinely felt that we were building something special.

“I would like to thank Todd Johnson for giving me the opportunity to manage the club. I am incredibly grateful to the supporters and, most importantly, the players, who I am genuinely gutted for.

“The group is a fantastic one, and I wish the squad every success for the season ahead.

“Really disappointed the journey has ended so soon, but I leave with great pride in what Paul Bracewell, Karl Halabi and I were building at the club.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“My time at Woking FC has been an eye-opening managerial experience and one that will undoubtedly make me stronger for the next challenge in my career.”

SunSport has approached Defoe for comment.

Sports.title: Is it fair Argentina have an automatic spot in World Cup 2030?
Sports.content:
ARGENTINA have already secured their place in the 2030 World Cup after a never seen before Fifa decision to have six co-hosts.

The team missed out on winning this year’s World Cup after a 1-0 extra time defeat to Spain – that was followed by an ugly brawl.

The majority of the matches will be held in Spain, Portugal and Morocco but Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay are also set to have one match each on their shores.

Arsenal and Manchester United have both been linked with a move for Aston Villa star Ollie Watkins, with both Premier League clubs holding a long-standing interest in the striker

Arsenal can pull on Ollie Watkins' heartstrings in order to beat Manchester United in the battle to sign him. Waktins, 30, has emerged as a target for both Premier League giants as the summer transfer window hots up.

‌



The striker has been away representing England at the World Cup but is shifting his focus back to club football now that the tournament has finished. Aston Villa fended off interest from United last summer, while Arsenal saw a £60million bid rejected in January 2025.

‌



Now, a report has claimed that Watkins could be available for £40m, with Turkish heavyweights Fenerbahce also keen to sign him. It's added that Villa are already lining up a replacement: Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson, who spent last season on loan at Bayern Munich.

‌



Arsenal are looking to bring in a striker, with Julian Alvarez understood to be their top target. But Watkins represents another Premier League-proven option - and he's shown willingness to join the Gunners before.

Sports.title: Man Utd have Erik ten Hag to blame as another Marcus Rashford escape route blocked
Sports.content:
Man Utd have Erik ten Hag to blame as another Marcus Rashford escape route blocked

Marcus Rashford still has two years left on his £325,000-a-week Manchester United contract and it has made finding a permanent transfer close to impossible this summer

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford's status at Manchester United has changed significantly in the past few years (Image: Getty Images)

Three years ago, Marcus Rashford was on top of the world. The Manchester United academy graduate was signing a bumper new five-year contract with his boyhood club on the back of the best season of his career.

‌



Rashford returned 30 goals and 12 assists in 56 appearances in the 2022-23 campaign, becoming the first player to breach the 30-goal mark for United since Robin van Persie in 2012-13 season. His reward was a gigantic pay rise, from £200,000-a-week to £325,000-a-week.

‌



He was 25 years old and, as John Murtough said in the announcement, in the prime of his career.

‌



"As he enters his prime years, we know there is still so much more to come from him, and we can see the hunger that Marcus feels to achieve the highest levels of success here at Manchester United," United's then football director said.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd drop clearest hint yet over Marcus Rashford's future as club bosses reach out READ MORE :

“Working with Erik ten Hag and his coaches is the perfect environment for Marcus to continue to develop into one of the best attacking players in the world.”

‌



"I couldn’t be more excited for the future under this manager," Rashford said of Ten Hag, who himself had just signed a one-year contract extension with United, yet would only last a further three months in the role.

United were delighted with the situation at the time. And while Rashford's form hasn't dropped off a cliff - he got 14 goals and 14 assists last season after all - that contract has caused all kinds of problems, becoming a weight the forward has had to drag around.

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford is likely to stay with Manchester United this summer due to his gigantic wages (Image: Jose Breton/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

‌



Rashford still has two years left on his £325,000-a-week deal at United, but neither he nor the club want him to fulfil it. United are desperate to offload the England international and the feeling is mutual.

A permanent move to Barcelona, where he flourished on loan in 2025-26, has not materialised, with the Catalan giants going for Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi instead of paying £26m for his services. And now, after the conclusion of the World Cup, Rashford is stuck.

United want him off their wage bill, yet despite many interested parties, there is no deal that suits them. Barcelona wanted another loan, while United are unwilling to sell to a Premier League rival.

‌



View 3 Images Erik ten Hag and John Murtough were the men behind Marcus Rashford's bumper deal (Image: PA)

Rashford rejected approaches from Galatasaray and Fenerbahce, leaving no realistic exit routes left. A report from La Gazzetta dello Sport sums up the issue. United are in talks with Roma over the signing of France midfielder Manu Kone, who is valued at €60million (£51m) by his club.

Michael Carrick's side don't want to pay that much for the World Cup star and, it is noted, could offer Rashford as part of a deal. Yet his sky-high wages would make him, by some distance, the highest-paid player in Serie A and therefore is way out of Roma's league.

‌



Under Sir Jim Ratcliffe's ownership, United have made a point of cost-cutting across every department, even if it brings negative headlines. The club's top brass must be cursing former manager Ten Hag, ex-executive Murtough and the other old decision-makers.

Rashford is still away on holiday at present, having been given a three-week break after the conclusion of England's World Cup campaign. But through no fault of his own, his colossal wages mean he is set to return to United - a club that don't want him - against his own wishes.

Vinicius Jr transfer: Arsenal's move to sign Real Madrid star to be BLOCKED by Jose Mourinho

Arsenal would be interested in signing Brazil star Vinicius Junior from Real Madrid should he fail to sign a new contract in Spain, but it appears that Jose Mourinho is keen to halt an exit

View 2 Images Arsenal are interested in a move from Vinicius Junior (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal's potential move for Vinicius Junior looks set to be ruined before it’s even begun, with Jose Mourinho poised to intervene. The Gunners hold an interest in the Brazil international, who sees his contract at the Bernabeu expire next summer.

‌



The North London side have explored a move, with Gunners chiefs having approved a move at all levels of the club. As it stands, no club-to-club talks have taken place, as first reported by The Athletic.

‌



Real would be keen on selling Vinicius for a considerable fee as opposed to losing him for nothing at the end of his deal. But it appears that new boss Jose Mourinho might want a say.

‌



According to The Telegraph, the former Chelsea and Manchester United boss would put a stop to any exit after expressing a desire for all of his key players to remain at the club ahead of his first season in charge following his return.

Mourinho returned to Madrid in the summer following a spell with Portuguese side Benfica. He was named as Alvaro Arbeloa’s replacement, the Spaniard having now joined Fulham following his exit.

Mourinho’s relationship with Vinicius was already under the spotlight ahead of his move back to Spain. His comments after the Brazilian was allegedly racially abused by Benfica’s Gianluca Prestianni in a Champions League showdown between the two teams were widely criticised.

‌



Asked at the time if the winger had aggravated the crowd, Mourinho replied: “Yes. I believe so.

View 2 Images Jose Mourinho is not keen on Vinicius Junior leaving Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

"It should be the crazy moment of the game, an amazing goal. Unfortunately [he was] not just happy to score that astonishing goal. When you score a goal like that, you celebrate in a respectful way."

‌



He added: "I told [Vinicius], when you score a goal like that you just celebrate and walk back. When he was arguing about racism, I told him the biggest person in the history of this club [Eusebio] was black.

"This club, the last thing that it is, is racist. If in his mind there was something in relation to that, this is Benfica. They [Vinicius and Prestianni] told me different things. But I don't believe in one or another. I want to be an independent."

Vinicius has been with Real Madrid since a move from Brazilian side Flamengo in 2018. He has made 376 appearances since then and has scored 128 goals, helping Real to three league titles, two Champions Leagues and much more.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe makes telling Bruno Guimaraes transfer admission as Arsenal prepare £70m bid
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe makes telling Bruno Guimaraes transfer admission as Arsenal prepare £70m bid

Newcastle have already been forced to sell Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon in the summer transfer window and could lose yet another key player in Bruno Guimaraes, who wants to join Arsenal

View 2 Images Eddie Howe appears resigned to losing Bruno Guimaraes (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Eddie Howe has admitted that he doesn't know if Newcastle will keep hold of captain Bruno Guimaraes this summer, as speculation linking him with a move to Arsenal gathers pace.

‌



Newcastle have already sold midfielder Sandro Tonali to Tottenham and forward Anthony Gordon to Barcelona, banking around £170million in the process. And now the prospect of losing Guimaraes to the Premier League champions is looking increasingly likely.

‌



The Gunners are ready to test the Magpies' resolve with a £70m bid for the Brazil international. That is reportedly short of their valuation of £80m, but the 28-year-old is keen to leave St James' Park this summer and that could prove to be the deciding factor.

‌



Guimaraes is yet to return to Newcastle as they prepare for the 2026-27 campaign, having been given three weeks off after playing for Brazil at the World Cup. But speaking after a disappointing 1-1 draw with Gateshead on Saturday, Howe struck a downbeat tone on the situation.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal exploring stunning Vinicius Junior transfer as Real Madrid star's move approved READ MORE :

"I have spoken to him normally as I would do," the Newcastle boss said. "Bruno is a fantastic person and we had some really good conversations before and during the World Cup and after the World Cup.

‌



"What we speak about has to remain private. He is a great player and a great person."

He added: "Look, I don't know what is going to happen with Bruno's future, that is for other people to speculate about. But also conversations that I'm not part of."

Asked about the plan for his return in pre-season, Howe said: "Yes, I think the plan off the top of my head, I think it's 31st [July].

‌



View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes is still on holiday after playing for Brazil at the World Cup (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

"I think he's due back, so he gets an extended break because he went further in the competition and he's enjoying a holiday at the moment with his family. There's nothing to say that Bruno won't be back training with us."

Newcastle have signed midfielder Aladji Bamba from Monaco for £34m, which goes some way to replacing Tonali. They have also signed Sean Steur, Ewen Jaouen and Bazoumana Toure, yet there are familiar frustrations around transfers on Tyneside, with their best players heading for the exit after a 12th-place finish in the Premier League last season.

‌



Asked about a comparison with the £125m sale of Alexander Isak to Liverpool last summer, Howe said: "I don't think it's fair to compare situations and what happened previously. I think you've got to look at it in its own right. Bruno is the captain of our football club.

"He's been an unbelievable player and person all through the time that we've worked together. I speak on behalf of everyone at the football club. We absolutely love him and, of course, everyone would want him to stay."

Arsenal are yet to make a formal approach to Newcastle for Guimaraes and will be met with a rejection if they bid £70m. Guimaraes has made 195 appearances for Newcastle since joining from Lyon in 2022 and still has two years left on his Magpies contract.

Sports.title: Barcelona release statement as Nou Camp worker dies during stadium redevelopment
Sports.content:
Barcelona release statement as Nou Camp worker dies during stadium redevelopment

Barcelona have said they regret that a worker has died while working on the Nou Camp renovation, as club president Joan Laporta offered his personal condolences

View 2 Images A worker has died during the redevelopment of the Nou Camp

A man who was working on the Nou Camp renovation has died, with Barcelona offering their support to his grieving family.

‌



The 54-year-old, who has not been named, is thought to have died as a result of "a blow" while working on Friday, the Catalan regional police said. The iconic stadium has been undergoing major work for almost three years and the emergency services were called to the stadium. His death has led to an investigation.

‌



Work at the stadium began in June 2023 and is expected to be completed in early 2028, as Barcelona look to bolster their capacity to 105,000 - making it one of the largest grounds in the world.

‌



The club put out a statement following the tragedy which read: "FC Barcelona deeply regrets the death of the worker who lost his life yesterday in the workplace accident that occurred during the renovation works at Spotify Camp Nou. The club wishes to express its deepest condolences and extend its heartfelt support to his family, friends, and colleagues.

Arsenal exploring stunning Vinicius Junior transfer as Real Madrid star's move approved READ MORE :

"FC Barcelona president Joan Laporta wishes to personally convey his condolences to the family and places himself at their disposal on behalf of the entire club."

Barcelona's rivals, Real Madrid, have revamped the Bernabeu over the past decade, making it one of the most iconic and aesthetically impressive stadiums in the world. Barca have now responded as they look to modernise their stadium.

‌



They returned to their iconic home back in November after more than two years when they beat Athletic Bilbao in front of a reduced capacity of 45,401 with cranes and construction work still very much taking place. The overall project is set to cost around £1.1billion.

View 2 Images Barcelona returned to a partially finished Nou Camp back in November (Image: The incident occurred while work was carried out at the Spotify Camp Nou (file))

Since moving back to the Nou Camp, Barcelona have won every single home game in La Liga. The only team to secure a result there was Atletico Madrid, who registered a 2-0 victory en route to knocking out the Catalans in the last eight of the Champions League.

Barcelona memorably won the first El Clasico back at the Nou Camp in May by downing Real 2-0, in turn securing La Liga. Hansi Flick's side are eyeing up a hat-trick of Spanish titles as they prepare for a full season back into their long-term home.

Sports.title: Arsenal plot return dates for World Cup stars as one trains at former club
Sports.content:
Arsenal plot return dates for World Cup stars as one trains at former club

Arsenal are preparing to welcome back a host of their World Cup stars, who will return in phases, as they face decisions over the fitness of Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka

View 3 Images Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka were both monitored by England for fitness issues during the World Cup (Image: MB Media/Getty Images)

Arsenal are readying for the return of several of their World Cup stars - but face decisions on how best to manage Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka.

‌



Several of the Gunners' players have been back as they're put through their paces, but the majority of their big-hitters were present at this summer's tournament. Those players are entitled to a minimum of three weeks off after their involvement for their countries.

‌



England stalwart Rice has been managing neural pain in his hamstring for more than six months. He was also hampered by sickness during the World Cup and that meant he was hauled off at half-time during the quarter-final win over Norway.

‌



Saka was held back for much of the tournament by Thomas Tuchel, who claimed he was still playing through the pain barrier following an Achilles injury. The winger himself claimed it was fit and healthy and wanted to play more, but Arsenal will now assess him and his colleague as they seek to get them primed for the season.

Kai Havertz is expected to return in the coming days, reports the Evening Standard, but the versatile forward has been training at his former club Bayer Leverkusen this week in preparation.

Piero Hincapie and Viktor Gyokeres have also had their three weeks of holiday after the World Cup and should return next week. Brazilian duo Gabriel and Gabriel Martinelli are also due to be back at the start of next week.

‌



Arsenal will play against Girona in Spain on August 1 and Arteta will have some of his World Cup players back, but the clash will come too soon for the likes of Martin Odegaard. Over the 11 days that follows that game they will face Real Betis, Borussia Dortmund and Como.

View 3 Images Kai Havertz has been going through his paces at Bayer Leverkusen ahead of his return (Image: Getty Images)

Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke were part of England's squad but were by no means regulars, meaning they will be fresher than some ahead of their return.

‌



Norway were beaten by England was on July 11, meaning Odegaard will be available to train again in the week commencing August 3. Spain duo David Raya and Martin Zubimendi have been celebrating their country's triumph played very little football.

Mikel Merino proved himself to be a huge hit off the bench, scoring late winners against Portugal and Belgium, but his impact role meant his minutes were limited, which will aid him in pre-season.

View 3 Images Mikel Merino was a star off the bench, but was not heavily utilised by Spain (Image: Getty Images)

Sports.title: Russell forced to change power unit for Hungarian GP after water leak
Sports.content:
George Russell has been forced to change his power unit ahead of the Hungarian Grand Prix after a crack on his engine caused a water leak in qualifying.

Russell qualified a disappointing seventh for Sunday's race but came to a halt at the end of Q3 as the team detected a loss of water pressure.

It means the Mercedes driver will take on his fourth power unit of 2026 but will not be hit with a grid penalty as the change is to the same specification and does not take him above the season-limit of four engines.

Mercedes believe the water leak happened after Russell ran over the exit kerb at Turn 4 during his final run in Q3, where he did not improve his lap time.

"We lost water pressure and I had a water leak. When I stopped on track, the car was leaking a load of water," Russell, who is 50 points behind championship leader and team-mate Kimi Antonelli, told Sky Sports F1.

"Fingers crossed it doesn't affect anything for the race."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell reacts to stopping on track during qualifying at the Hungarian Grand Prix due to a water leak

It is the latest unreliability issue for Mercedes which has impacted both Russell and Antonelli in recent races.

Both drivers have lost valuable points due to engine-related retirements this season but Russell was "lost for words" at the previous race in Belgium after a bug in the power unit software led to a lack of straight line speed performance and a race-ending collision with Lewis Hamilton at Spa-Francorchamps.

Mercedes have fixed the bug for this weekend's Hungarian Grand Prix.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver George Russell spins after contact with Lewis Hamilton and his race ends on the opening lap, but was the Ferrari driver's penalty fair?

"The software is the same for all the cars, and it was there in every car, but it affected George more than Kimi," explained Mercedes technical director Simone Resta on Friday.

"We also need to bear in mind that, when comparing their performance in the last few races, Kimi was on a fresher power unit, which is, of course, always a bit better than quite a used power unit.

"That will change in the next races when we start to have a fresher power unit on George's side. So, there's a bit of everything. There's a bit of software, but there's also Kimi being out of phase with George's programme. You sum up everything when you look at the final result."

Russell: Would have been nice to be higher up

But, even prior to Saturday's water leak in Hungary, Russell was off the pace compared to team-mate Antonelli - a continuation of their pace gap during the European run of events.

Russell faces the prospect of seeing his 50-point deficit to Antonelli in the championship increase and the British driver is unsure how easy it will be to get into the fight for the podium to potentially limit the damage.

"We were probably even further on Friday but we had the strongest race pace, which tends to say it's not a car problem but a tyre problem," he said.

"Time will tell in the race if we struck the right balance between the qualifying setup and race setup. We probably know we could make the car faster in qualifying trim at the expense of race performance.

"It's going to be difficult to overtake. It would have been nice to be higher up."

Sports.title: Hamilton loses second on Hungarian GP grid after penalty
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has been relegated from second to fifth on the Hungarian Grand Prix grid after a penalty for blocking McLaren's Oscar Piastri at the end of qualifying.

Hamilton lost out on pole position to Lando Norris in the other McLaren by the narrowest of margins after failing to improve his provisional-pole time, but then soon found himself placed under investigation by stewards for an incident involving Piastri.

Hamilton had been the first of the leading drivers to complete his final lap - positioning he was left surprised by - and as he slowed down once he crossed the line, he appeared to block Piastri through Turn One as the McLaren started its final timed attempt behind him.

Stewards summoned both drivers and team representatives after qualifying to review the incident and ultimately judged that Hamilton had unnecessarily impeded Piastri, handing him a three-place grid demotion.

10) Nico Hulkenberg, Audi

The penalty promotes Hamilton's Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc to second place on Sunday's grid behind Norris and, as it stands, world championship leader Kimi Antonelli up to third and Piastri to fourth.

Antonelli, though, is the subject of a separate stewards' investigation over an alleged failure to slow for yellow flags waving when Max Verstappen spun on his final Q3 lap at the final corner.

Speaking before the penalty was confirmed, Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur said any blame fell on the team and not Hamilton.

Vasseur told Sky Sports F1: "We told him [about Piastri] but it was far too late.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton said he was expecting the worst as stewards investigate the alleged blocking incident with Oscar Piastri during Qualifying at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

"If there's a mistake, it's our mistake."

Hamilton himself said soon after qualifying: "I was told literally when he was at the apex behind me, so I had no idea he was coming. I thought everyone came out behind me. I was the first out, so I thought everyone had finished the lap.

"I think Charles was coming up behind me when I left the pit lane, as far as I was aware.

"Crazy, because it had been clean, and obviously it wasn't intentional."

Sports.title: Norris snatches Hungarian GP pole before Hamilton penalty shuffles order
Sports.content:
McLaren’s Lando Norris snatched Hungarian Grand Prix pole from Lewis Hamilton before the Ferrari driver was later demoted from second on the grid by a penalty for impeding.

Hamilton appeared to be on course to claim his first Grand Prix pole since the same event three years ago when he was a tenth clear of Norris after the first runs in Q3, but the McLaren driver found improvement as his rivals struggled on the second run to edge 12 thousandths of a second clear of his compatriot.

It turned out that Norris would have claimed pole regardless, as Hamilton was later demoted from second to fifth on the grid by a penalty incurred for impeding the other McLaren of Oscar Piastri during Q3.

Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli, who leads Hamilton by 45 points at the top of the Drivers' Championship, had finished fourth behind the other Ferrari of Charles Leclerc as the Silver Arrows' streak of 10 poles to start the season came to an end, but both drivers move a place up the grid as a result of the seven-time world champion's penalty.

Piastri earns a promotion to fourth, but Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who spun at the final corner on his final flying lap, stays where he ended the session in sixth.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris snatches pole off Lewis Hamilton as Max Verstappen and George Russell struggle in Q3 at Hungaroring.

George Russell's struggles continued as he finished seventh, with further concern arising when his Mercedes suffered a power unit issue and broke down on his in-lap at the end of the session.

Antonelli also remains at risk of a grid penalty as he awaits the outcome of a post-session investigations for not sufficiently slowing as he approached yellow flags warning him of Verstappen's spin.

A 17th career pole for reigning world champion Norris is his first since the Las Vegas Grand Prix in November last year, and comes on a weekend where McLaren brought a significant upgrade package to a car that had largely underwhelmed to this point in 2026.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton's P2 is under threat as Oscar Piastri was blocked during qualifying at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

Norris said: "A tough qualifying. These guys [Ferrari] were very quick. It's been tight the whole weekend but we seemed quick from the first laps we did and we brought a few upgrades.

"It's hard to know how much it helps in terms of lap time but it certainly helped today. Very happy to be back on top, especially at a track where you certainly want to be on pole."

British rookie Arvid Lindblad continued his strong form for Racing Bulls by claiming ninth, while Nico Hulkenberg rounded out the top 10 for Audi.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anthony Davidson takes a look at Lando Norris' flying lap to take Pole position at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

Fernando Alonso provided some encouragement for Aston Martin as he took advantage of his heavily upgraded car to get the team into Q2 for the first time this season.

While Alonso will start from 16th after finishing last in Q2, the performance indicates progress ahead of another huge weekend for Aston Martin following the summer break at the Dutch Grand Prix when their engine supplier Honda will also bring a significant upgrade.

Sports.title: Kalpana defeats Calandagan in King George battle
Sports.content:
Kalpana battled her way to a thrilling victory in the international clash of the generations landing a thrilling King George VI And Queen Stakes at Ascot.

Wearing the same Juddmonte colours carried to victory by three-time winner Enable, the five-year-old mare exacted sweet revenge on her conqueror 12 months earlier when she had finished second to Calandagan.

Sweeping into the lead well over a furlong out off the back of a ferocious pace set by Ballydoyle pacemaker Action, the Andrew Balding-trained mare powered clear up the straight.

From there to the line she galloped on strongly to hold off the surge of last year's winner Calandagan to win by one and a half lengths at 13-2.

Irish Derby winner Benvenuto Cellini stayed on well to finish third under Ryan Moore with last year's dual Derby winner Lambourn in fourth.

A field containing the last two winners, Derby heroes, two Japanese raiders, the Arc second and the winners of multiple Group Ones looked on paper the race of year. And on the track it did not disappoint.

For Colin Keane it was his biggest victory since being appointed as Juddmonte's retained rider and he said: "She's a very special mare, we thought she was coming here with a big chance but saying that, realistically I thought if she was third it would be a massive run to the Japanese horse (Masquerade Ball) and the French horse but it just shows how good she is.

"I did think last year she improved from run to run as she's such a big girl and she does herself very well but Andrew said she was 10 kilos lighter or something today so that was a good sign.

"Hopefully she can keep going that way as the year goes on.

"I opted to come in because I thought Wayne (Lordan on Minnie Hauk) would keep going longer than he did but he kind of stopped but she came back for me and she can quicken nearly instantly when you want her, she gets you out of trouble when you need her.

"I'm more delighted for the mare, although she's won two Group Ones she's deserved a couple more and she showed her true class today.

"That's definitely her best performance, it was one of the strongest renewals of the race as there were horses from all over the globe so for her to do it today is very special.

"It's a privilege to ride in these colours and get opportunities like that."

Balding said: "She's pretty damn good isn't she? And she can do it on any ground as well!

"It worked out perfectly today and I never need to tell Colin what to do, he always knows what he's doing and it was a fabulous ride.

"I've just felt she has been better this year and it was a struggle to get weight off her last year, but this year I felt she has trained leaner and lighter and I've been happier with her all along.

"I don't know what the difference is but she is so much fitter this year and it told at the finish.

"It's a huge privilege to train for Juddmonte and these wonderful horses and it makes my job easier.

"It's an honour to win this, it's one of the most important races of the year and Dad (Ian Balding) won it of course with Mill Reef."

"Anything is possible moving forwards and we'll discuss it. The Arc didn't work out last year because of the draw and that is a danger again, but anything is possible and she's thriving on her racing, so you couldn't even rule out the Yorkshire Oaks, she's right at the top of her game."

Barry Mahon, European bloodstock and racing manager for Juddmonte, said: "Colin got a lovely trip round and was just sitting there waiting coming into the straight.

"It's one of the biggest days for me since being in my role, right up there with Bluestocking in the Arc and Field Of Gold at Royal Ascot last year. It's a memorable one for sure

"I'm not sure what the timeline is between the Arc and Champions Day is but I'm sure Paris will be in the discussions and we'll see what the owners want to do.

"It's very straightforward working with Andrew and he's having some great results for us. He's a brilliant people person, with a brilliant team and staff around him."

Regardless of that, Benfica’s António Silva is lined up to replace Marcos Senesi, while the search is continuing for a right-back. With a first season in the Europa League ahead, planning accordingly to ensure the squad is sufficiently robust to cope with a more hectic schedule than usual is paramount. WU

Major ins Álvaro Rodríguez (Elche, £21.4m) Major outs Luis Sinisterra (Cruzeiro, £5.2m), Marcos Senesi (Tottenham, free)

Brentford

Usually a big sale pushes the Bees into action but not this summer. Experience has been on the agenda, with Jaidon Anthony and Callum Wilson acquired, while the arrival of the young centre-back Jannik Schuster could mean the end of Ethan Pinnock’s time with the club. They are, as always, likely to look at bringing in players with potential. The Manchester United teenager Noah Ajayi falls into this category but whether a deal progresses remains to be seen. WU

Major ins Jaidon Anthony (Burnley, £15m), Jannik Schuster (Red Bull Salzburg, £14m), Callum Wilson (West Ham, free)

Brighton

Investing in the defence early has freed up time to do other critical business, with a central midfield refresh potentially in the offing, while there is a desire to bolster the winger bullpen. Evan Ferguson is back at the club after a loan spell at Roma but whether he has a future at the club remains to be seen. If not, finding suitable support for the 35-year-old Danny Welbeck will be part of the strategy with the a Conference League campaign awaiting. Bart Verbruggen has attracted interest in Europe and a departure would call for a new No 1 to be found. WU

Major ins Luka Vuskovic (Tottenham, £46m), Zadok Yohanna (AIK, £21.5m), Pascal Struijk (Leeds United, £18m), Costinha (Olympiakos, 11m) Major outs Jan Paul van Hecke (Tottenham, £52m), Diego Coppola (Paris FC, £15.3m), James Milner (retired), Solly March (released)

Chelsea

Marc Cucurella’s sale has left a hole to fill at left-back. Options there include a return for Newcastle’s Lewis Hall or a move for Rayo Vallecano’s Pep Chavarría. The midfield is also looking light with Andrey Santos out the door and Enzo Fernández linked with a move away. The reluctance to sign a goalkeeper suggests 20-year-old Mike Penders is not far from competing for the No 1 spot. The capture of Morgan Rogers will excite supporters, but they still crave a top centre-back and striker. BM

Major ins Morgan Rogers (Aston Villa, £117m), Marco Palestra (Atalanta, £47m), Geovany Quenda (Sporting, £40m), Emmanuel Emegha (Strasbourg, £21.6m) Major outs Marc Cucurella (Real Madrid, £52m), Andrey Santos (Manchester United, £50m), Tyrique George (Everton, £18m)

View image in fullscreen England attacker Morgan Rogers is an exciting signing for Chelsea. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA

Coventry

Without putting too fine a point on it, quality across the board is required. The club are still working on bringing the Brighton goalkeeper Carl Rushworth back after a successful loan in the Championship but price and competition for his signature will complicate matters. Finding strikers capable of converting chances will be integral to their chances of survival for Frank Lampard’s side. Norman Bassette has returned to Belgium after spending last season out of loan. WU

Major ins Loum Tchaouna (Burnley, £20m), Aurèle Amenda (Eintracht Frankfurt, £15.4m), Frank Onyeka (Brentford, undisclosed fee)

Crystal Palace

Making sure Maxence Lacroix, Jean-Philippe Mateta and Adam Wharton are still at the club come kick-off is imperative. Chelsea’s interest in Lacroix and Wharton will cause the most concern, while extending Mateta’s deal beyond the end of the season will need to be addressed. The starting lineup is strong but greater depth, with another European campaign in the offing, is imperative for the club. Óscar Mingueza was a sensible signing on a free, especially after not replacing Marc Guéhi in January. Walter Benítez may leave in search of first-team football, which would leave a gap in the goalkeeping department. WU

Major ins Óscar Mingueza (Celta Vigo, free)

Everton

Young, developing potential has been recruited so far in the form of Hayden Hackney – player of the season in the Championship with Middlesbrough in 2025-26 – Tyrique George and Merlin Röhl, the last two after loan spells with David Moyes’s side last season. But established players are still required to fill several weak spots, especially at right-back, a position that has needed strengthening for far too long now, and centre-forward. Left-back, central midfield and another wide player – the return of Jack Grealish possibly – would also be on the wishlist. Andy Hunter

Major ins Tyrique George (Chelsea, £18m), Merlin Röhl (Freiburg, £17.3m), Hayden Hackney (Middlesbrough, £16.5m) Major outs Séamus Coleman (released)

Fulham

It is a new era at Craven Cottage under Álvaro Arbeloa and there is much work to be done. The loss of Raúl Jiménez and, more important, the player of the season, Harry Wilson, means there are holes to fill. Like a year ago, it’s been a slow start to the window and things will need to speed up if they are to find a new striker, winger and a centre-back. Real Madrid’s Franco Mastantuono and Gonzalo García are under consideration, having previously worked with Arbeloa. WU

Major ins Jonah Kusi-Asare (Bayern Munich, £5.2m) Major outs Issa Diop (Ipswich, £8.5m), Harry Wilson (Leeds, free), Raúl Jiménez (Wolves, free)

View image in fullscreen Leeds signing Harry Wilson excelled last season for Fulham. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA

Hull

After avoiding an expected six-point deduction for breaching spending rules by selling the goalkeeper Ivor Pandur and the midfielder Aidon Shehu to Rangers and Panathinaikos respectively for a combined £8.5m at the end of June, the playoff winners aim to make 10-12 new signings before September. Reinforcements are required all over the pitch, with central defence, central midfield and attack particular priorities. “Think about us like a volcano,” says Hull’s owner, Acun Ilicali. “It’s boiling right now and it’s going to erupt.” Yet as much as the manager, Sergej Jakirovic, needs new faces he will be anxious to retain last season’s exceptionally powerful team spirit. Inspired loans and free transfer imports could prove crucial. Louise Taylor

Major ins Jack Butland (Rangers, £3.5m) Major outs Ivor Pandur (Rangers, £6m)

Ipswich

Promotion brings enough problems but doing so with a new manager brings added complexity as Gary O’Neil seeks to shape his squad. The aim is to be better prepared for the Premier League than last time by signing those with the physicality to compete in the top flight, preferably having done so before, hence the signing of Issa Diop. Inroads have been made but the spine of the team needs strengthening, especially in midfield and at centre-forward. WU

Major ins Emersonn (Toulouse, £24m), Abdul Fatawu (Leicester, £20m), Issa Diop (Fulham, £8.5m), Chuba Akpom (Ajax, £7m) Major outs Arijanet Muric (Sassuolo, £6m)

Leeds

Daniel Farke has traditionally preferred to operate with a small, closely bonded, first-team squad but acknowledges a little expansion is required. As the defender Joe Rodon recently put it: “We want to make our squad bigger and better.” So far, though, the goalkeeping department has shrunk appreciably, with Karl Darlow and Illan Meslier having left while Lucas Perri is coveted by Torino. If new keepers currently top Farke’s shopping list – and Manchester City’s and England’s James Trafford in particular – the Southampton central midfielder Shea Charles is not far behind. Leeds seem determined to acquire the 22-year-old but the Champonship club are reluctant sellers who will demand top dollar. With Harry Wilson and Tarik Muharemovic having already arrived to reinforce attack and central defence respectively, considerable focus is on midfield where Julian Brandt, a free agent after leaving Borussia Dortmund, is also coveted. LT

Major ins Tarik Muharemovic (Sassuolo, £34.1m), Harry Wilson (Fulham, free) Major outs Pascal Struijk (Brighton, £18m), Karl Darlow (Manchester United, free)

Liverpool

Arne Slot wanted two new wingers and a right-back before he was sacked in May and the change of head coach has not changed Liverpool’s priorities. Victor Muñoz has been signed as a versatile forward but not as an immediate starter under Andoni Iraola, and the pursuit of top wide talent continues. Bradley Barcola and Yan Diomande are of interest, although Paris Saint-Germain may determine both their futures. Iraola is concerned at the thinness of his defensive options and, while in an ideal world he would consider Conor Bradley to be Liverpool’s first-choice right back, the Northern Irishman’s recovery from a serious knee injury is likely to force another transfer move. AH. AH

Major ins Jérémy Jacquet (Rennes, £55m), Víctor Muñoz (Osasuna, £34.5m) Major outs Mohamed Salah (released), Ibrahima Konaté (Real Madrid, free), Andy Robertson (Tottenham, free)

View image in fullscreen England midfielder Elliot Anderson has completed his move to Manchester City. Photograph: Nathan Ray Seebeck/Imagn Images/Reuters

Manchester City

Elliot Anderson may already have joined for a British record transfer fee but City are still in the market for another midfielder, with the 18-year-old Morocco international Ayyoub Bouaddi being targeted for about £85m. Enzo Maresca also has Malo Gusto, one of his right-backs when he was Chelsea head coach, on the radar. A striker will be on the list, too, if Omar Marmoush leaves. And with Real Madrid retaining an interest, will Rodri sign on again? Spain’s World Cup-winning captain has a year left on his contract and his stock has rocketed. The incomings mean several players could leave, with Kalvin Phillips, Jack Grealish, Tijjani Reijnders, Nico González, Savinho and James Trafford among them. Jamie Jackson

Major ins Elliot Anderson (Nottingham Forest, £116m), Mathys Detourbet (Troyes, £21.6m), Jeremy Monga (Leicester, £12.5m) Major outs Nathan Aké (Fenerbahce, £7m), Bernardo Silva (Real Madrid, free), John Stones (free agent)

Manchester United

Michael Carrick is keen to add a third new midfielder after the arrivals of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, with Real Madrid’s Eduardo Camavinga, Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, Roma’s Manu Koné and Fulham’s Sander Berge on the list. He is also considering a move for a left-back: Newcastle’s Lewis Hall and Fulham’s Antonee Robinson are being monitored. There will be outgoings too. At 28 Marcus Rashford is in his prime and available, surely for a fee in the same region as the £26m Barcelona balked at. Player and club want an exit yet at the moment he will start the new season at United. For the right deal this will change. JJ

Major ins Andrey Santos (Chelsea, £50m), Youri Tielemans (Aston Villa, £35m) Major outs Rasmus Højlund (Napoli, £43.2m)

Newcastle

Much hinges on whether Bruno Guimarães stays or departs for Arsenal during a summer already featuring a significant changing of the St James’ Park guard. The adjustment to life after Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali could be eased if Eddie Howe is able to attract a higher calibre central midfielder – Monaco’s Aladji Bamba has joined for £34m – and goalkeeper – Parma’s Zion Suzuki is one possibility. Most signings will be expected to conform to Newcastle’s new transfer policy of recruiting players aged 24 and under, with a valuation broadly between £20m and £40m. Meanwhile Nick Pope, Joe Willock and Jacob Murphy could depart. The club are operating under a three-year Uefa settlement agreement after breaching European spending rules but Howe’s overriding current priority is keeping Guimarães. LT

Major ins Bazoumana Touré (Hoffenheim, £43m), Ewen Jaouen (Reims, £21.6m), Sean Steur (Ajax, £20m), Aladji Bamba (Monaco, £34m) Major outs Sandro Tonali (Tottenham, £92.5m), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona, £69.3m), Kieran Trippier (Wolves, free)

Nottingham Forest

Spending the money made from the Elliot Anderson sale is a top priority. Lucas Bergvall leads the list of replacements and the midfielder has told Tottenham his preference is to move to the City Ground but a deal needs to be agreed. If not, Monaco’s Lamine Camara could become part of the thinking. A new right-wingback and striker are also being plotted, with Sporting’s Ousmane Diomande a target in central defence. There is no requirement to sell any key players but the futures of some on the fringes are up in the air. WU

Major outs Elliot Anderson (Manchester City, £116m)

Sunderland

Régis Le Bris says he is hoping to add “six or seven” new players this summer. Sunderland’s manager wants to ensure the squad is sufficiently robust to cope with the twin demands of Premier League and Europa League campaigns but has been bolstered by Granit Xhaka’s decision to recommit to the club amid interest in the captain from Chelsea. If recruiting holding midfield cover for Xhaka is one transfer priority, so too is providing Brian Brobbey with high-calibre attacking competition while also fortifying the right-winger and left-back positions. Le Bris is under no pressure to sell, so any attempts to acquire his increasingly influential attacking midfielder Enzo Le Fée will be strongly resisted. LT

Major ins Thomas Meunier (Lille, free) Major outs Eliezer Mayenda (Rennes, £17.1m)

Tottenham

Despite acquiring a new central midfield and a new central defence, Roberto De Zerbi said Spurs are “not finished yet” in the transfer market. An upgrade on Richarlison up front should be a priority, while Marcus Rashford could be a blockbuster arrival out wide. As for outgoings, Cristian Romero and Lucas Bergvall could follow Luka Vuskovic and Will Lankshear through the door. Interest in Pedro Porro will be high after his outstanding World Cup and there is still uncertainty over Guglielmo Vicario’s future in goal. BM

Major ins Sandro Tonali (Newcastle, £92.5m), Mateus Fernandes (West Ham, £85m), Jan Paul van Hecke (Brighton, £52m), Andy Robertson (Liverpool, free), Marcos Senesi (Bournemouth, free), Martin Dubravka (Burnley, free) Major outs Luka Vuskovic (Brighton, £46m), Radu Dragusin (Fiorentina, loan)

Sports.title: Missing a major football tournament? Fear not, Wafcon 2026 is about to start
Sports.content:
The men’s World Cup may have finished but do not worry, the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon) is ready to pick up where Spain and Argentina left off. The 34-match event will take place between 26 July and 16 August, which sandwiches it between football’s global showpiece and the start of the league season in Europe. Here’s your guide to one of the most underrated but interesting events on the sporting calendar.

Why is it being played now?

The tournament was scheduled to take place in three Moroccan cities – Rabat, Casablanca and Fes – between 17 March and 3 April. However, only 12 days before it was due to start it was postponed for what the Confederation of African Football called “unforeseen circumstances”. Strangely, the conflict in the Middle East, which affected several travel routes, was never cited as one of them. Caf’s communications director, Luxolo September, said Morocco requested new dates “for a number of reasons”, none of which were disclosed.

South Africa appeared to offer to host the tournament, before Morocco was reconfirmed and a new window was announced. A revised match list, which included only two of the three original host cities, Rabat and Casablanca, was revealed on 25 June. The draw remained the same.

Several teams, including South Africa and Nigeria, expressed frustration at the late change, especially as they had already been playing warm-up matches in preparation for the tournament. Also, the change meant that, for many players, they will be out of season.

What is the setup?

This is the first time the tournament will be played with 16 teams – up from 12 in the past two editions – but the inclusion of the final four sides was unsatisfactory. They were added to the tournament only after the qualification process, which ran from February to October 2025, had been completed. The four sides – Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, Mali and Egypt – were picked on rankings.

While the Egypt midfielder Nadine Ghazi admitted that the team’s qualification was “different, if I can put it like that”, they hope to take inspiration from their men’s side, who reached the World Cup last 16 before losing to Argentina.

Another team that will be looking to their male counterparts’ performances for motivation is Cape Verde, who are one of two tournament debutants. Malawi are the other first-timers.

The teams are divided into four groups of four. The top two sides from each group will progress to the quarter-finals. All matches kick off at 6pm or later local time, unlike the 2025 edition, when some teams played at 3pm in extreme mid-summer heat.

Who are the favourites?

The competition’s most successful competitors, Nigeria, achieved “Mission X” and won their 10th Wafcon title in 2025, and it is difficult to look past them this time. They have retained the core of that squad, captained by Rasheedat Ajibade, but will be without the defender Ashleigh Plumptre because of a foot injury. The striker Asisat Oshoala and the goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie headline their squad.

View image in fullscreen Nigeria, who defeated Morocco in last year’s final, are aiming for a record-extending 11th Wafcon title. Photograph: Abdel Majid Bziouat/AFP/Getty Images

Morocco have been the runners-up in the past two editions and will be looking to go one better, especially as this could be the last in their trio of home tournaments. The 2028 Wafcon is set to be held elsewhere.

Other strong candidates are the 2022 champions, South Africa, who have an experienced squad, and Zambia, who were bronze medallists in 2022 and quarter-finalists in 2025.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Who are the biggest stars?

Malawi will make their first Wafcon appearance, with many eyes on sisters Tabitha and Temwa Chawinga. Tabitha, who will captain the side, plays at European powerhouse OL Lyonnes, while Temwa is at Kansas City Current, where she has been voted the NWSL’s MVP for two successive seasons. She was also the highest-ranked African player on the Guardian’s 100 best female footballers in the world last year in sixth place.

Local fans will get behind the Morocco captain, Ghizlane Chebbak, who has won the Golden Boot at the past two Wafcons, scoring eight times across those tournaments. At 35 years old, this may be her last major tournament and she will not want to move on without a trophy.

View image in fullscreen Malawi’s Tabitha Chawinga (left) and her sister Temwa will be making their Wafcon debuts.

Zambia’s NWSL heavyweights Barbra Banda and Racheal Kundananji scored three goals each at the last tournament but could not take the team past the quarter-finals. Given their reputations the pair will be hoping to ensure Zambia can continue to enhance their reputation as serious continental challengers.

Ghana were the most improved side last year, when they lost to Morocco on penalties in the semi-final. Their forward Princess Marfo, who recently signed for PSV Eindhoven, and Evelyn Badu, fresh off a hat-trick for Montreal Roses, are two to keep an eye on.

What’s at stake?

In short: money and major tournament qualification. Prize money at the last Wafcon increased by 45% in total, with each team earning at least $125,000 (£94,000) and the winners, Nigeria, pocketing $1m. This time there is something else at stake too: the four semi-finalists will qualify for the 2027 World Cup in Brazil, while the four losing quarter-finalists will play off to decide which two teams advance to the inter-confederation deciders.

Sports.title: Arsenal make shock approach to sign Vinícius Júnior from Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Arsenal are exploring a shock deal to sign Vinícius Júnior from Real Madrid. The Press Association understands that Arsenal have inquired about the Brazil international, who has one year remaining on his contract at the Bernabéu.

It is believed that any move for Vinícius – who scored 22 goals for Real last season and four for Brazil at the World Cup – is at a formative stage as Mikel Arteta looks to land a marquee signing to build on the club’s first Premier League title in more than two decades.

Vinícius, 26, fits that bill, with Atlético Madrid’s Julián Álvarez, RB Leipzig’s Yan Diomande and Bradley Barcola of Paris Saint-Germain also on their radar.

Arsenal bolstered their attacking options with the £34m signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge this week. Morgan Rogers had also been identified as a target, but it is believed Arsenal were not prepared to pay more than £80m for the England international, who ultimately joined Chelsea in a £117m deal – a British record fee.

Vinícius’s future at Real is uncertain after José Mourinho’s return and the club could cash in on the player, rather than risk losing him for nothing in a year’s time.

Mourinho, who has signed a three-year deal at the Bernabéu, was criticised for comments he made after Vinícius accused Benfica’s Gianluca Prestianni of racially abusing him during a Champions League tie in February.

Mourinho, Benfica manager at the time, said “something happens, always” in matches where Vinícius plays. Prestianni was banned for six matches after he admitted to using homophobic language towards Vinicius.

Tzolis followed Piero Hincapié – who turned his temporary deal into a full-time switch – and the goalkeeper Illan Meslier, a free signing from Leeds, as Arsenal’s third addition.

Bruno Guimarães could also move to the Emirates with Arsenal keen on signing the Brazil international from Newcastle.

Speaking after Newcastle’s 1-1 pre-season draw at Gateshead on Saturday, manager Eddie Howe said: “We don’t want to lose our best players. I’ve spoken to him [Guimarães] as I would do. Bruno is just a fantastic person. We’ve had some really good conversations, both before the World Cup, during the World Cup and after the World Cup.

“I don’t know what’s going to happen with Bruno’s future. That’s for other people to speculate about.”

Sports.title: Defoe’s shock Woking exit came after ‘growing concerns’, says club
Sports.content:
Jermain Defoe’s departure from Woking came after “growing concerns” at the club with Jody Brown, the National League side’s director of football, claiming the former Tottenham striker failed to turn up for training.

Defoe’s contract at the National League club was mutually terminated on Thursday after four months in charge. In is first managerial job, the 43-year-old oversaw two wins and one defeat in six matches. The former England forward had said it was “impossible for me to continue” and described his time at the club as an “eye-opening” experience.

But the club responded strongly on Saturday. “The recommendation to appoint Jermain as manager was mine, and I take full responsibility for it,” Brown said. “After meeting with him on several occasions, I believed he was the right person to lead the club into an exciting new era.”

But he went on: “However, in recent weeks there had been feedback from across the club, including players, staff and other departments, regarding growing concerns.

“To better understand the situation, I asked Jermain and Paul [Bracewell, the assistant manager] for a brief report outlining the squad’s current depth, recruitment targets and any operational challenges, so we could provide the support required and accelerate preparations for the season. That report was requested on more than one occasion but was never received.
