“A meeting was subsequently scheduled involving the directors, manager, assistant manager and head of operations to review preparations for the season. Neither Jermain nor his assistant attended that meeting or that day’s training session. Throughout his tenure, Jermain had never communicated any serious concerns directly to me, so I am not going to speculate on his reasons.”



Defoe has not publicly responded to Woking’s claims.

Sports.title: Jürgen Klopp vows to change Germany but threatens to quit if family hounded by media
Sports.content:
Jürgen Klopp said he wants his team to “change a country” after being confirmed as Germany’s new head coach, but threatened to stand down if his family are hounded by the media during his time in charge.

In a forthright first press conference upon his unveiling as Julian Nagelsmann’s replacement, Klopp also suggested the role will be his final job in top-level football and expressed regret after poking fun at his predecessor while working as a television pundit during the World Cup. He is tasked with reviving Germany, who lost to Paraguay in the last 32 and have not made the last 16 since winning the tournament in 2014.

It marks a return to the dugout for Klopp two years after leaving Liverpool, where he ended a glorious nine-season tenure after explaining he felt fatigued. Since January 2025 he has worked as head of global soccer for Red Bull but a comeback to frontline action had appeared inevitable since Nagelsmann departed on 3 July.

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp was in forthright mood in his first press conference as Germany head coach. Photograph: Hannes Albert/EPA

Klopp vowed to transform a deeply fractured relationship between the national team and Germany’s public, citing his work at Liverpool as an example of the way football can galvanise a wider community.

“I want to create a situation where fans go home after the game and say: ‘Wow, that was cool,’” he said. “I want people to say: ‘Wow, it was worth putting the TV on for 90 minutes to see Germany play.’ I’ve lived and experienced how football can change a city. And I think it’s not only about cities, it’s also about the country. Ideally, football can change a country.”

The 59-year-old’s contract will run until after the 2030 World Cup. Klopp, however, warned that he would not tolerate invasive treatment from journalists and that he would be prepared to depart without compensation if he felt his family’s privacy had been violated.

“I’m taking this job even though I’ve seen how you treated Nagelsmann,” he said. “I’m taking this job even though I’ve seen how you’ve treated, in England, Thomas Tuchel. The day you don’t want me any more, I’m gone, without any severance pay. If you say tomorrow: ‘He’s shit,’ tell me to my face and I’m out. If you behave badly and don’t leave my family in peace, I’m gone, I’ll just turn away.

“Criticise me if something doesn’t work. Jürgen Klopp is not going to have any career after the national team. This is the pinnacle of my career as a coach. I will give it everything I’ve got.”

Klopp was criticised last month when, speaking with the former Germany player Thomas Müller on television during coverage of the group stage match with Curaçao, he appeared to hint Nagelsmann’s days were numbered by saying he was “still” picking the team. That was followed by a quick apology; Klopp repeated the sentiment on Friday and said the pair have yet to speak since his appointment was confirmed.

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp, in his role as Magenta TV pundit, with Kylian Mbappé after France’s World Cup quarter-final against Morocco. Photograph: Greg M Cooper/EPA

“We haven’t had any exchange,” he said, wishing Nagelsmann a happy 39th birthday for Thursday. “It was a joke. In retrospect it was one of the worst ‘funny’ remarks I have ever made. I feel awfully sorry, I’ve apologised a million times.

“It was just a rash thing to say, with no ulterior motive whatsoever, and I can only wish him the best.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Now he can go on to pastures new and I’m absolutely sure he will have many opportunities to coach a big team in future.”

Klopp promised Germany will play expansive football with wingers but admitted they must find their own way to compete with the depth of talent available elsewhere. “Success is performance relative to expectations,” he said. “When we ask in Germany: ‘Are we as good as France?’ and the answer is no, that’s not true. If we ask: ‘Do we have players like Dembélé, Mbappé, Doué and Barcola?’, no we don’t, but we can still beat them.

“We don’t want to play like Argentina, Spain, England or France. We want to do it the German way, very intense. Are we the No 1 team right now? No, we accept that. There are 11 teams ahead of us in the ranking. We can beat them, but for this to happen we need to play very good, very intense football.”

International football will demand a change of rhythm for Klopp after a lifetime spent in the domestic game. “I think contact with a team is not necessarily about working with them day in, day out,” he said. “Sometimes it will be 30 minutes or an hour and that will be on the pitch. But all of them have a mobile. I’ll talk to them, listen to them, watch games and give my feedback. That, too, is developing players and making them better.”

Klopp’s reign will begin with a ­baptism of fire in Amsterdam against the Netherlands on 24 September, one of four Nations League games in the space of 11 days. “The players have to show me, and not just say it, that playing for Germany is a super special thing,” he said.

Sports.title: ‘You need to evolve’: Enzo Maresca plots life after Pep at Manchester City
Sports.content:
Relaxed and tanned, Enzo Maresca offered a warm note with his first words to the media as the manager of Manchester City, who must somehow follow the generational Pep Guardiola. “Before we start, I would like to send a message and a big hug to Kevin Keegan’s family for this moment,” said the Italian in tribute to a football legend, following his death on Monday.

Keegan, of course, was a former City manager who had at Newcastle famously locked horns with Sir Alex Ferguson when he led Manchester United, the fierce rivals of Maresca’s new team. When the 46-year-old, sat on the dais occupied for 10 mostly glittering years by Guardiola, offered an unsolicited reference to Ferguson – and Arsène Wenger – you could see he comprehended the mammoth task before him.

How do you follow the man who claimed 20 trophies in a decade and who ranks alongside Ferguson? Well, by mentioning, and so trying to tame, the elephant in the room. “The history of the manager with many years in the same club always struggled a little bit. After Sir Alex, after Arsène,” Maresca said. “But also, it’s a challenge to try to do the right things immediately for this organisation, for the fans, for everyone.”

Speaking in front of a giant “Welcome back Enzo” billboard, a reference to his previous leading of City’s elite development squad in 2020-21 as well as his stint as Guardiola’s assistant manager in the 2022-23 treble season, Maresca would have been aware the font of goodwill will not prove deep if results go south. Certainly not from that most fickle of constituencies – fans. So Maresca cutely pointed to the patience of City’s chairman, Khaldoon al-Mubarak, and his executive. “This club has had three managers in 17 years,” he said. “This is not normal, so this is one of the things that I’m confident we can do a great job and continue to do the job that has been done in the last years. Roberto [Mancini] was here, then Manuel [Pellegrini] and then Pep – for 10 years.”

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca with Pep Guardiola at a June 2023 Manchester City training session. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

Mancini’s tenure began in December 2009, ended with his sacking in May 2013, and was angst-ridden: anathema to al-Mubarak and his chief executive, Ferran Soriano. If Mancini could be volatile, Pellegrini proved serene, and Guardiola was, simply, a genius. Al-Mubarak’s and Soriano’s experience of Maresca during his two previous seasons at City obviously convinced them that he is the full package: an accomplished football man who is of equable character.

Yet Maresca’s exit from his previous post at Chelsea on New Year’s Day ended with an apology from him, and City paying the west London club £17m in compensation. Maresca’s shutters came down for the first – and only – time when his conduct was raised. “I feel quite lucky in terms of my former clubs – Leicester, Chelsea – I think we did a great job,” he said. “In both clubs, the identity of the team was clear, the success of the team was clear, and I feel very lucky to be part of these clubs. But now we are here today. That is the most important thing, just about City. And nothing to add.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Maresca made Leicester Championship champions and the next season took Chelsea to fourth in the Premier League and a Conference League triumph before claiming the Fifa Club World Cup last summer, a 3-0 evisceration of Paris Saint-Germain in the final a calling card that may well have sealed the City job.

He talked of “titles” for the coming season. To aid this mission, Maresca has Elliot Anderson, a £116m buy from Nottingham Forest, to patrol midfield, and potentially Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, who shone for Morocco at the World Cup, to further bolster this department. He also retains an interest in Malo Gusto, one of his right-backs when at Chelsea, and if Omar Marmoush leaves, the market will be entered for a similar, pacy forward.

One player Maresca certainly does not wish to lose is the peerless Rodri, who lifted the World Cup for Spain on Sunday and received the Golden Ball, and whose control of a contest in the ever-more frantic domestic game is priceless. The 30-year-old will have surgery on a back problem on Monday. The word is it is not too serious, though he will miss out when City host Bournemouth on the opening weekend of the season. The more important date is 1 September, when the transfer window closes: will Real Madrid have made a move for a footballer who has a year left on his terms and is declining to sign the new deal offered by City?

Of more immediate concern for Maresca is flying out on Tuesday for a pre‑season tour of Asia that features matches with Inter in Hong Kong and K-League All Stars and Atlético Madrid in Seoul. For the trip Maresca will have back City’s A-listers who exited the World Cup early, including Josko Gvardiol, Mateo Kovacic and Abdukodir Khusanov.

View image in fullscreen Elliot Anderson was a key player for England at the World Cup and was Manchester City’s first signing of the summer. Photograph: Marta Lavandier/AP

“I’m working at the moment with many young players,” he said. “That is always good because they are full of energy and some of them are very good. The last group of players are going to join three or four days before the Community Shield and we will have all the squad.” After that Cardiff game with Arsenal on Sunday 16 August, the bid to successfully succeed Guardiola begins in earnest.

“You need to adapt, evolve,” Maresca added in reference to his playing style. “Set pieces, man to man – it’s a little bit the direction where football is going. We managers, it’s our duty to find solutions.” We are about to discover how good he is at this.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola backs backroom staff to help cure Liverpool’s set-piece ills
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has outlined the roles his backroom staff will play in trying to improve Liverpool’s set-piece record next season and admitted he was “very lucky” to inherit a talented coaching team at Bournemouth.

Iraola has brought several members of his Bournemouth backroom team with him to Liverpool since succeeding Arne Slot last month. Tommy Elphick, a boyhood Liverpool fan, and Shaun Cooper have joined as first-team coaches while Iraola’s long-time colleague Pablo de la Torre has arrived as assistant coach. Alejandro Rosalen has taken over as first-team goalkeeping coach after five years with Napoli.

Iraola worked alongside De la Torre in his first coaching job at AEK Larnaca, and again at Rayo Vallecano, and said having trusted confidants alongside him would be invaluable for his first season in charge at Anfield. “For me, it was important they came with me,” said Iraola, who will take charge of his first Liverpool game on Saturday in a pre-season friendly against Sunderland in Nashville. “Pablo is a physical coach but has been with me almost all the years I have been coaching. So, for me, he is much more than a physical coach really. He is an assistant and we know each other very well.

“I was very lucky with Tommy and Shaun when I arrived at Bournemouth. Because I was unlucky to have the issue with my assistant coach Iñigo Pérez [who was denied a work permit when attempting to follow Iraola from Rayo Vallecano to Bournemouth]. After, it worked out very well for him because now he is coaching Villarreal. Maybe we play him in the Champions League.

“But when I had Tommy and Shaun there, we did not feel the need to bring in another assistant. They were very prepared, they were very helpful for me in terms of understanding the English culture, the mentality of the players, what they were used to, what they like in training, even the small details that maybe in Spain are different. Also the experience Tommy has at Aston Villa, Bournemouth, Brighton, Huddersfield; they can be in a closer position to the players. They can feel more identified. I am a little bit older. Some of the players maybe didn’t know I was a player.”

One requirement for Iraola and his backroom staff will be to address Liverpool’s problems at set pieces. Only Bournemouth (26), Crystal Palace (25) and Leeds (24) conceded more set-piece goals than Liverpool’s 23 in what proved Slot’s final season as head coach, having won the title in his first. “They are very good coaches,” said Iraola. “We kind of ­understand the game similarly and they have different roles in the coaching staff, they help with set pieces also. That’s the reason I continued with them.

“Tommy does defensive set plays, Shaun does more offensive, more ­creative ones. But also we are working very well here with the set-piece analyst [Lewis Mahoney], who was very good in the second half of last season. He is already with the club, so they are working on some stuff.”

Sports.title: Dismissed solicitor is still acting for footballers in brain injury court case
Sports.content:
The solicitor dismissed by a group of over 1,000 rugby players with brain injuries who are suing the sport’s governing bodies is still leading a similar claim on behalf of dozens of former footballers.

Richard Boardman told a hearing at the Royal Courts of Justice this week of his intention to “come off the record,” with the claimants indicating that they had unanimously agreed to terminate their dealings with his firm, Rylands Garth.

Boardman’s management of the case was strongly criticised by the presiding judge, Master Jeremy Cook, who highlighted alleged “widespread non-compliance” and “misleading evidence,” with particular regard to his failure to make good on a pledge to provide the court with all of the claimants’ medical records.

Master Cook is now considering whether to strike off the case entirely, which would leave a large cohort of former union and league players including England World Cup winners Steve Thompson and Phil Vickery with nothing to show for six years of gruelling legal battles.

Despite being dismissed by the rugby players however, Boardman is still acting on behalf of a group of 23 former footballers who are suing the Football Association, English Football League and FA of Wales as a result of permanent brain injuries sustained during their careers.

The group includes the families of World Cup hero Nobby Stiles, former Newcastle manager Joe Kinnear and four former players from the Premier League era. With a far smaller number of claimants, and as a result fewer medical records, the football case is seen as more manageable for Rylands Garth.

Coincidentally, the FA changed their defence team in the case earlier this year and both parties remain in the process of exchanging documents.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The rugby claimants are in the process of appointing new solicitors, but until they have done so Boardman remains notionally in charge despite being absent from court for the last day and a half of hearings this week. The firm Leigh Day has been consulting on the case since February and is considering whether to take it on.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi let himself down – failure to call out Argentina is an insult to football
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi let himself down – failure to call out Argentina is an insult to football

Lionel Messi has come under fire for failing to condemn Argentina’s physical approach during the World Cup.

The South Americans were at the centre of various controversies during the tournament due to perceived over-physical tactics resulting in a number of tense confrontations.

5 Lionel Messi and Argentina hardly covered themselves in glory during the World Cup final Credit: AFP

5 Leandro Paredes aggressively hit out at Gavi after the final whistle Credit: Getty

Argentina have long adopted football’s dark arts in a bid to gain a psychological advantage over their opponents.

And that’s despite historically producing some of world football’s greatest-ever talents.

Lionel Scaloni’s men were far from their best at the World Cup, often relying on the Messi's wizardry to pull themselves out of the mire.

They were taken to extra time by minnows Cape Verde in the round of 32 before a miraculous late turnaround against Egypt in the last 16.

They were taken to extra time once more in an ill-tempered quarter-final with Switzerland before breaking English hearts in a frantic final ten minutes to book their spot in the final.

But it was the 1-0 defeat against Spain in the final where ten-man Argentina showed themselves in a negative light.

Enzo Fernandez was given his marching orders in the second half before teammates Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes were seen manhandling multiple Spain players after the final whistle.

Their classless antics continued into the trophy presentation where all but one Argentina player turned their backs on Spain's trophy lift.

Former Chelsea striker Tony Cascarino cast his expert eye over Argentina’s fortunes during the World Cup and expressed his disappointment at the incidents.

While Messi opted to distance himself from the on-field controversies, Cascarino believes the 39-year-old should have addressed the behaviour of his teammates in his post-World Cup Instagram post thanking fans for their support.

5 Argentina players couldn't bring themselves to watch Spain lift the trophy Credit: Getty

5 Tony Cascarino spoke of his disappointment at Messi's failure to address his side's antics

Lack of leadership

"They've got some really good players in their squad,” Cascarino said on the Sports Breakfast.

"I was a bit disappointed in Lionel Messi if I'm honest about not actually reacting to the way they played.

"Because he's been the highest [best] player I could ever think of – top notch.

"And would Johan Cruyff have accepted the Netherlands playing that way?

"No, he wouldn't have, he wouldn't have accepted it as the great player that he was, and there's other greats along the way.

"I was surprised that Lionel Messi didn't sort of say, 'Hey, look, physicality is part of our game, but we've got a lot of talent and we should have shown a bit more of that.'

5 A tearful Messi faced up the reality that he may never don the Argentina shirt again Credit: Getty

"Now I know that won them the game against England.

"But I just felt that he's been that good, is he comfortable with Argentina really playing that way?"

Messi broke down in tears after Argentina’s World Cup final defeat.

The Inter Miami star is expected to call time on his international career following 207 caps and 125 goals for La Albiceleste.

In a heartfelt post to his 515 million Instagram followers, he wrote:"The pain is immense, and it will take time for this wound to heal. But I also choose to hold on to all the good things … the matches we played, giving everything we had, will stay in our memories forever.

“With the support of an entire country, together with the hard work and effort of this group, we once again managed to be among the best teams in the world.

“Today it's difficult to fully appreciate what we achieved, but this team reached two consecutive World Cup finals. Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and every message.

“Once again, we came together as a country, united by immense pride of being Argentine. I also want to congratulate Spain on winning the championship."

Sports.title: Eddie Howe ‘doesn’t know’ if Bruno Guimaraes will stay despite ‘good conversations’ at Newcastle
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe ‘doesn’t know’ if Bruno Guimaraes will stay despite ‘good conversations’ at Newcastle

Eddie Howe has admitted his uncertainty over the future of Bruno Guimaraes at Newcastle United this summer.

talkSPORT understands the Brazilian has agreed personal terms with Arsenal ahead of a potential move.

2 Guimaraes continues to be linked with an exit to Arsenal Credit: Getty

Arsenal are also set to face no competition from rival clubs for the 28-year-old, who has two years left on his contract at St. James' Park.

Guimaraes is keen to move to the Premier League champions, who are on course to make a bid north of £70million for his signature.

An exit would come as a significant blow to Newcastle ahead of the new season.

Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali have already left for Barcelona and Tottenham Hotspur respectively.

Howe has addressed the speculation over his club captain, with he and fans being left in the dark about whether he stays or goes.

"I've spoken to Bruno before, during and after the World Cup," he said via Keith Downie after a 1-1 pre-season friendly draw with Gateshead.

"We have had some really good conversations. He's just a fantastic person.

"I don't know what’s going to happen with his future, that's for other people to speculate about. There's conversations I'm not part of."

Howe added: "I don’t think it's fair to compare (to Alexander Isak last summer). You've got to look at it in its own right.

"He's captain of our club and been an unbelievable player, through the whole time we have worked together.

2 Howe is not sure if his captain will stay at the club beyond the summer Credit: Getty

"I speak on behalf of everyone at the club, we absolutely love him and of course everyone would love him to stay.

"He's due back on the 31st (July), and there's nothing to say he won't be back."

Newcastle reinforcements

Although Guimaraes could follow Gordon and Tonali out of the exit door, Newcastle have been busy with their recruitment.

Ewen Jaouen was their first arrival in an £18m move from Reims, and then Bazoumana Toure joined from TSG Hoffenheim for £43m.

Newcastle have also brought in Sean Steur from Ajax in a deal worth around £23m.

Their latest signing was announced on Friday, with Aladji Bamba making the move from AS Monaco for £34m.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi issues stern message to Tottenham star Lucas Bergvall with talks planned
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi has scheduled talks with Lucas Bergvall but insists the door is open for any player wanting to leave Tottenham.

The Sweden international has informed Tottenham chiefs of his desire to find a new club this summer after failing to hold down a spot in the starting XI.



3 Lucas Bergvall sees his immediate future away from Tottenham Credit: Getty

Bergvall, who represented Sweden at the World Cup, has cut short his summer break to join his Spurs teammates on the club’s pre-season tour of Australia and New Zealand.

However, his future remains uncertain with five weeks remaining in the transfer window.

Speaking at his first press conference in Auckland, De Zerbi made his stance clear on players who may be plotting a future away from the club.



“Listen, I was very clear at the start of my time in Tottenham. I said 'Who doesn't want to stay in Tottenham, who is not happy, is not proud to stay here, has to leave,'” the Italian told reporters.

“I want proud players who are happy to stay here and to go on the pitch at Tottenham Stadium with a big motivation.



“If you think also in the World Cup, the motivation makes the difference. The motivation is to be happy to stay in one team.”

Planned talks

Asked specifically about Bergvall’s future, he added: “I have not spoken with Lucas yet, I will in the next days.



“We will make the best decision for the club, for Lucas, for me, for every one of us. Without problems, Lucas is a big, big talent.

“There will be a big competition to play because at the end I think we will have two players for each position.

“If he wants to stay, I will be happy. Otherwise, we have to find a new solution with Johan Lange, with Vinai (Venkatesham). It's not my business after the decision to leave (if that happens).

3 Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi told reporters he is due to have sit down talks with Bergvall in the coming days Credit: Getty



There has been plenty of Premier League interest in Bergvall this summer.

Nottingham Forest made their intentions known but saw their advances rebuffed.

Newcastle went a step further by tabling a £46million offer for the 20-year-old only to see their bid rejected.

It remains to be seen whether Bergvall will secure a move away from Tottenham before deadline day with Spurs holding out for £50m for the Swede.



De Zerbi to prioritise his attack

Elsewhere, De Zerbi revealed that focus would be switched to bolstering his attack ahead of the new season.

Spurs have been active in the transfer market with the signings of defenders Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson.

3 The Swede's hopes of pinning down a first-team spot have taken a huge blow following Spurs' summer shopping spree Credit: Getty

De Zerbi has also strengthened his midfield options after landing Sandro Tonali and Matheus Fernandes for a combined £185m.



And now the Italian has confirmed that he is on the look out for attacking reinforcements.

“The target now is to complete the attacking positions,” he said.

“We want the first target, the first level, because we have already important players.

“But I think to start a new project we need another couple of important players for sure.”

Tottenham’s two-game tour sees them take on Auckland FC at 4am on Sunday morning (UK time).



They then head to Australia to play Sydney FC on Wednesday morning at 10.45am (UK time).

Sports.title: Trevoh Chalobah in advanced talks to depart Chelsea amid £26million offer
Sports.content:
Como are in advanced talks to sign Trevoh Chalobah after making a £26million offer for the Chelsea defender, talkSPORT understands.

Chalobah has been a major target of ex-Blues star Cesc Fabregas this summer, with the Italian side now submitting a third bid for him.

4 Trevoh Chalobah has been on Chelsea's books for his entire career Credit: Getty

Move approaching?

According to talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs, Chelsea want around £30m plus £5m in add-ons for their academy graduate.

In June, Como submitted a bid worth more than £22million for Chalobah, which was knocked back.

And while their latest improved offer still falls short of this, negotiations between the two sides are now set to accelerate over the weekend.

talkSPORT previously reported that the Premier League giants were prepared to sell Chalobah, and a departure now appears more likely as they close in on the signing of Maxence Lacroix.

The Crystal Palace defender is expected to arrive at Stamford Bridge in a deal worth north of £55m.

Lacroix's arrival would push Chalobah further down the pecking order in west London, who does not appear part of new boss Xabi Alonso's plans.

The 27-year-old has two years left on a long-term contract signed in 2022, which includes an option to extend it for another 12 months.

But the Blues prepared to cash in on him now, despite being one of the club's most consistent performers in a tough 2025/26 campaign.

Chalobah made 47 appearances in all competitions, and was ultimately rewarded with a late World Cup call-up for England.

He was a late replacement for Tino Livramento after the Newcastle man suffered a calf injury, and made his tournament debut in the Three Lions' crazy 6-4 third-place play-off win over France.

4 Chalobah would work under Fabregas should he move to Como Credit: Getty

Blues reunion?

Como are looking to strengthen by pulling off the signing of Chalobah's ahead of their first-ever Champions League campaign.

Under Fabregas, the Serie A outfit secured a fourth-place league finish last term to qualify for Europe for the first time.

And should they succeed in their pursuit of Chalobah, it would see him reunited with a familiar face in Fabregas.

The pair previously shared a dressing room at Chelsea, during the Spaniard's five-year stay in west London.

A Cobham academy graduate, Chalobah has been with the Blues since the age of eight.

He signed his first professional contract in March 2018 - while Fabregas was a key player for Chelsea.

4 Chalobah could be set to depart Chelsea after making 151 appearances for the club Credit: Getty

4 The defender has spent this summer as part of England's World Cup squad, following his late call-up Credit: Getty

Chalobah was named on the bench in the 2018 FA Cup final, when Chelsea beat Manchester United 1-0 at Wembley.

Fabregas played the full 90 minutes that day, but the two never shared the pitch together at Stamford Bridge.

The Spaniard has already managed to talk one of his old teammates into joining Como, with Alvaro Morata completing a permanent move after spending last season on loan in northern Italy.

And Chalobah has certainly managed to catch Fabregas' eye in the years since his departure from Chelsea in 2019.

After a series of loans in his early career, the centre-back has gone on to establish himself in the Blues backline in more recent seasons.

Last season was his best in west London, with his 47 appearances the most he has ever made in a single campaign for the club by some distance, while he also chipped in with two goals.

Sports.title: Arsenal exploring shock deal to sign Vinicius Jr after Premier League rivals decide against move
Sports.content:
Arsenal exploring shock deal to sign Vinicius Jr after Premier League rivals decide against move

Arsenal are contemplating a move for Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior, talkSPORT understands.

The Gunners are yet to engage in club-to-club talks for the Brazilian, with the player viewed as an option rather than their number one target.

4 Vinicius Junior is on Arsenal's radar ahead of a possible summer switch Credit: Getty

The 26-year-old has also been offered to Liverpool, however the Reds have opted against pursuing the transfer.

Arsenal’s interest comes after Real Madrid tabled an offer for RB Leipzig star Yan Diomande.

The LaLiga giants saw an opening bid of £85.4million rejected by Leipzig.

However Madrid are confident of tying up a deal for the Ivory Coast international.

Gunner get ya?

Vinicius Jr and Diomande are part of the same agency meaning Diomande could be a direct replacement for the Brazilian.

It is also believed that Vinicius Jr's wages could prove to be stumbling block for the Premier League champions should they look to formalise their interest.

And there is currently no indication that Vini Jr will end up at the Emirates, despite being on Arsenal's radar.

Though they are prepared to open talks if they are given encouragement from the player.

Real Madrid are keen to not lose the forward on a free transfer with the winger tied down at the Bernabeu until 2027.

As of yet, there has been no breakthrough in terms of Vini Jr extending his stay.

4 The winger showed he has lost none of his shine in the World Cup Credit: Getty

4 Could the player end up at the Emirates this window?

Should Real fail to make progress on a deal then a move away form the club cannot be ruled out, according to sources at the Spanish club.

Renewal talks have taken place for over a year with an agreement having come close.

Vinicius Jr previously halted negotiations after falling out with former boss Xabi Alonso.

He has been linked with a money-spinning move to Saudi Arabia with Al Ahli with a €1bn five-year contract offered to him last year.

Brazil's talisman

The winger was arguably Brazil's standout player during the World Cup.

He featured in each of his country's five matches at the tournament, scoring four goals before their eventual round-of-16 defeat to Norway.

4 Vini Jr endured a frustrating season for Madrid but still posted 22 goals Credit: Getty

Last season, he netted 22 times in an underwhelming campaign for Real Madrid.

Los Blancos ended the season without silverware having finished runners-up to rivals Barcelona in La Liga.

But he has been embroiled in high-profile controversies during the course of the season including a racism storm in the Champions League clash against Benfica in February.

Sports.title: Jermain Defoe’s Woking exit explained as club issue bizarre statement
Sports.content:
Jermain Defoe failed to turn up for training prior to his departure as Woking boss, the club’s director of football has revealed.

The 43-year-old’s contract was mutually terminated on Thursday despite only having taken the role in March.

4 Jermain Defoe spent just six matches in charge of National League side Woking Credit: Getty

The former Premier League striker claimed this week that it was ‘impossible for me to continue’ as Woking boss.

Defoe took charge of just six matches, winning two and losing once.

However, a bizarre statement from the club’s director of football Jody Brown appeared to hit back at the former Tottenham and West Ham man.

Brown claimed that Defoe missed both training and a pre-arranged meeting this week amid ‘growing concerns’ within the club during pre-season.

Woking statement

A statement posted on the club’s website read: “Jermain Defoe was an outstanding player, scored a vast number of goals, and is a very likeable guy.

“The feeling I get from within the football industry and its global support is not one of great surprise, but of course our own fanbase want and deserve some kind of clarity.

“The recommendation to appoint Jermain as manager was mine, and I take full responsibility for it. After meeting with him on several occasions, I believed he was the right person to lead the club into an exciting new era.

“As we have seen many times before, success as a player does not always translate into management and leadership. I sincerely hope to see him succeed in whichever direction he follows.

“I do not intend to discuss internal matters more than necessary or attribute blame. I’ve seen the speculation. Instead, I want to make clear that the club was fully committed to supporting Jermain in every sense throughout his time in the role.

“All player recruitment, staffing decisions and football matters were heavily influenced by Jermain, and he was given the necessary operational and board support. In any organisation there are processes to follow.

4 Defoe spent nearly four months in the Woking dugout Credit: Getty

“Just days before his departure, the club were delighted to finalise the signing of an excellent player identified by Jermain, again illustrating the support the club had given right up until his final day.”

Unease within the club

Brown then provided details of the concerns that had been raised within the club regarding Defoe’s output.

“Jermain’s feedback was always positive, and he regularly expressed his enthusiasm and excitement for the season, both publicly and privately. I can therefore appreciate the surprise and subsequent speculation surrounding his sudden departure.

“However, in recent weeks there had been feedback from across the club, including players, staff and other departments, regarding growing concerns.

“To better understand the situation, I asked Jermain and Paul for a brief report outlining the squad’s current depth, recruitment targets and any operational challenges, so we could provide the support required and accelerate preparations for the season.

“That report was requested on more than one occasion but was never received.

4 The former Premier League striker shared his wealth of experience with the non-league club Credit: Getty

“A meeting was subsequently scheduled involving the directors, manager, assistant manager and Head of Operations to review preparations for the season.

“Neither Jermain nor his assistant attended that meeting or that day’s training session. Throughout his tenure, Jermain had never communicated any serious concerns directly to me, so I am not going to speculate on his reasons.

“Every football club faces challenges. Players want more game time, improved contracts or transfers. The media team might want better equipment, the medical department more interns, the strength and conditioning staff larger gym space. and the car park attendants may want more coffee. But people do not just fail to turn up.

“The experience has highlighted lessons for both myself and the club, particularly around communication with Jermain and his representatives throughout the four months and six matches he was with us.

"Throughout that period, the club’s objective remained the same: to support the players and staff and give the project every opportunity to succeed.

“I wish Jermain every success in the future and thank him and his staff for their efforts.

“Our focus is now firmly on Woking Football Club and everyone who cares about it, while maintaining the standards, culture and preparations required ahead of the new season.”

4 Defoe thanked Woking for his first opportunity in management Credit: Getty

Defoe's confirmation

Defoe had previously spoken out on his exit - claiming the experience would help him in the next stage of his managerial career.

He wrote on Instagram: "Following recent discussions, I can confirm that I have mutually agreed to leave my position as manager of Woking FC.

"Unfortunately, circumstances have ultimately made it impossible for me to continue in the position.

"I am extremely proud of the work undertaken during my time at the club and genuinely felt that we were building something special.

"I would like to thank Todd Johnson for giving me the opportunity to manage the club.

"I am incredibly grateful to the supporters and, most importantly, the players, who I am genuinely gutted for. The group is a fantastic one, and I wish the squad every success for the season ahead.

"I'm really disappointed the journey has ended so soon, but I leave with great pride in what Paul Bracewell, Karl Halabi and I were building at the club.

"My time at Woking FC has been an eye-opening managerial experience and one that will undoubtedly make me stronger for the next challenge in my career."

Sports.title: West Ham reject bid for El Hadji Malick Diouf from Premier League side
Sports.content:
West Ham have rejected an offer from Brentford for El Hadji Malick Diouf and insist he is not for sale, talkSPORT understands.

The 21-year-old was one of the Hammers' standout performers last season, as they were ultimately relegated to the Championship.



5 El Hadji Malick Diouf looks set for Championship football in the upcoming season Credit: Getty

Diouf impressed at left-back in his debut campaign in the Premier League after joining in a £22million deal plus add-ons from Slavia Prague, with his performances seeing him linked with a move away from the London Stadium.

talkSPORT previously reported that Manchester United were interested in signing the Senegal international back in April.

A deal ultimately did not materialise, and it now appears any possibility of a move is off the table.



Hammer blow

With Brentford now having a bid for Diouf waived away, it understood that West Ham have no plans on selling him.

The Irons had been in need of player sales following their relegation, but they have since recouped £153million in departures.



Mateus Fernandes joined rivals Tottenham in a £85m deal, before Crysencio Summerville signed for Saudi outfit Al Hilal for £68m.

This leaves the Hammers' finances in a healthy position, and are now no longer under any obligation to offload players.



It is also understood that Brentford's bid for Diouf, which is unknown, fell short of what the east London side would be tempted by.

Had the offer been accepted, the defender would have become the second player to head to the Bees after leaving West Ham.

Callum Wilson recently moved to west London on a one-year contract following the expiry of his contract at the London Stadium.

5 Keith Andrews is looking to strengthen in the left-back area for Brentford Credit: Getty



5 Nuno Espirito Santo will be reluctant to let key man Diouf go Credit: AFP

It is currently unclear whether Brentford will make another offer for Diouf, who would likely have to come up with a seriously improved bid.

Keith Andrews has several left-back options available at Brentford, with Rico Henry and Aaron Hickey both specialists in the position.

But the pair have both struggled with injuries in recent years, as Hickey spent almost two years out with a hamstring problem before returning last October.



Meanwhile Henry is currently out with a hamstring issue, after making 25 Premier League appearances last term following his return from an ACL injury.

In their place, winger Keane Lewis-Potter has deputised well, but the Bees would no doubt be eager to bring in a designated left-back.

Big guns staying?

As for West Ham, holding onto Diouf would represent another major boost as they head into their first Championship season since 2011.

5 Diouf has been capped 23 times by Senegal, three of which came at the 2026 World Cup Credit: Getty



5 West Ham have kept hold of their talismanic captain Jarrod Bowen ahead of their upcoming Championship season Credit: Getty

Nuno Espirito Santo's side are bidding to seal an immediate return to the top-flight by winning promotion, and they will have captain Jarrod Bowen there to spearhead the charge.

Despite being tipped to leave the club, with Liverpool and Aston Villa touted as suitors, Bowen instead signed a revised contract until 2030.

And the Hammers could also now have Diouf on hand in their promotion push, who proved himself a key asset last term.



The Senegalese enjoyed an encouraging debut season at West Ham, providing five assists in 32 Premier League appearances last term.

Diouf also featured for Senegal at this summer's World Cup, playing in three of their four games as they were ultimately knocked out in the round of 32 by Belgium.

Sports.title: Frustrated Lewis Hamilton is handed a three-place grid penalty in another blow to Ferrari star after he had pole position snatched away by British rival Lando Norris
Sports.content:
A big cheer and then Lewis Hamilton was left shaking his head. From a likely pole one moment to demotion down the grid a couple of hours later, his world championship hopes rocked in Hungary.

The first jab was Lando Norris snatching the front spot with a late and skilled ambush. The second punch was administered in the stewards’ room, where Hamilton was inevitably penalised for inadvertently impeding McLaren’s Oscar Piastri.

Hamilton was relegated from second on the grid to fifth. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who qualified fourth, was elevated to third. That is how cruelly the pendulum swung against Hamilton, who is 45 points off the Italian after 10 rounds.

Poor Lewis, he was let down by his Ferrari team not warning him that Piastri was coming up fast behind him, and now he has it all to do having looked to be favourite for victory, conceivably even from second on the grid.

Before his setbacks, Hamilton seemed to think he had qualified first, judging by how he pulled into parc ferme next to the marker with No 1 on it.

Norris was still out on track and piecing together his smooth assault on the top, a chance he was gifted by Hamilton being unable to improve on his first run that had temporarily put him in command.

Lewis Hamilton was left frustrated after having pole position snatched away at the 11th hour - and then he was bunged down to fifth with a grid penalty

Reigning champion Lando Norris roared through to claim his first pole of the year by 0.012s

Barely any driver was conjuring extra speed in the final stages, bar Norris, who pipped Hamilton by 0.012sec to secure the first pole of his title defence. The No 1 marker was moved by officialdom in front of the world champion’s McLaren. No 2 was placed by the red car.

Then, Hamilton’ summons to the stewards at 6pm local time, an appointment all the more galling because his car is fastest, a point he believes he could have underlined today in normal circumstances.

‘We have been doing a great job all weekend,’ he said, slow to raise much cheer in the immediate aftermath, distracted by the prospect of his incoming penalty. ‘I felt solid throughout qualifying and, for some reason, we went out first, which I don’t think was the right call.

‘And for some reason the grip wasn’t there then.

‘We’re obviously competitive but I think tomorrow is going to be a hard day. We’ll fine-tune things tonight to give ourselves the best chance.’

One positive to hang on to is that the Silver Arrows looked a shadow of their formerly dominant selves.

Indeed, this was the first time this campaign that neither of their cars set the qualifying pace. Instead, Hamilton’s team-mate Charles Leclerc was third fastest, later promoted to second.

George Russell, in the second Mercedes, was only seventh quickest, his championship dream increasingly bleak. Fifty points off the summit, he had to abandon his car on his way into the pits, a water leak having sprung his latest dose of bad luck. He will be fitted with a new engine for the race, saying good riddance to his last one.

Sports.title: Arsenal explore ambitious move for Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Junior
Sports.content:
Arsenal have made initial enquiries over the availability of Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior.

With Jose Mourinho's side exploring the purchase of Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig, the Premier League champions have checked on the Brazilian's status as speculation grows over where his future lies.

The 26-year-old has the same representatives as Diomande, who was also on Arsenal's radar, and there has been interest from Saudi Arabi over the past 12 months.

Vinicius Jnr is one of a number of forward targets Arsenal are exploring, with Julian Alvarez, Yan Diomande and Bradley Barcola also of interest.

Liverpool are considered favourites for Barcola but his situation could change if PSG fail to land Diomande with Madrid leading that charge and trying to close the deal quickly.

Arsenal are keen to sign a left winger this summer - and Vinicius Junior would represent a major coup for the Premier League champions

Vinicius Jnr is in the final year of his contract and if an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Madrid could be open to selling, rather than lose him for free next summer.

The deal would represent a sensational coup for Arsenal if they were successful but the clubs are still to open official talks.

Last year Al Ahli were willing to offer a €1bn five-year contract offer.

Liverpool were also credited with interest earlier this window but are not in the mix for a player who earns around £520,000 a week.

Vinicius Jnr has scored 128 goals across eight seasons in Madrid, and narrowly missed out on the Ballon d'Or to Rodri in 2024.

Daily Mail Sport has reported that Gabriel Martinelli is up for sale as Mikel Arteta looks to add more firepower to his forward line.

Leandro Trossard has already been sold to Besiktas, while Arsenal confirmed the signing of Greek winger Christos Tzolis for £34million from Club Bruges on Thursday.

Sports.title: Why Arsenal paid £34m for Norwich flop Christos Tzolis: The problem insiders insist Greece star will solve, similarities with Leandro Trossard and what it means for Gunners' forward hunt
Sports.content:
Rewind to September 2021. Norwich City’s record signing Christos Tzolis arrived at the Emirates to face an Arsenal team bottom of the Premier League table on zero points.

Five years later, after an ill-fated spell at the Canaries and a fast rise in the Belgian Pro League, Greek winger Tzolis now finds himself signing for the Premier League champions in a £34million deal from Club Bruges. It’s a remarkable turnaround for both parties.

The 24-year-old recorded an extraordinary 40 goal contributions (17 goals, 23 assists) in 36 league appearances last season, which landed him on Mikel Arteta’s radar.

It wasn’t an anomaly for Tzolis, either, having arrived in Belgium fresh off a loan spell with Bundesliga 2 side Fortuna Dusseldorf. There he mustered 34 goal contributions in 37 games. His performance in Greece’s 2-1 Nations League victory over England at Wembley in October 2024 also caught the eye.

With Leandro Trossard having joined Besiktas, Tzolis is the like-for-like replacement. The comparisons between the pair are interesting. They both played in the Belgian Pro League, are proficient in front of goal and are pacy, adaptable attackers.

The Greek forward is predominantly a winger like Trossard, but can also play as a No 10. Last summer, for example, Crystal Palace strongly considered Tzolis as a replacement for Eberechi Eze.

Christos Tzolis recorded an extraordinary 40 goal contributions (17 goals, 23 assists) in 36 league appearances last season for Club Bruges

The 24-year-old is predominantly a winger but can also play as a No 10

Hayk Milkon, Club Bruges' assistant manager until February, previously said: ‘He's able to fulfil different roles. Coming from the left side — giving him this space to start wide and then find the moments to get more inside — that's where he's at his strongest.

‘If he's assigned to play really wide to get these one-on-ones, he's able to do it. But he's always strongest the closer he is to the goal. Whenever he's more central, you can expect him at any moment to attack the space.’

Another similarity between Tzolis and Trossard is their availability. Trossard was only injured for four matches in three-and-a-half-years at Arsenal, those games coming in his final season in north London. Tzolis has a similar record at Club Bruges, missing just two matches due to injury across two seasons.

The new arrival is two-footed but likes to cut in from the left on to his right foot where he can provide fizzing passes or make inroads to goal. His shooting efficiency, paired with an unpredictability of whether he hugs the touchline or cuts in, can cause havoc.

Goals from their wingers is an area in which the Gunners are aiming to improve. Last season, among Arsenal’s wide attackers, none reached double figures in the Premier League. One man who will be looking over his shoulder is Gabriel Martinelli. The Brazilian scored just one league goal last term. Arsenal’s left-wing spot is up for grabs.

Tzolis will need time to adapt to a new league, though, and therein lies comparisons to another Arsenal forward: Viktor Gyokeres. The Swede started slowly before getting going in the second half of last season to round off the campaign with 21 goals across all competitions. Gyokeres had a failed spell in England with Brighton before moves to Coventry and Sporting Lisbon kickstarted his career.

There is some caution to be had around Tzolis’ output, of course. The Belgium Pro League is the eighth strongest league in the world, according to Opta's Power Rankings — one place below the Championship.

And what is also clear is that Tzolis has very big boots to fill. Affectionately dubbed ‘Mr Clutch’ by supporters for his habit of striking in crucial moments, Trossard leaves Arsenal as a cult hero who proved great value for his £27m move from Brighton in January 2023.

Tzolis has managed nine goals for Greece across his 34 appearances

He will be charged with filling the void left by Arsenal cult hero Leandro Trossard, who has joined Besiktas in Turkey

Across the 2025 calendar year, Trossard registered more goal contributions than any Arsenal player, with 13 goals and 12 assists. Mikel Merino followed with 13 goals and eight assists, while Declan Rice managed nine goals and 11 assists.

Trossard's late winner against West Ham in May, a pivotal moment in Arsenal becoming champions, underlines why he became such a trusted figure under Arteta. Such an impact will be hard to replicate at Premier League level for Tzolis.

The impending arrival of the Greek international, who has nine goals in 34 appearances for his country, doesn’t halt Arsenal’s plan to bring in more attacking reinforcements this summer. They retain an interest in Atletico Madrid’s Julian Alvarez and Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola.

The challenge for Tzolis is proving his remarkable numbers in Belgium can translate to England. If he can do that, Arsenal may have found the long-term successor to one of Arteta’s most trusted attackers.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland leads party-goers in Norway's iconic rowing celebration as he joins Man City stars at team-mate's glamorous Italian wedding
Sports.content:
Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma married his childhood sweetheart yesterday — with a host of his City team-mates in attendance at the lavish reception.

Erling Haaland was among the guests in Fasano, southern Italy, joined by his partner, Isabel Haugseng Johansen.

The Norway star, fresh from accumulating an army of new fans at the World Cup, opted for a black suit, bow-tie and sunglasses as he happily walked hand-in-hand with Johansen.

He was later filmed leading a group of guests in recreating Norway's iconic 'rowing' celebration from the tournament in North America.

City midfielder Mateo Kovacic was also pictured at the wedding. Italian football legend Paolo Maldini, former City boss Pep Guardiola and new Tottenham signing Sandro Tonali were also said to be among the attendees.

Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma married his childhood sweetheart Alessia Elefante in Italy yesterday

City stars Erling Haaland and Mateo Kovacic, joined by their partners Isabel and Izabel, and were among the guests. Haaland later led party-goers in Norway's iconic 'rowing' celebration

Donnarumma and Elefante, an interior designer, have been together for 10 years

Donnarumma, 27, tied the knot with his long-time partner Alessia Elefante, a 28-year-old interior designer.

The pair have been dating for 10 years, having met in their hometown of Castellammare di Stabia, near Naples.

They also have a son together — Leo, born in 2024. The couple announced their engagement in May with an Instagram post that read: 'Long-term contract signed.'

They wed in the Church of Saint George Martyr in the hilltop town of Locorotondo before joining the revellers in Fasano.

Haaland certainly enjoyed the night, excitedly banging a drum as chanting party-goers sat on the floor rowing — copying the post-match celebration that Haaland and his team-mates made famous in their impressive World Cup campaign.

The 26-year-old has been making the most of his break after the tournament, having holidayed in Italy with Johansen this week.

Sports.title: Alan Shearer's daughter Hollie is married! Singer, 31, ties the knot with England rugby star Joe Marchant in a legal ceremony
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer's daughter Hollie is married!

Sports.title: Bahrain Grand Prix to be hosted in Malaysia in bizarre change to F1 calendar after Middle East chaos - with another extra race lined up
Sports.content:
Formula One will stage the ‘Bahrain’ Grand Prix in Malaysia in a strange twist to the war-interrupted world championship calendar.

Daily Mail Sport understands the replacement venue will be confirmed on Sunday and be held on October 4 between the Azerbaijan and Singapore rounds.

The race will carry the name of the Gulf kingdom, which was due to host its event in April before America and Israel attacked Iran, in an agreement brokered between Crown Prince Salman of Bahrain and the King of Malaysia.

Retaliatory strikes on American military bases in the Middle East have made it impossible to restage the fixture in the region and the enterprising plan to switch it to Sepang International Circuit – an eight-hour flight from Bahrain – was met with Formula One’s full support.

The Bahrain-bankrolled event will extend the season to 23 races, though that number would be trimmed if the concluding two rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi on November 29 and December 6 also fall victim to hostilities.

The 'Bahrain' Grand Prix will in fact be held at Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit (pictured) this year

The arrangement was brokered by Crown Prince Salman of Bahrain (left) and the King of Malaysia, in light of the chaos in the Middle East following Donald Trump's attack on Iran

In that case a single extra race would be added in Imola, mostly likely on the earlier of the two vacated dates, restoring the world championship to 22 rounds.

Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari would be an ideal venue if either of the two leading championship contenders, Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari, or Italian Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes, were to claim the title there. As long as the weather holds.

Sports.title: How £75m Bruno Guimaraes can take Arsenal to next level: Better numbers than Declan Rice, leading Mikel Arteta's press and how his deep passes unlock low blocks
Sports.content:
Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Arsenal have been here before with Bruno Guimaraes. The Gunners wanted him four years ago when he was still at Lyon but, in the end, the Brazilian chose Tyneside.

If that were not bad enough, the announcement video he posted on his social media, captioned ‘a beautiful chapter is coming’ began with clippings of news headlines of Arsenal’s interest.

More than four years later and Arsenal are back again. This time, Guimaraes wants them too. He has told Newcastle he wants to join Arsenal and now it’s down to the clubs to thrash it out. A fee of around £75million should do it.

That’s a fair whack for a player about to turn 29, much older than the usual profile of Arsenal signings under Arteta, but in Guimaraes they would have a ready-made addition to take them to the next level, as they bid to retain their first Premier League title in 22 years and expunge the pain of the Champions League final defeat by Paris Saint-Germain.

As owner Josh Kroenke said at the end of the season: ’It is about trying to stay at the top knowing everyone is trying to climb the mountain after you.’

Guimaraes would help them do that. There’s good reason why Arteta wants him. He’s physical. He’s versatile. He can play box-to-box, deep-lying playmaker or destructor. Or, as we’ll come to see, all of them, all at once.

Arsenal are pushing hard to sign Bruno Guimaraes (left) from Newcastle to bolster their midfield as they bid to retain their Premier League title

Arsenal tried to sign Guimaraes from Lyon in 2022, but were beaten to the signing by Newcastle

The 28-year-old Brazilian has 48 caps for his country, representing them at the last two World Cups

BRUNO'S BRAWNS PL midfielders since Jan 2022 Tackles Joao Palhinha (Fulham/Spurs) 410 Moises Caicedo (Brighton/Chelsea) 408 Joao Gomes (Wolves) 380 Bruno Guimaraes (Newcastle) 356 Alexis Mac Allister (Brighton/Liverpool) 353

BRUNO'S BRAINS PL midfielders since Jan 2022 Open play chances created Bruno Fernandes (Man Utd) 359 Martin Odegaard (Arsenal) 276 Bruno Guimaraes (Newcastle) 197 Morgan Gibbs-White (Wolves/Nottm Forest) 197 Bernardo Silva (Man City) 197

Declan Rice needs a rest. The Arsenal and England midfielder played 69 matches for club and country last season. Arteta ran him into the ground – he has previous for this, just ask Bukayo Saka – and, by the end, you could tell.

He played through a hamstring injury from Christmas onwards and was substituted early in England’s victory over Croatia with ‘neural pain’ in his back.

'The body's been through a lot this season,’ he said after England’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina. 'I think you can see I'm mentally done, physically done. I need a break now.’

Only, Arsenal’s title defence starts in less than a month. Having Guimaraes will allow Arteta to rest his linchpin.

But that’s only one reason. He’s Rice, and he’s more. In many ways, he’s the complete central player. Over his four and a half years at Newcastle, he ranked in the top five midfielders for both tackles and chances created from open play. Only Rice and Bruno Fernandes have run more miles since Guimaraes joined the Premier League.

His tenacity out of possession will be ideal for Arteta’s intense press. He wins the ball back but then he does something with it.

What has been clear in recent seasons is how over-reliant Arsenal are down the right and, conversely, how under-served they have been at playing through the middle. Saka is the main source of attacking threat while creator-in-chief Martin Odegaard also likes to drift that side.

Guimaraes is the ideal player to fix that. Nine goals for Newcastle last season was as many as Rice and Zubimendi combined, while his five assists match Rice’s figure.

Declan Rice has admitted he is suffering from neural damage in his lower back and hamstring - and did not appear to be at full fitness during the World Cup

Guimaraes' nine goals for Newcastle last season was as many as Rice and Zubimendi combined, while his five assists matches Rice’s figure

So much of his creativity for Newcastle comes through the middle. As you can see from the chances created maps below, many of Rice's come tucked into the left channel and frequently not until he gets into the final third.

Guimaraes is more focused in central areas and, quite frequently, from deep.

That could be crucial for Arteta. His ability on the ball from deeper areas will allow Arsenal to be quicker and more direct when they have possession, an aspect of their play Arteta is keen to improve if they are to push on once more.

Where Rice creates his chances from, focused largely on the left 'half-space' just outside the box

Guimaraes' map is far more varied, and he is able to create chances from deeper - which will help Arsenal against low blocks

For too long, they have struggled to break down defences with cutting passes and instead turned back to set-pieces or Saka.

Towards the back end of last season, we saw Arsenal try to implement this more, especially in their Champions League semi-final victory over Atletico Madrid where they used the pace of Viktor Gyokeres to exploit space in behind the defence.

William Saliba’s ball (below) led to the move that set up Saka’s winning goal. In the same game, however, the Arsenal crowd got on Rice’s back when he had the chance to do the same but turned it down and passed it sideways.

Guimaraes loves a pass from deep to set his team-mates away. Arsenal know that only too well, Guimaraes having sent a defence-splitting ball through to Jacob Murphy to run clear in their clash early in the season.

He attempted more through balls and line-breaking passes per game than either of them too.

William Saliba chips in behind the PSG defence to find Viktor Gyokeres

But Rice was unable to do the same, and instead passed back inside to Martin Odegaard

Guimaraes showed against Arsenal last season that he is eager to get attacks started rather than build up slowly and allow the defence time to settle

Not only that, though, he can dribble the ball with purpose himself too. Guimaraes created 13 chances for his Newcastle team-mates following ball carries last term, more than both Rice (eight) and Zubimendi (three) combined.

His delivery from set plays, the cornerstone of Arsenal’s attack, is also superb with a couple of assists coming from corners last term.

All of that shows why Arteta wants him, and why he’s so keen to splash the cash on a player that’s not far off 30. Because he can play the Rice role or he can play the Zubimendi (or Myles Lewis-Skelly) one. Rice can sit in, Guimaraes can push on. Or the other way around. He can split defences, he can run at them.

What better way to push on again than by signing a player who can do it all.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua fight LIVE RESULTS from Tyson Fury warm-up bout
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua ready to defy Tyson Fury in build-up to mega-fight

Anthony Joshua has vowed to haunt Tyson Fury long after they belatedly settle their bitter rivalry.

The two British heavyweights each ruled the world in their prime without ever crossing paths in the ring. But providing Joshua, 36, swats aside Kristian Prenga tonight, he and Fury, 37, will finally collide later this year. Their long-awaited showdown will be a clash of personalities as much as a contrast of fighting styles.

Joshua has held his tongue for a decade in the face of a tirade of abuse from his fellow countryman. The Olympic champion has been a poster boy for his bluechip sponsors while Fury thinks nothing of crossing the line between class and crass. The Gypsy King believes he can shatter his rival's corporate veneer and expose his raw working-class roots. But Joshua is confident he won't let his mask slip.

"Tyson Fury won't get under my skin," he said. "It's about boxing and it's about skill; I'm not trying to win a press conference, I'm not trying to win a weigh-in. I'm trying to win a fight. I don't think the Anthony Joshua from Watford needs to come out in that aspect, it needs to come out in the ring. I will let him talk and let him have his fun.

"I've seen Fury's community, and they're unbelievable talkers; that's the culture they're from. They have no problem calling each other out and saying, 'I'll drive 60 miles next week and meet you down there'. I can't go up against someone who has been doing it since he was 10 years old and think I'm going to win.

"I've got to let him do what he's good at, and my job is to beat him in the ring. There will be nothing better than getting my hand raised."
