World.title: Costa Rica Flooding Closes 267 Schools as Sarapiquí Evacuations Climb
World.content:
If you live in Sarapiquí, Guápiles, Siquirres or the South Caribbean, today is not going to be a normal Friday. Schools are closed. Route 4 was cut through Sarapiquí. Hundreds of your neighbors slept in shelters. And the ground under all of it is holding about as much water as it can hold.

The Comisión Nacional de Emergencias (CNE) counted 800 people evacuated into nine shelters by late yesterday afternoon, according to CNE president Alejandro Picado. That figure is a running total of everyone pulled out of harm’s way, not a snapshot of who was still sheltered by nightfall.

Counts released earlier in the day ran lower and measured something different — more than 500 people in shelters at one point Thursday, and 348 people across six shelters in another CNE tally. The numbers move by the hour as families go home and new evacuations begin, so treat any single figure as a photograph rather than a measurement.

Picado named Sarapiquí as the hardest-hit canton. The communities sending the most people out are Naranjal 1, Naranjal 2, Carretones, Mortero, La Chave, El Palmar, Cureña and Cureñita. Firefighters and Red Cross crews used rafts and small boats to reach houses in El Tigre, Naranjales and El Nogal, where water covered the streets. The CNE delivered 1,250 food parcels and was arranging another 1,000, along with drinking water for households cut off from safe supply.

Your children are probably not in class today and depending on where you live that may have changed after you went to bed. The Ministerio de Educación Pública first suspended lessons Thursday and Friday at 157 schools — 138 in the Sarapiquí regional directorate, 14 in Guápiles and five in Siquirres, under the Limón directorate.

Late last night the ministry extended the suspension to all 110 schools in the Sulá regional directorate, which covers the South Caribbean. That brings the national total to 267 campuses closed. If your kids attend school anywhere between Bribri, Cahuita and Puerto Viejo de Talamanca, check the ministry’s official channels this morning rather than assuming yesterday’s list still applies.

The thing worth understanding today is why ordinary rain is now doing extraordinary damage. The Instituto Meteorológico Nacional reported Thursday that river basins across the Caribbean, the Northern Zone and the South Pacific are sitting near 95 percent saturation. Soil that full behaves like a paved parking lot.

Rain that would normally soak in instead runs straight off the hillside and into the nearest quebrada, which is why a moderate afternoon downpour can now push a river over its banks in under an hour. The IMN measured 20 to 50 millimeters (0.8 to 2 inches) of rain Thursday morning alone, with peaks of 60 to 85 millimeters (2.4 to 3.3 inches) around Horquetas, Sarapiquí, Montaña Sagrada, Pococí and Cariari. Overnight Wednesday into Thursday, Canta Gallo de Limón took 81.8 millimeters (3.2 inches) and Sarapiquí 44.2 millimeters (1.7 inches).

There is a second, less obvious risk on the Río Sarapiquí. Emergency crews spent yesterday verifying whether a landslide has formed a plug in the river channel. A plug like that acts as an accidental dam. It holds water back, the level builds behind it, and then it fails all at once — sending a surge downstream with almost no warning to anyone below it. That is the specific scenario the CNE is watching, and it is the reason to take an evacuation instruction seriously even if the river in front of your house looks calm at the moment you receive it.

Roads are the other daily problem. Route 4 was blocked in Sarapiquí on Thursday, and Route 32 over the Zurquí has closed repeatedly this month when material comes down on the carriageway. Confirm the status with the MOPT before you commit to a drive, because the alternates are slower than they look on a map: Vara Blanca handles light vehicles only, and Bajos de Chilamate–Vuelta Kooper takes any vehicle but adds real time. If you reach standing water on a road, turn around. You cannot see whether the roadbed underneath has washed out, and moving water pushes a vehicle sideways long before the water reaches the door.

Travelers should build slack into today. The overland route to Tortuguero runs Guápiles to Cariari to the La Pavona dock, straight through the affected corridor, and the same weather that closed schools can close a boat schedule. Lodges in Sarapiquí, La Selva and the Puerto Viejo de Sarapiquí area are inside the flood footprint. Call ahead rather than driving out and finding out. In Talamanca, rising rivers damaged dikes, roads and homes, and the CNE delivered aid to 50 fishing families in Puerto Viejo, Punta Uva and Manzanillo who could not get out on the water.

The forecast offers a partial break and then takes it back. The IMN expects a warmer, brighter morning as cloud cover thins, but an active Intertropical Convergence Zone and a hit of humidity moving in off the Caribbean should rebuild rain through the afternoon and into the night.

The North Caribbean starts cloudy with drizzle and intermittent rain and keeps a chance of showers all day, with Guápiles between 22.4 and 28 degrees Celsius (72 to 82 Fahrenheit). The South Caribbean follows the same pattern. Do not read a dry morning as the end of this. The IMN expects tropical wave No. 25 to reach the country on Sunday, landing on ground that will have had no time to drain.

The yellow alert stands for the Northern Zone, the north and south Caribbean, and the canton of Turrialba. If you are in those areas, keep your phone charged, keep documents and medication somewhere you can grab in one motion, and go when the municipal emergency committee tells you to go. Emergencies go to 9-1-1.

World.title: International News:Argentina President condemns World Cup critics over treatment of Messi and team
World.content:
International News:Argentina President condemns World Cup critics over treatment of Messi and team

By Zoila Palma: Argentina President Javier Milei has defended the country’s national football team and Lionel Messi following widespread criticism of their controversial 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign.

Argentina reached the final but lost 1-0 to Spain in extra time, missing the opportunity to become only the third nation to win consecutive World Cup titles.

The team’s run drew criticism from rival fans over its narrow victories, aggressive style of play and a post-match altercation following Spain’s extra-time win in the final.

Some also accused FIFA and match officials of favoring Argentina, while Egypt reportedly filed a complaint seeking an investigation into refereeing decisions during its controversial 3-2 Round of 16 defeat to the South American side.

Milei responded to the criticism through a series of posts on Instagram, sharing one message that read: “Do you have enemies? It means you once defended something. We defend Argentina.”

He also posted: “The problem with Argentina is that we are conspicuous, we don’t go unnoticed, people are jealous of us, and we are good at almost everything.”

Milei later shared an AI-generated image of himself ripping open his suit to reveal an Argentina jersey, captioned: “Long live Argentina, damn it!”

His comments came after Messi’s wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, also defended Argentina in a social media post criticizing the team’s detractors.

“Proud to be Argentine. Argentina is exactly like a family; we may disagree and quarrel amongst ourselves, but if someone from outside comes and insults us, we will tear out their liver,” her Instagram story read.

World.title: “Tek Time fi Read” Book Festival to distribute more than 10,000 free books
World.content:
“Tek Time fi Read” Book Festival to distribute more than 10,000 free books

By Zoila Palma: Belmopan youth are preparing to distribute more than 10,000 free books to children and teenagers during the fifth annual “Tek Time fi Read” Book Festival, scheduled for Saturday, August 8, at the Belmopan Civic Center.

The literacy celebration, organized by the youth-led Tek Time fi Read Project, will run from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. and aims to encourage a lifelong love of reading among Belizean children.

Children and teens ages 0 to 18 will participate in interactive, reading-focused games to earn points that can be exchanged for new and gently used books.

Children who attend dressed as their favorite book characters will also have an opportunity to receive bonus book prizes, while teachers can select up to 25 free books for their classrooms.

The festival will also feature a book exchange and sale, a local author table, a food court and other activities for families.

The initiative, established in 2018 by participants in the Belmopan Youth Spiritual Empowerment Program, has since brought more than 57,000 books into Belize, installed public Book Boxes, renovated libraries and conducted literacy outreach across the country.

More than 50 Belmopan youth volunteers between the ages of 11 and 30 are involved in organizing the event.

Admission to the festival is free, with children, parents and educators encouraged to attend.

Ian Anderson’s Caves Branch Jungle Lodge is returning as the event’s main financial sponsor, while Books for Development and community donors are providing major book contributions.

World.title: Belize represented at the 12th Commonwealth Sports Ministers meeting in Glasgow, Scotland
World.content:
Belize represented at the 12th Commonwealth Sports Ministers meeting in Glasgow, Scotland

By Zoila Palma: Anthony Mahler, Minister of Tourism, Youth, Sports and Diaspora Relations, and Devin Daly, Minister of State for Youth and Sports are representing Belize in the 12th Commonwealth Sports Ministers Meeting in Glasgow, Scotland, ahead of the 2026 Commonwealth Games.

The Belize delegation includes CEO Nicole Usher Solano, Cherie Nisbet, Belize High Commissioner to the United Kingdom, and Allan Sharp, President of the Belize Olympic and Commonwealth Games Association.

The meeting brought together sports ministers, senior government officials and Commonwealth Games leaders from across the Commonwealth under the theme “Reimagining the Power of Sport towards Healthier, Fairer and Equitable Commonwealth Communities.”

Discussions focused on strengthening international cooperation, promoting integrity and inclusion in sport, advancing athlete safeguarding, and leveraging sport as a catalyst for health, youth development and sustainable growth. The meeting also adopted a joint outcome statement to help shape Commonwealth priorities ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) later this year.

Belize is represented at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games by five athletes competing in Swimming, Cycling and Athletics.

The Ministry extended best wishes to Team Belize as they proudly represent our nation in the Commonwealth Games from July 23-August 2.

World.title: International News: More than 70,000 evacuated as wildfires rage near Madrid, Spain
World.content:
International News: More than 70,000 evacuated as wildfires rage near Madrid, Spain

By Zoila Palma: More than 70,000 people have been forced to evacuate their homes as severe forest fires spread across areas near Spain’s capital, Madrid.

Authorities have ordered residents to flee to safety as firefighters battle the blazes amid challenging conditions.

In the province of Ávila, northwest of Madrid, approximately 38,000 people have been evacuated, according to Francisco Martín Aguirre, the Spanish government’s prefect for Madrid. Another 35,000 people have reportedly been evacuated from areas surrounding the capital, while more than 20,000 others are unable to leave their homes because of the fires.

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s government on Friday declared a “state of emergency of national significance” in the Greater Madrid area and Ávila.

According to Spain’s public broadcaster RTVE, it is the first time the country has issued such a declaration in response to forest fires.

The Interior Ministry said weather conditions improved overnight on Saturday, helping emergency crews in their efforts to contain the fires.

World.title: CARICOM launches “I am Agriculture” video competition for high school students across region
World.content:
CARICOM launches “I am Agriculture” video competition for high school students across region

By Zoila Palma: The Caribbean Community (CARICOM) is inviting secondary schools across the region to participate in its “I am Agriculture: Youth in Agriculture” High School Video Competition, giving students an opportunity to showcase their creativity while highlighting the importance of agriculture.

Schools are being challenged to produce a 60-second video that demonstrates why agriculture matters and inspires their communities, countries and the wider Caribbean region.

The competition aims to encourage greater youth engagement in agriculture and promote awareness of the sector’s role in the region’s development.

Students can compete for cash prizes, with US$1,700 awarded to the first-place winner, US$1,300 for second place and US$1,000 for third place. The competition is open to secondary schools across CARICOM, and entries must be submitted by September 4, 2026, at 11:59 p.m.

The first-place prize will be presented during the 20th Caribbean Week of Agriculture, scheduled to take place in Jamaica from September 27 to October 2, 2026.

World.title: International News: Nearly £20 million worth of cocaine seized from banana shipment in UK
World.content:
International News: Nearly £20 million worth of cocaine seized from banana shipment in UK

By Zoila Palma: UK Border Force officers have seized approximately £19.2 million worth of cocaine that was concealed inside crates of bananas aboard a refrigerated cargo ship.

The 240-kilogram shipment was discovered after the MV Atlantic Klipper docked in Portsmouth, having travelled from South America via the Caribbean, BBC reports.

The National Crime Agency (NCA) said the Class A drug was seized on Wednesday and has launched an investigation into the shipment. The cocaine was subsequently moved to a secure location with support from the Joint Operations Unit, a specialist collaboration between Hampshire Police and Thames Valley Police.

The NCA said the seizure represents a major blow to the organized crime group responsible for transporting the drugs.

World.title: Team Belize proudly represents at 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games in Dominican Republic
World.content:
Team Belize proudly represents at 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games in Dominican Republic

By Zoila Palma: Following a vibrant ceremony on Friday, the competition begins today for our Beach Volleyball teams at the 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic.

“Best of luck to Francis Hauze & Ernest Broaster and Nelissa Ramirez & Clara Sabal as they proudly represent Belize on the sand. Check the competition schedule to see the times they will be competing,” Belize Volleyball Association said.

The Belize Volleyball Association extended best wishes to Team Belize and our entire delegation as competition gets underway across the Games.

“Represent Belize with pride, give it your all, and enjoy every moment on this regional stage.

Go Team Belize!,” the association expressed.

World.title: Belize achieves full membership in World Health Organization Global Drug Safety Monitoring Programme
World.content:
Belize achieves full membership in World Health Organization Global Drug Safety Monitoring Programme

By Zoila Palma: Belize has officially become a full member of the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Programme for International Drug Monitoring (PIDM), marking a major step forward in the country’s efforts to strengthen medicines safety and protect public health.

The achievement follows years of work by the Ministry of Health and Wellness to improve Belize’s national pharmacovigilance system, regulatory oversight and monitoring of medical products, with technical support from the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO). Belize initially joined the programme as an Associate Member in 2020.

According to PAHO, full membership recognizes Belize’s growing ability to “detect, assess, understand, and prevent adverse effects or other medicine-related problems,” while allowing the country to contribute data and expertise to the global monitoring network coordinated by WHO and the Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC).

PAHO has supported Belize through initiatives focused on post-marketing surveillance, adverse event reporting, health professional training, data exchange and participation in regional and international regulatory networks.

A key factor in Belize achieving full membership was improved interoperability and information exchange, strengthened through the Data Bridges project supported by PAHO.

“This enables the country to contribute to regional and global efforts to identify potential safety signals and respond to emerging risks associated with medical products,” PAHO noted.

Belize now has direct reporting links to global surveillance systems through VigiFlow/VigiBase and the Global Surveillance and Monitoring System (GSMS), while also strengthening its Drug Inspectorate Unit and expanding regulatory and surveillance activities.

“Strengthening regulatory systems remains a public health priority for the Pan American Health Organization,” PAHO said, noting that Member States endorsed a policy in 2022 aimed at strengthening national regulatory systems for medicines and other health technologies.

As a full PIDM member, Belize will have greater opportunities to collaborate internationally, access global safety analyses and information, and contribute to the detection of medicine-related risks, including those linked to substandard and falsified medical products.

World.title: Hitman’s appeal denied
World.content:
Simone Campbell-Collymore, whose confessed killer Wade Blackwood had his appeal rejected on Friday.

THE Court of Appeal on Friday upheld the sentence and conviction of killer Wade Blackwood, who in 2021 was sentenced to life in prison after confessing to being the trigger man in the 2018 murder of 32-year-old businesswoman Simone Campbell-Collymore.

The then 24-year-old, in a confession, detailed how he had been subcontracted to kill Campbell-Collymore in a $2-million murder-for-hire plot hatched by her then husband Omar “Best” Collymore.

Thirty-six-year-old taxi driver Winston Walters was also killed during the incident which took place outside Campbell-Collymore’s Forest Ridge apartment in Red Hills, St Andrew, on January 2, 2018.

The two men involved in the shooting that day were identified by the police, from closed-circuit television footage in the vicinity, as Blackwood and a now-deceased Corporate Area don who went by the name Jim.

Blackwood, who had been held by cops in April 2018, had pleaded guilty in January 2021 to two counts of murder and one count of illegal possession of firearm before the Home Circuit Court in downtown Kingston.

He was sentenced to life imprisonment for his role in the murders, ahead of the other individuals involved in the plot, with 35 years on each count of murder before eligibility for parole, and eight years and six months for illegal possession of firearm. Those sentences, however, were to run concurrently, making it so that he would serve 35 years before applying for parole.

Friday, the Appeal Court, which heard the matter over two days, in handing down its decision ruled that based on the fact that Blackwood was resentenced on February 9, 2024, after a plea agreement was reached, the basis of his appeal was obsolete.

Blackwood, through his attorney Shenieka Sparks, in supplemental grounds of appeal filed this year, had contended that a discount for his guilty plea was “unreasoned and inadequate”.

He further argued that the sentencing judge had erred in setting 30 years as a starting point to arrive at his ultimate sentence. According to Blackwood, compared to other similar cases, the discount was “out of parity”.

The Jamaica Observer was told that when Blackwood was advised of the decision of the Appeal Court he accepted that he would not continue challenging his sentence and a notice of abandonment was filed on his behalf.

As such, Blackwood will serve 20 years before he is eligible for parole, as was the sentence imposed on following his plea deal.

In February 2024, Blackwood — who testified against his co-accused following a deal with prosecutors — claimed he was pressured into committing the act by Jim, who was supposedly the leader of a gang his brother had been involved with.

Blackwood claimed that Jim, in levelling death threats at him and his family, told him that he had to carry out the killing to repay his brother’s debt for a firearm that had been seized by the police.

Blackwood, in negotiating with the prosecution, had 15 years shaved off his sentence, which now makes him eligible for parole after 20 years.

At the end of the substantive trial, Collymore, who was slapped with two life sentences, was also sentenced to one year and six months for conspiracy and ordered to serve 46 years and six months before becoming eligible for parole. His co-conspirators Dwayne Pink, Michael Adams, and Shaquille Edwards were also handed life sentences.

In the highly publicised incident, Campbell-Collymore and Walters were ambushed and shot dead outside the apartment complex where she lived with her then husband and children.

The Crown, at the close of its case, established that Collymore ordered the hit to claim his wife’s multimillion-dollar life insurance policies from which their two children were entitled to 15 per cent each while Collymore was entitled to 70 per cent of the benefits.

He was also listed as trustee for the children and their portion. Those policies were taken out by the couple three months before the murders.

Collymore was collared by cops at Norman Manley International Airport while attempting to flee the island a day before his wife’s funeral.

Earlier this month, Collymore, alongside his co-accused Pink, Adams, and Edwards, appeared before the Home Circuit Court again where they are all facing charges of illegal possession of firearm, shooting with intent, and conspiracy to murder with respect to an unnamed woman the businessman was in a relationship with at the time he orchestrated his wife’s death.

A new conspirator, Carey Jonas, is also named on the indictment with respect to the new matter.

On Thursday, Edwards, who had entered into plea negotiations with the prosecution and pleaded guilty to the new charges, was sentenced to six years and nine months for his part in that crime.

Edwards, however, has already spent more than seven years in custody and is set to be released.

World.title: No ease in honey shortage
World.content:
President of the St James Bee Farmers Association Dennis McKay with two bottles of honey, on Tuesday.

MONTEGO BAY, St James — The nation could be facing a severe honey shortage by the end of the year as the long-term effects of last October’s Hurricane Melissa continue to cripple the beekeeping industry, according to president of the St James Bee Farmers’ Association Dennis McKay.

He said even the intense heat now being felt across the country pales in comparison to the lingering effects of the Category 5 storm.

“It’s not so much the heat that is the crisis for the bees. Probably the major problem at this time is the impact of the hurricane and the trees that are missing. The storm turned down all the trees that provide the nectar and the pollen that support the bees. They are unable to get the nectar, so they cannot get enough nectar to store that we can get honey,” McKay told the Jamaica Observer Tuesday.

He explained that this period would ordinarily be the height of the honey-producing season, when beekeepers harvest their largest volumes. However, with many nectar-producing trees destroyed and only now beginning to recover, bees are gathering just enough food to sustain their colonies rather than building honey reserves.

“As the bees get the little nectar, it is only enough to feed them, not enough to store. So that is the major crisis as it relates to where the beekeeping and the honey business is going to go,” he said.

The dramatic decline in production has left many farmers with only a fraction of their usual harvest.

“A man used to get maybe 100 bottles from an apiary, [now] he only gets four bottles,” McKay said, adding that even large commercial operators who previously sold honey by the drum are now only able to provide a few bottles.

“He’s not getting enough that he can be selling by the drum, like before,” he added.

McKay also noted that many beekeepers suffered another devastating blow when they lost entire colonies during the hurricane.

“We are heading into a honey crisis,” he warned.

According to McKay, the dwindling supply has already sent up retail prices.

“Right now, honey used to be selling for $3,000 a bottle. I went into a supermarket and see it for $4,800, before tax added. This is the middle of the honey season; this is a time when everybody get honey,” he said.

McKay predicted that prices could climb even higher by Christmas.

“Going down to December, you might be paying $7,000 per bottle,” he cautioned.

While some damaged trees are beginning to regenerate, McKay said recovery is likely to be gradual and warned that another major weather event could worsen the situation.

“The existing trees now that are coming up, they may blossom next year, or we might have to start talking about importation of honey,” he said.

However, he expressed concern about relying on imported supplies, arguing that consumers cannot always be certain of their authenticity.

“I am seeing online where honey is made without bees. It’s only when you buy your local honey [that] you can have certain confidence that at least it come from bees,” McKay said.

Following the hurricane, the Government distributed sugar to beekeepers to help sustain weakened colonies. McKay said the assistance was useful when nectar was scarce.

“Bees don’t make honey with sugar. They use the sugar syrup to feed their young. As soon as trees start to blossom they don’t want that sugar water anymore,” he underscored.

He also suggested that support programmes should have included replacing lost colonies, noting that while some districts still have flowering trees, many of the bees needed to pollinate them and produce honey were wiped out during the hurricane.

“We have to be concerned because some people depend on that for a living,” McKay said.

World.title: Job scam victims repaid in court but case not closed
World.content:
MONTEGO BAY, St James — Decarlos Christie, who pleaded guilty to conspiracy to defraud, has repaid a total of $200,000 to two women who fell prey to a job scam.

With the payment, part of his case has been resolved but he has been remanded as he still owes one of the women $57,000. There is also a third alleged victim.

Decarlos, who is jointly charged with his brother Bryan Christie, appeared before Judge Kaysha Grant-Pryce in the St James Parish Court on Wednesday. Two of three complainants attended the hearing. One was repaid the full $52,000 she had paid while another received $148,000 of the $205,000 of which she was allegedly defrauded. Judge Grant-Pryce has directed that efforts be made to contact the third complainant

Following Wednesday’s guilty plea Decarlos was admonished and discharged in relation to the matter involving the complainant who received full restitution. He is expected to pay the outstanding balance owed to the second complainant by July 29, when the matter will next be before the court. While he was remanded in custody, his brother’s bail was extended.

During the hearing Decarlos maintained that his brother, Bryan, used his personal information without his knowledge or consent to carry out the transactions while he was in custody in St Ann on unrelated matters. Decarlos insisted that he had no involvement in the alleged scheme.

According to the allegations, in January the first complainant was introduced by telephone to a man identifying himself only as “Mr Campbell”, who claimed to be offering overseas job placement opportunities. She was allegedly instructed to deposit $52,000 into a bank account registered to Decarlos Christie.

Police say a second complainant later deposited $205,000 into the same account for the same purpose, while a third complainant transferred $10,000. Investigators allege the complainants were subsequently assured they would travel to Kingston as part of the overseas employment programme. However, the promised arrangements did not materialise, prompting reports to the police.

During the investigation, police reportedly found that Decarlos’s bank card and account information were in Bryan’s possession, leading to the former being charged. Police further allege that Bryan was the individual who communicated with the complainants while posing as “Mr Campbell” and offering the overseas job opportunities.

World.title: Rvssian continues to rise on Billboard Latin charts
World.content:
From left: Rauw Alejandro, Wizkid and Rvssian.

Jamaican producer Tarik “Rvssian” Johnston continues to make moves on the Billboard Latin charts with his latest entry PONGO, which features Rauw Alejandro and Wizkid.

On Hot Latin Rhythm Songs, PONGO bolts from #22 to #14 in its 9th week. This is Rvssian’s first entry on this particular Billboard chart.

However, on Latin Airplay, the song which peaked at #41 in May, steps up a notch from #47 to #46. This is his fifth entry on Latin Airplay, with Nostalgico being his highest peak at #9 in 2021.

PONGO re-enters Hot Latin Songs at #38 and becomes the eighth entry on the chart for the Head Concussion Records/Rich Immigrants boss. His highest peak on this chart came in 2017 with Kippy Kush, featuring Farruko, Nicki Minaj, Bad Bunny, and 21 Savage stalling at #5.

The song becomes Rvssian’s sixth entry on Latin Rhythm Airplay, cruising from #13 to #11 in its 16th week. Both Santa and Nostalgico are his biggest hits on this chart, with each peaking at #6.

Echo (FIFA World Cup 2026) by Daddy Yankee and Shenseea, which rose to #1 three weeks ago on Latin Airplay, tumbles from #6 to #28.

Spin by American R&B singer Kevin Ross, which was produced by Jamaican producer Kheilstone, remains at #5 on Billboard’s Hot Adult R&B Airplay, while staying firm at #22 on Billboard’s R&B/Hip Hop Airplay chart.

Jamaican (Bam Bam), a reconstructed house/Afrobeats/dance version of Sister Nancy’s 1982 hit Bam Bam (credited to producers HUGEL and SOLTO) backtracks from #14 to #15 on Billboard’s Warm Global Dance Radio chart (it peaked at #4), while on Hot Dance/Electronic Songs chart it rises from #19 to #17 in its 24th week.

The song dances from #31 to #28 in its 17th week on Billboard’s Global Excluding US chart, and bullets from #63 to #53 on Billboard’s Global 200.

Still on Global 200, (When You Gonna) Give it Up to Me by Sean Paul and Keyshia Cole moves from #117 to #110. Sean Paul’s other entry, Cheap Thrills, with Sia, inches up from #139 to #138.

Sean Paul continues the double on Global Excluding US, with Cheap Thrills firm at #90 and (When You Gonna) Give it Up to Me inching up from #71 to #68.

Over on the Billboard Reggae Albums chart, Legend by Bob Marley and the Wailers remains at #1 for 340 non-consecutive weeks, while Best of Shaggy: The Boombastic Collection by Shaggy and Sean Paul’s The Trinity at #2 and #3 respectively.

World.title: Hill wary of call for ganja amnesty
World.content:
HILL...I have to remind you all that ganja is a Schedule 1 drug. It’s the same thing as fentanyl, the same thing as cocaine

SAVANNA-LA-MAR, Westmoreland — While a key stakeholder in the cannabis industry continues to call for an amnesty to regularise farmers operating outside the regulated sector, Minister of Industry, Investment and Commerce Senator Aubyn Hill has sounded a cautionary note. He pointed to the complex international legal landscape in explaining his stance on the matter.

“I have to remind you all that ganja is a Schedule 1 drug. It’s the same thing as fentanyl, the same thing as cocaine. It’s in the same category as heroin. It is seen as a bad drug,” the minister stressed.

He was addressing a Westmoreland Chamber of Commerce and Industry meeting at the Hotel Commingle in Savanna-la-Mar on Wednesday. He gave a breakdown on the implications for international trade and travel.

“Even today, because it’s a Schedule 1 drug, if you fly in the airspace of the United States, you are illegal. You can be taken out. You see what happened to those guys out there in the sea? That can happen to a ganja plane flying in the airspace of the United States, legally,” warned the minister.

He further emphasised that strict compliance with international drug laws is essential to maintaining Jamaica’s standing in global trade.

Hill was responding to questions posed by Cannabis Licensing Authority (CLA) board member Verald Vassell, better known as Ras Iyah V. The Westmoreland ganja advocate — who served on the CLA board from 2016 to 2021 and returned in 2024 — has consistently pointed to the need for an amnesty to transition illicit farmers into the legal medical cannabis industry.

During Wednesday night’s meeting Ras Iyah V highlighted what he said was continued harassment farmers face at the hands of the police.

“As the minister in charge of the CLA, what are the plans? Because I know the regulation has been amended recently. But what are the plans, the road map, and if you can explain how this is going to work? Because, as for me, I see a certain approach that creates a glut in the market, and then there is no market… Can you explain what is the road map going forward to bring our ganja farmers from being considered illegal into the legal industry? Because most of these farmers have been out-financed,” stated Ras Iyah V.

Acknowledging the concerns raised by the advocate, Hill outlined recent legislative changes aimed at easing operational restrictions for small-scale cultivators.

“Under my leadership with the permanent secretary and the people in the ministry, we changed the law. Because the very small farmer was constantly complaining of being put upon, [saying] they can’t get their things done. And we said, ‘Alright, you must have a fence of… five feet,” relayed Hill.

The minister pointed out that these regulatory adjustments provide greater flexibility for traditional farmers and workers trying to satisfy compliance requirements.

Addressing the issue of a market glut, Hill attributed the surplus to the initial surge of interest following the decriminalisation of cannabis.

“Understand that the glut that is developing is because when ganja was decriminalised, the euphoria that came around it encouraged people to go into it. Everybody was in it. There was one firm in Canada that seemed to have made a lot of money and then the thing collapsed. But that euphoria took a lot of people in,” the minister said.

Under the Dangerous Drugs Act, which came into effect on April 15, 2015, provisions were implemented for the possession and smoking of ganja; the use of ganja by those of the Rastafarian faith; and the use of ganja for medical, therapeutic, and scientific purposes.

“Our law allows people who use ganja for their religious practices to be exempt. But they have to go through a process,” explained Hill.

Regarding ongoing police enforcement, he noted that while adults are permitted to possess up to two ounces of ganja without criminal charges, the police must act whenever boundaries are breached.

World.title: ‘Record everything’
World.content:
Health and Wellness Minister Dr Christopher Tufton addressing Members of Parliament and senior ministry officials during a working breakfast on the Health Hurricane Response Programme (HHRP) on Thursday. Garfield Robinson

Health Minister Dr Christopher Tufton has urged officials working on the ministry’s $6.04-billion Health Hurricane Response Programme (HHRP) to meticulously document every decision and expenditure.

According to Tufton, he wants no discrepancies to tarnish the project when the Auditor General’s Department inevitably comes to scrutinise the rebuilding project.

Speaking on Thursday at a working breakfast with Members of Parliament from the five western parishes affected by the October 2025 Hurricane Melissa, who heard an update on the HHRP, Tufton said that while the Ministry of Health and Wellness intends to move quickly to restore and modernise damaged health facilities, speed must not come at the expense of transparency or accountability.

The HHRP is a Government-funded initiative aimed at restoring, retrofitting and expanding health services disrupted by Hurricane Melissa. Backed by approximately $6.04 billion over three fiscal years beginning in 2026/27, the programme will rehabilitate and modernise the Savanna-la-Mar Public General Hospital and 101 health centres and across Hanover, Westmoreland, St James, Trelawny and St Elizabeth.

It also seeks to introduce the ministry’s Primary Health Care Reform by reclassifying selected facilities into community, district, and comprehensive health centres, bringing more services closer to where people live.

Against that backdrop, Tufton made it clear that the programme’s legacy should not be overshadowed by avoidable procurement or governance concerns.

“For us, what is important is the completion of the project with standards. They have been instructed to record everything, to catalogue every step because, as night follows day, the auditor general will audit. And I’m saying this to all of us here because sometimes we have particular requests that sometimes may be reasonable, sometimes may not be too reasonable: I don’t want, in another year or two, we table something in Parliament that says the hurricane response programme is plagued with all sorts of whatever,” Tufton said.

He urged programme managers to keep comprehensive records so they will be able to satisfy any future review by oversight bodies.

“So the team has specific instructions: Document everything. And make sure when the auditor general comes you just hand them the box with all the files, because they will come — and I’m not criticising them, that’s their job — but document everything and just hand it to them. And the same for the IC [Integrity Commission] or whoever else who may want to come.

“So it means that if they tell you something can’t work, you may say, ‘Okay, explain it,’ and they’re instructed to explain but we’re working quickly, which is all the more reason why we have to follow the rules,” he expressed.

The minister also acknowledged that some of the biggest hurdles facing the programme have little to do with construction itself.

Among them is unresolved land ownership issues affecting dozens of health facilities earmarked for upgrading, a problem he said must be addressed before public money can be invested in those locations.

“We have to deal with approvals, mayors — [and] that’s a big issue because, believe it, some of these health centres are on lands that we have no title for and or they are leased, some long-term lease,” Tufton said, explaining why local authorities and agencies would play a critical role in keeping the programme on schedule.

He stressed that while the Government wants to accelerate the rebuilding programme, it cannot ignore legal and regulatory requirements surrounding public expenditure.

World.title: MAJOR MOVES!
World.content:
Nickalia Fuller, formerly of Tivoli Gardens Photo: Naphtali Junior

MOUNT Pleasant Football Academy have made a habit of attracting Jamaica’s top football talent since its promotion to the Jamaica Premier League in 2018.

The reigning Concacaf Caribbean Cup champions have done it again by securing the signatures of coveted attackers Nickalia Fuller and Trayvone Reid.

Jamaica Reggae Boyz winger Fuller and last season’s Jamaica Premier League (JPL) golden boot runner-up Reid are currently in Trinidad and Tobago with Mount Pleasant, who are seeking one of two qualifying spots in next month’s Caribbean Cup through the Caribbean Football Union (CFU) Club Shield.

Twenty-one-year-old Fuller leaves his hometown club Tivoli Gardens FC after four seasons, having registered 16 goals and eight assists across the last two campaigns. His performances earned him a place in the Reggae Boyz squad this year under interim Head Coach Rudolph Speid, scoring once in four appearances.

Mount Pleasant attempted to sign Fuller during the January transfer window, but he opted to remain at Tivoli who eventually finished tenth, missing the play-offs.

With the signing finally completed, Sporting Director Paul Christie believes Fuller can make a significant impact at the club.

“His resume is there, he’s one of the most exciting young players in the entire JPL,” he told the

Jamaica Observer. “We hope that he can replicate that at Mount Pleasant, donning the Mount Pleasant brand and hopefully that he can light up not only Jamaica but the Caribbean and Concacaf should Mount Pleasant carry the flag as deep into that realm of the season.”

“We’ve seen a glimpse of what he can do. We are seeing it now in the blue so we hope that he continues and grow from strength to strength and continue enhancing the brand for the project so that we can continue to create future leaders and impact positively on lives and livelihood for the people not only in Jamaica but in the Caribbean.”

Reid, another Tivoli product, has also made the journey to the north coast club after having one of the best individual performances in JPL history.

Despite Harbour View’s relegation, the 26-year-old registered an impressive 21 goals and six assists in 37 games, the most goal contributions by a local player in the 21st century.

Christie, however, believes former Kingston College and national youth player Reid will bring more than just goals to the club.

“There are things about this player that a lot of people in Jamaica don’t know. He’s competitive, he’s a leader, he has a football brain and a football mindset and Mount Pleasant and Jamaica and the Caribbean should benefit from that,” he said.

Although Fuller and Reid are widely viewed as the marquee signings, Christie says the acquisition of Reggae Boyz defender Ricardo Thomas is a major boost to the club’s quality.

The 28-year-old left back, who has 14 caps for Jamaica, joins from Arnett Gardens where he spent the last two seasons.

“His profile would fit in the Mount Pleasant model and we are just privileged to be able to have him at this time and I would think that he can assist us to raise the level and to help us get to our ultimate goal,” said Christie.

Nothing is guaranteed but I think we are lucky to find this fit for the programme and the project at this time so I think that he’s a good capture. He has settled well and been training well so far.”

Mount Pleasant have also welcomed back young star Kevaughn Wilson who spent last season on loan at Arnett Gardens. Defender Gadaill Irving, striker Chevaughn Walsh and wingers Devonte Campbell and Alex Marshall have all left the club.

New signings Fuller, Reid and Thomas could all make their debuts on Tuesday when Mount Pleasant begin action in the quarterfinals of the CFU Club Shield.

Theodore Whitmore’s men, who arrived in Trinidad on Wednesday, were due to start their campaign in the round of 16 on Sunday but their opponents All Saints United of Antigua and Barbuda withdrew from the tournament,

Mount Pleasant now await the winner of Sunday’s clash between Weymouth Wales of Barbados and SV Britannia of Aruba.

The finalists of the Club Shield will advance to the Caribbean Cup, joining the likes of JPL champions Portmore United and finalists Cavalier FC.

World.title: One traffic light not enough for Trelawny, says mayor after deadly crash
World.content:
The mangled Toyota bus involved in last Friday morning’s fatal crash in Trelawny Horace Hines

FALMOUTH, Trelawny — Mayor of Falmouth and chairman of the Trelawny Municipal Corporation, Councillor C Junior Gager says he will be renewing calls for the installation of traffic lights and additional street lights across the parish following last week’s crash on the Trelawny bypass that claimed seven lives.

Trelawny has only one set of traffic lights, near Florence Hall.

Gager, who said traffic lights at key locations would help reduce speeding, pledged to intensify representation for their installation. He also said he will continue pressing for more street lights to improve night-time visibility.

“We do think traffic lights are needed at various sections of the roadway in the parish — that would help to ease down the speed of the motor vehicles on the roadways — so yes, we will be making representation for traffic lights,” the mayor told reporters this week.

“We are also making representation for street lights so that in the night, the place is properly lit. We will be meeting soon and we will try to make representation, or repeat the requests that we have been making over time, so that we can see how best this might be accommodated,” he added.

The mayor commended the Trelawny police for their consistent highway patrols but lamented that some motorists return to speeding once cops leave the area.

“The police are doing a very good job but sometimes when they aren’t there, that’s when motorists decide to speed,” he said, adding that many drivers continue to ignore posted speed limits.

Describing the recent tragedy as “cause for concern”, Gager said the loss of seven lives underscores the need for improvements to road safety.

“One life lost is one too many,” he said, encouraging drivers who become tired or sleepy to pull over and rest rather than risk continuing their journey.

“We might want to reach our destination at a certain time but it is best we reach there safe and sound,” he added.

The mayor also extended condolence to the families and friends of the seven victims.

“I want the families to know that we share in the grief they are experiencing,” Gager said.

According to the Trelawny police, a Toyota Hiace bus carrying five occupants was travelling towards St Ann while a Hino motor truck carrying three occupants was heading towards Montego Bay.

Investigators reported that on reaching the vicinity of Bogue Gate, the Toyota bus reportedly drifted onto the right side of the road and slammed head-on into the oncoming truck.

Five people, including the driver of the Hino truck, died at the scene. The remaining occupants were rushed by ambulance to Falmouth Public General Hospital where two later succumbed to their injuries. The condition of the Toyota bus driver, who was said to be in a critical state after the crash, is not immediately known.

World.title: Romanian airspace violated twice in 2 days
World.content:
Romanian Air Force F-16 fighter jets waiting for an aerial refueling, while they participate in an exercice. | Clement Mahoudeau/AFP via Getty Images

Romanian fighter jets shot down drones in separate incidents on Friday and Saturday.

Romanian fighter jets on Friday and Saturday morning shot down two drones that were violating the country's airspace.

On Saturday morning, Romanian radar "detected another unauthorized penetration of the national airspace by a drone operating in the vicinity of the Ukrainian border" and two Romanian F-16 jets shot it down in an unpopulated area close to the border, the Romanian defense ministry said in a statement. Romania already shot down another drone on Friday.

Romanian Foreign Minister Oana Toiu said that the drone shot down on Friday "was a Shahed-type drone, the same kind Russia launches, night after night, against Ukraine."

"Two incursions in 48 hours are not an accident, they are a pattern, and our answer to that pattern is consistency: detection, interception, protection of our citizens, full transparency with our allies," Toiu said.

In a social media post, European Council President António Costa "commend[ed] the Romanian authorities for their swift and effective response."

World.title: Record-breaking wildfires burned nearly 100,000 hectares in France, interior minister says
World.content:
Nearly 200,000 people have been evacuated because of the fires in southwestern France out of which more than 167,000 are in Gironde, the department of Bordeaux, and around 30,000 in the nearby Landes department.

French President Emmanuel Macron on Friday announced that he requested the activation of an EU emergency mechanism, which has prompted other EU countries including Portugal, Croatia, Slovakia and Sweden to send airplanes and helicopters to help France.

"Europe stands with France and Spain against the devastating wildfires that are hitting them," European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wrote in a social media post on Saturday, stressing that France is already benefitting from five planes and two helicopters provided by other EU countries while four planes will arrive in Spain on Saturday.

France's Nuñez confirmed that Saturday afternoon an Airbus A400 military plane will start throwing a fire retardant product at the wildfires. That is on the top of Canadair and other French and European aircraft.

The wildfires have been the subject of political controversy in France in recent days, with both the hard-left France Unbowed and the far-right National Rally accusing Macron of underinvesting.

Spain has declared the state of emergency in the Madrid and Ávila regions.

"Our priority is to save lives, protect communities, and fight the fires," Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said on Saturday. Around 80,000 people have been evacuated or are confined because of the wildfires, Spanish media report.

World.title: Italy’s defense minister offered adviser job to ousted Ukrainian defense chief
World.content:
The Italian minister said Fedorov was "moved" by the proposal and saw it as "a mark of respect and friendship," but he didn't elaborate on whether Fedorov accepted or not.

Crosetto strongly praised Fedorov, who has been credited with bringing a technology overhaul to Ukraine's military but also clashed with top generals.

“Fedorov embodies innovation; he is one of those who has completely changed the rules of the game on the battlefield, enabling Ukraine first to hold its ground and then to take the initiative,” Crosetto said, adding that Fedorov was faced with "a resistance to change" that is also a problem in Italy, France and Germany.

Fedorov hasn't responded publicly to Crosetto's offer.

Crosetto, who is a top figure in Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's Brothers of Italy party, also made clear that he is in favor of continuing to borrow via EU loans from the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) scheme rather than financing defense spending through national public debt. But he made clear that it was up for the Treasury to make that decision.

Crosetto's comments come as the Italian government is mulling applying for only €5 billion to €7 billion under the SAFE scheme, instead of €15 billion, as initially planned.

World.title: NATO intern arrested over espionage suspicions
World.content:
The Canadian national of Chinese origin is suspected of spying for a third country and being part of a criminal organization.

Belgian police on Friday arrested an intern at NATO's strategic headquarters of the Allied Powers Europe (SHAPE,) suspecting her of "spying on behalf of a third country and of being a member of a criminal organization," the Belgian Federal Prosecutor Office wrote in a statement on Saturday.

The intern, a Canadian national of Chinese origins, "had come to the attention" of the security services of SHAPE, NATO’s strategic command for operations in Mons, Belgium.

Belgian authorities searched her home and office on Thursday.

Belgian prosecutors gave no further details on what the woman is suspected of.

Camille Gijs contributed to this report.

World.title: ICC member states remove chief prosecutor over sexual misconduct claims
World.content:
“I have no other way to describe it but an escalation of attempts,” she said in the interview, adding that she feared for her job and hence was afraid to say “no” to Khan’s advances.

Khan has denied any wrongdoing and, according to Reuters, called the Friday vote “unlawful, procedurally unfair and unsupported by evidence.”

The vote to fire Khan comes a week after the U.S. administration announced a campaign to dismantle what it called a “threat posed by the ICC to U.S. sovereignty.” Washington argues that the court should not have the authority to investigate and prosecute U.S. citizens.

Last year, the U.S. sanctioned Khan and other ICC employees after they issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant over alleged war crimes in Gaza.

World.title: We’ve fallen in love with drones, but they’re not the sole answer
World.content:
They are not. But nor are they mere bit players.

The enthusiasm for drones is understandable. According to the Kyiv Post, on July 9 alone “Ukraine said it struck 14 Russian vessels overnight in the Sea of Azov, including 12 tankers allegedly belonging to Moscow’s sanctioned ‘shadow fleet.’ Ukraine’s drone commander said a total of 35 ships had been hit over the previous 96 hours, while Ukrainian forces also targeted 45 military sites in occupied Crimea and southern Ukraine.”

It’s as if Ukrainian drones are everywhere. And not only is Ukraine using them to hit Russian targets without causing devastating losses to human life the way, say, missiles would; it’s also able to do so at enormous distances.

Drones hit Russian shadow vessels in the Black Sea. They hit Russian shadow vessels in the Mediterranean. They hit Russia’s oil refineries. They hit Russia’s Baltic Sea oil terminals. They’re causing constant problems for the Russian military, and have hit Russia itself. Earlier this month they even struck an oil refinery in Siberia.

In fact, Ukraine’s drones have become such a success that they’re triggering increasingly loud demands for NATO’s European members to shift their focus to these mostly small and cheap weapons. Look at how drones have helped Ukraine shift the course of the war! Look at how much you can achieve at relatively small expense! Drones are the future! Our governments are behind the curve! That’s how the argument goes.

But while drones are indisputably part of the future of warfare, they’re also still experimental and lack clear rules of engagement.

World.title: Israel's move to recognise Armenian genocide stalls under regional pressure
World.content:
The Israeli parliament's decision to postpone a vote on recognising the Armenian genocide by Ottoman Turkey is being seen as a triumph for regional diplomacy, as Azerbaijan in particular seeks to avert a further escalation in tensions between its close allies.

Advertising

The Israeli government gave no official reason for postponing the vote to formally recognise the Armenian genocide by Ottoman Turkey during World War I, which would have ratified a motion approved by the cabinet last month.

Ankara strongly denies the deaths of hundreds of thousands of Armenians constitute genocide.

While the motion's architect, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar, called recognition a “moral duty”, critics say the move took aim at Turkey amidst rising tensions.

Based in Tbilisi, Israeli defence and security expert Eugene Kogan claims Israel badly miscalculated. “Foreign Minister Sa'ar could have waited and not just dropped a bomb that led to different repercussions coming from different sides,” he said.

Armenia, which is seeking to normalise ties with Turkey, reacted coolly, with Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan saying he saw no need to comment. Meanwhile, Israel’s close ally Azerbaijan reportedly lobbied Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to drop the motion.

“At the end of the day, it might be either dropped or dismissed, and it will not come again to the new parliament agenda,” predicted Kogan.

The Knesset dissolved on 17 July and won't reconvene until after elections scheduled for 27 October.

Israel's recognition of the Armenian genocide unsettles Turkey and Azerbaijan

Azerbaijan's influence

The Israeli newspaper Haaretz reported that pressure from Azerbaijan tipped the scales, though officials deny it.

Azerbaijan supplies nearly 40 percent of Israel’s oil and is a major customer for Israeli arms. The two countries’ partnership involves frequent Israeli ministerial visits and strong military cooperation, especially crucial for Israel given Azerbaijan’s border with Iran.

Baku also maintains a deep alliance with Ankara, summed up in the phrase “one nation, two states”. As Israeli-Turkish tensions flare over the Gaza conflict and Ankara’s support for Hamas, Azerbaijan is walking a diplomatic tightrope.

Zaur Gasimov, a Caucasus expert at Istanbul’s Turkish-German University, believes Baku viewed the Israeli genocide motion as a direct threat to its difficult balancing act.

“I can imagine that there were negotiations and talks on various levels between political elites of both countries,” he said. “For Israel, Azerbaijan is still of paramount importance. I would even say it's much more significant than it used to be with regard to the situation in and around Iran. So Baku was and is maybe the key intermediary between Israel and the Republic of Turkey.”

In what may be a calculated move to turn up the heat on Israel, Azerbaijan’s President Ilham Aliyev welcomed Palestinian Prime Minister Mohammad Mustafa this month. It was the first visit by a Palestinian leader since 2011.

“They [Israel] perceive it with a great sense of caution,” claimed analyst Kogan. “They don't know exactly what came out of this particular meeting between Aliyev and the Palestinian prime minister. And so there is a lot of guessing games right now taking place in both Tel Aviv and Jerusalem about the outcome.”

Such ambiguity over Baku’s intentions could strengthen its diplomatic hand, he suggested: “If Aliyev is involved in this Palestinian issue directly and no longer indirectly, it makes the situation very different for the Israelis.”

Turkey warns it could be Israel's 'next enemy' as tensions escalate

Syrian precedent

Baku is already leveraging its strong relationships with both Israel and Turkey to cool tempers.

“We have organised meetings between Turkey and Israel in Baku, specifically at the very beginning of the change of the Assad regime in Syria, where both parties had their own legitimate concerns,” said Hikmet Hajiyev, chief foreign policy adviser to the Azerbaijani president.

Syria is viewed as a potential flashpoint, with Israel and Turkey having a military presence. One tangible outcome of Azeri-brokered talks was the establishment last year of a military hotline in Syria, providing a rare glimmer of hope as tensions continue to mount.

“It's not unavoidable that Israel and Turkey will reach confrontation. I think we can stop this process,” argued Gallia Lindenstrauss, a specialist in Turkish foreign policy at Tel Aviv University's Institute for National Security Studies.

“They have a hotline between the Israeli Air Force and the Turkish Air Force, making sure that we will not have a collision in the skies of Syria, because we know both air forces are operating there. And the hotline has managed to keep the situation quiet. If I'm trying to find some anchor of reassurance that Turkish-Israeli relations can be controlled, it's Syria.”

As Israel approaches elections, a temporary lull in Turkish-Israeli tensions is anticipated. Still, since the main opposition shares the government’s concerns over Turkey, relations are set to remain fraught.

World.title: Serbia's LGBTQ+ community faces 'epidemic of violence'
World.content:
Documented cases of violence against LGBTQ+ people in Serbia have never been higher. The attacks are part of a larger shift in society targeting marginalized people.

Amid a slew of blows and homophobic insults, the woman on the bus lashed out at Aleksandar Savic and stabbed him with a sharp object. Later, in the emergency room, doctors treated Savic for a cut to the calf and injuries to his eye.

Incidents like the July 11 attack on Savic — also know as drag queen Alexis Plastik — don't happen often in Belgrade. But violence against people who don't look or act like the mainstream in the EU candidate country is becoming increasingly common.

Just a few hours earlier, Vladimir Arsenijevic, author and program director of the annual Krokodil Literary Festival, was attacked in central Belgrade in the middle of the day by right-wing thugs, as he was preparing for a memorial event commemorating the 1995 Srebrenica genocide.

Speaking with broadcaster N1, Plastik called out the "epidemic of violence" in Serbia. The increasing violence by groups associated with President Aleksandar Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party, SNS, has reinforced the feeling among many people that anyone who is different can become a target, and that no one is safe.

Participants in the 2023 Pride parade in Belgrade were confronted by anti-gay protesters and a heavy police presence Image: Marko Drobnjakovic/AP Photo/picture alliance

"Violence is becoming increasingly normal, while protection against it is anything but guaranteed — especially for those who speak out against social or political problems, or who are unpopular with the general public," said Matija Stefanovic, the program coordinator for the LGBTQ+ group Da se Zna! ("For Your Information!"), which documents violence against queer people in Serbia.

"The fact that most of these attacks aren't investigated and that the perpetrators are rarely held accountable means they can't be dismissed as isolated incidents," said Stefanovic. "They represent a systemic problem that further stokes violence and emboldens perpetrators to continue attacking marginalized people, without having to fear significant consequences."

The social climate has become decidedly harsher for Serbia's LGBTQ+ community over the last few years, with the community also increasingly the target of right-wing nationalist government.

More recorded attacks than ever before

Da se Zna! is based in an unassuming office on a side street in the center of the Serbian capital. Aside from a lone rainbow-colored nutcracker standing on a shelf, hardly anything indicates the group's purpose: it's the only organization in Serbia to document attacks on queer people — threats, vandalism, physical assault.

Not much in the offices of Da se Zna! indicates the group's purpose Image: Tobias Zuttmann/DW

"Last year, we counted 110 cases — more than ever before," said Stefanovic. That's due in part to the fact that the NGO is becoming more well-known, and queer people are increasingly ready to report incidents. But dramatic, high-profile cases like the aggression against Alexis Plastik are also happening more and more.

In mid-May, unknown assailants attacked Mornar, a queer bar in Belgrade, with tear gas. At the end of May, a trans woman and her partner were beaten unconscious one night — again, by unidentified attackers.

Many queer people in Serbia are scared of openly showing their identity. In a recent survey by the European Union Agency for Fundamental Rights, some 80% of respondents said they avoided holding the hand of their partner in public.

The latest edition of the Rainbow Map , compiled by the International Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans and Intersex Association, shows that Serbia has slipped to 29th place in Europe, six spots below the European average. Five years ago, it was in 22nd place.

Support amid threats of violence

The only solution to this stigmatization and violence is education, said Stefanovic. Next to the yearly Pride parade co-organized by Da se Zna!, activists also travel to small towns around the country with a Pride Caravan to send a message: we're here, and we're not going anywhere.

In some of the towns, they're greeted by a handful of supporters holding rainbow flags — and dozens of demonstrators shouting homophobic slogans.

LGBTQ+ activist in Serbia: 'I was abused by the police' To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

After the group published a list of the planned destinations for this year's caravan, they received several death threats. The event in Pirot, in Serbia's southeast, was called off on short notice in mid-July because police could not guarantee the group's safety. Three journalists covering the event were attacked by the mob.

"These protests show the sad reality for queer people living in a small Serbian town," said Stefanovic. "We try to show the people living in these towns that we know how hard it is — and that we haven't forgotten about them."

Struggle to live openly in a small town

Stefanovic knows exactly how it feels to grow up queer in a small town far from the cosmopolitan city of Belgrade.

"I wanted to be a boy for as long as I can remember. Every night I prayed to God that he would turn me into one," he told DW.

Only when Stefanovic moved to Belgrade for his studies did he feel free to openly live as a man Image: Tobias Zuttmann/DW

Only as a teenager did Stefanovic learn about other people that felt like him — and that they were known as trans. But this knowledge did nothing to ease his worries.

"Once I realized [who I was,] I felt the weight of everything I would have to go through as a result," he said.

It was only when Stefanovic moved to Belgrade for his studies that he felt free enough to openly live as Matija. He came out as trans, first to several professors at the university, then to friends. Finally, one day, he wrote to his parents, an eight-page letter in which he explained everything that had preoccupied him for years.

Stefanovic then made two life-changing decisions: he began hormone treatment to align his biological sex with his gender identity — and he did so openly. At the time, there were very few people living openly as trans in Serbia, and not much information was available on how to undergo gender-affirming treatment.

"It sounds totally cliche, but I wanted to become the person that I needed in my life when I first exploring my own gender identify," said Stefanovic. He filmed his transition, first putting his videos on YouTube and then on TikTok.

TV interviews followed soon after — and the attention of right-wing groups on Facebook. At first, the hate directed toward Stefanovic seemed unbearable. But he decided to keep going, to stay visible, so that trans people would someday belong.

Stefanovic knows that acceptance is a process, and that people can change their views. His family is a prime example — his conservative father was the first person to consistently use the right pronoun and new name. And last year, both his parents took part in Belgrade's Pride parade for the first time.

"I'm so proud of them," said Stefanovic. "My parents have become my greatest allies."

World.title: Europe wildfires rage on, forcing more than 250,000 from homes
World.content:
From the outskirts of Bordeaux to communities near Madrid, fast-moving wildfires in France and Spain are driving mass evacuations, destroying homes, and claiming lives.

As wildfires continue to engulf massive stretches of western France and central Spain, more than 250,000 people have been forced to flee, with flames devouring forests and homes near Bordeaux and Madrid.

Firefighters have said that the blazes, the largest recorded in both countries in recent years, are so massive that they cannot be tackled head on.

Record wildfires in Spain, France force thousands to flee To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Man killed in wildfire near Valencia

The Spanish Interior Ministry said Saturday that a man was killed in a wildfire in the town of Manises, near Valencia.

Local authorities said firefighters managed to bring the blaze in Manises under control but "unfortunately the fire has claimed the life of one person." The body was found in a car in a ravine.

Two French firefighters died earlier this week near Bordeaux and one in Sicily, Italy, which is now also battling blazes.

Wildfires have forced the evacuation of some 250,000 people in southwestern France and central Spain Image: Violeta Santos Moura/REUTERS

On France's Atlantic coast, 44,000 people were removed from the Cap Ferret peninsula, many by boat.

Towns near Bordeaux, the famed winemaking town popular with tourists, were evacuated "as a precaution" as strong winds fueled approaching flames.

On Saturday morning, regional authorities further ordered the evacuation of three of the city's western suburbs "to ensure residents' safety."

In all, French authorities say more than 197,000 people have been evacuated in France's western Gironde and Landes departments.

In Spain, the Interior Ministry said 70,000 have been forced to flee.

Wildfires in southern Europe cause mass evacuations To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

EU sending firefighting aircraft to France and Spain

Authorities in France say the country's two main blazes were sparked accidentally, however, as summers become drier and hotter the magnitude of such fires has increased exponentially.

French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, who said the government would do everything possible to protect citizens, warned that a wind shift had transformed the Cap Ferret blaze into "a large, self-sustaining fire that is extremely difficult to bring under control."

"It is now moving east, toward the Bordeaux metropolitan area," added Nunez, who pledged, "We are going to reorganize our response so we can fight it from the ground and prevent it from advancing toward Bordeaux."

Heat waves fuel wildfires across southern Europe To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

French President Emmanuel Macron called for European Union assistance on Friday as well as the mobilization of the French army to halt fires that have so far destroyed 22,000 hectares (54,000 acres) of land.

The European Commission announced that it is sending three firefighting aircraft to France and four to Spain in an effort to gain the upper hand.

This week's fires have injured dozens of firefighters and killed three of them — two in western France and one in Sicily, Italy, which is now also battling blazes.

The Tour de France has been shortened and will be effectively limited to Paris on Sunday because emergency services are needed to deal with wildfires in the country.

Spain declares national emergency

In Spain, the government has declared a national emergency as two of the country's three current fires, all burning near the capital Madrid, merge into one.

Madrid's regional emergency management services said the massive blaze has now reached "its peak and is currently beyond the capacity of firefighters to contain."

The largest active fire in the region, in Guadalajara province, has already laid waste to some 32,000 hectares.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez visited affected areas west of the capital on Saturday and stressed that the priority was "to save lives," as temperatures in the region topped 37 degrees Celsius (98.6 Fahrenheit).

NASA abandons comms facility amid Spain's summer of fire

The US space agency NASA on Saturday reported that it had been forced to evacuate its Madrid Deep Space Communications Complex (MDSCC), which is located in the region. The facility is one of three worldwide that allow the agency to communicate with spacecraft in distant parts of the galaxy — the others are located in Australia and the US.

"The safety and well being of our personnel is our highest priority and our thoughts are with the families and neighbors who are also experiencing the impact of the wildfires in the surrounding communities," said a statement released by the agency.

Wildfires raging near the Spanish capital Madrid forced the evacuation of a NASA deep space communications center Image: Gabri Solera/Europa Press/IMAGO

Spain, which regularly sees wildfires, has experienced an especially devastating summer. Earlier this month, fires in the south of the country killed 13 people.

Environmental officials say that 1,140 square kilometers (440 square miles) have already been lost to flames this year, more than five times the area burnt throughout the first half of 2025.

Edited by: Kieran Burke and Rana Taha
