World.title: Lenacapavir will slow HIV infections if there's enough of it and it reaches at-risk groups
World.content:
Lenacapavir is one injection, twice a year. It's a big improvement for people in high-risk groups, currently taking a pill a day against HIV infection. But its long-term impact depends on it reaching those very people.

For a healthy young woman in South Africa, the greatest risk of HIV may come from someone she wants to trust, but can't.

She may not know her partner's HIV status, may not always be able to insist they use a condom, and may have little control over whether he has other partners.

There is an option: Daily Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) pills keep antiretroviral drugs in the body at high enough levels to stop HIV before it can establish an infection.

But PrEP only works if she keeps taking the medication. Miss too many doses and drug levels can fall too low to provide sufficient protection.

She may forget, resent having to take a daily pill, or fear that a partner or relative will find the medication, causing stigma. She may also experience side effects from PrEP or struggle to obtain new supplies.

Zimbabwe takes a big shot toward an HIV-free future To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

How can lenacapavir help?

Taking medication consistently — known as adherence — is a challenge for people with conditions like hypertension and diabetes. With PrEP, however, the difficulty is even greater.

"You're asking people who are healthy, who don't have any illness, to take a tablet every day," said Salim Abdool Karim, director and co-founder of the Centre for the AIDS Programme of Research in South Africa. "That's a high bar."

"Repeated studies, including our own, show that patients who start taking PrEP, by month three, about half of them have given it up. By the end of the year, you're left with only a handful that are still taking PrEP," Abdool Karim told DW.

Lenacapavir sharply reduces that daily burden: It requires just one injection every six months.

"That's infinitely easier to do than to remember to take a tablet every day," he said. "For those who receive the injection every six months without fail, it works superbly because adherence is effectively complete."

But lenacapavir is still too expensive in some regions and access is low.

How does lenacapavir last so long in the body?

Most established PrEP drugs block enzymes that allow the virus to reproduce and spread — it uses the enzymes to copy its own genetic material and insert it into a human cell's DNA.

Lenacapavir works completely differently. It is the first PrEP drug to target the capsid, a cone-shaped shell that surrounds the viral genetic material. But the capsid is also essential to the virus' replication process, and therefore a promising target.

Lenacapavir attacks the capsid of HIV, shown in green because they are vital for the virus' ability to replicate and spread in the body Image: Cavallini James/BSIP/picture alliance

"[Lenacapavir] is the most potent molecule we know of against HIV," Wesley Sundquist, a University of Utah biochemist and leading expert on the HIV capsid, told DW.

Sundquist said lenacapavir remains effective over long periods and that it is potent even at low concentrations.

"It sets up a little depot that slowly dissolves," said Sundquist.

Which groups would benefit from lenacapavir?

Abdool Karim pointed to three groups where HIV incidence remains stubbornly high and greater PrEP uptake is urgently needed:

Adolescent girls and young women in parts of Africa

Younger gay men in the West

Vulnerable gay communities in Eastern Europe and Central Asia

In South Africa, a rollout for people at risk began in June 2026, backed by a July 2025 agreement between the drug's developer, Gilead, and a public-private financing organization called the Global Fund.

Gilead agreed to supply lenacapavir at no profit to up to 2 million people over three years.

Earlier, in October 2024, Gilead also agreed to allow the production of cheaper, generic versions of the drug in 120 resource-limited countries, where HIV infection rates are high.

But some countries still lack access to the drug.

Latin American countries excluded from lenacapavir deals

Melissa Scharwey of Doctors Without Borders said some Latin American countries, including Brazil, Mexico, Peru and Argentina have been excluded from recent rollouts of lenacapavir, despite having participated in clinical trials.

Even within eligible countries, vulnerable groups may still be missed, Scharwey told DW.

"There's by far not enough of it," said Scharwey, calling on Gilead to increase supply and sell directly to MSF at an affordable price of around $40 per shot.

The decisive question in driving down HIV, according to University of Washington epidemiologist Monisha Sharma, is whether the drug reaches the people and places where HIV is spreading most rapidly.

"In our modeling of South Africa, Zimbabwe, and western Kenya, providing lenacapavir to approximately 2–4% of the adult population, with targeted uptake among people at greatest risk, averted approximately 12–18% of new infections over ten years," Sharma told DW.

Is injectable HIV medication really a 'silver bullet'? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Lenacapavir 'unlikely to eliminate HIV on its own'

"Lenacapavir could substantially accelerate progress toward lowering incidence, but it is unlikely to eliminate HIV transmission on its own," said Sharma.

"This impact is highly dependent on affordable lenacapavir drug prices, efficient distribution channels, and targeted uptake among people with the highest HIV risk," she added.

That final condition is what gives Abdool Karim his greatest concern. Lenacapavir can largely solve the adherence problem for people who receive it. It cannot solve the harder problem confronting HIV specialists: identifying and reaching those in greatest danger.

"The problem is that those at highest risk need to come forward to take the medication. And often those at the highest risk don't see themselves at risk. That's why they're at risk," said Abdool Karim. "If we cannot reach those at highest risk, then we're not going to make a dent in this epidemic in the manner in which we were hoping."

Edited by: Zulfikar Abbany

World.title: Tour de France final stage shortened due to wildfires
World.content:
Security personnel assigned to the race have been redeployed to help contain major blazes near Bordeaux, reducing Sunday's final stage.

Sunday's final stage of the Tour de France will be shorter than planned because security forces have been redirected to help fight wildfires near Bordeaux, organizers and police said Saturday.

"In a spirit of national solidarity with the areas and communities affected, it was decided to adapt the route for the final stage from Thoiry to Paris," the Paris police and the event's organizers said in a joint statement.

Slovenian four-time champion Tadej Pogacar has all but sealed victory in the world-famous cycling race and only needs to finish Saturday's stage to secure a fifth Tour title in seven years.

Final stage shortened to 89 kilometers

The route for Stage 21 has been shortened to 89 kilometers (55 miles), down from the 133 kilometers originally planned.

It was set to begin east of Paris in Thoiry but will now start with two laps on the Champs-Elysees.

Riders will then race the circuit before finishing on the Champs-Elysees as usual.

The team presentation will still be held in Thoiry before riders are taken to Paris by bus.

The Tour first introduced the Montmartre loop to its final stage in 2025 [FILE: July 27, 2025] Image: Loic Venance/AFP/Getty Images

"The Paris police prefect and the Tour de France director salute the commitment of all the actors mobilized in the fight against the fires and express their full solidarity with the affected populations," the statement said.

Wildfires near Arcachon Bay, near Bordeaux in Gironde, and around Biscarrosse in Landes have destroyed more than 36,000 hectares of forest and forced nearly 200,000 people to evacuate.

Edited by: Rana Taha

World.title: Dozens dead after buses collide in eastern Syria
World.content:
The crash on a route notorious for deadly accidents prompted a large-scale rescue operation.

At least 35 people were killed and 30 others were injured when two buses collided in eastern Syria.

The crash happened on Saturday on a highway linking Damascus with Deir al-Zour province.

What else do we know about the crash?

The Interior Ministry said one bus was carrying security personnel, while the other was carrying civilians.

State television footage showed one of the vehicles engulfed in flames after the impact.

Military helicopters were dispatched to the site to help in medical evacuations Image: SANA/AFP

Military helicopters were sent to the scene to help evacuate the injured and recover the bodies.

The cause of the crash remains unknown.

The route is widely known as the "road of death" because of its frequent and often deadly accidents.

World.title: Germany news: Industry hemorrhaging 15,000 jobs a month
World.content:
07/24/2026 July 24, 2026 Foreign Minister Wadephul draws international law and traffic offense analogy in satire show interview

The show airs as Wadephul returns from a trip to Africa this week Image: Soeren Stache/dpa/picture alliance

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has taken the bold but risky move of appearing in a feature interview on public television's premiere weekly satirical comedy the "heute-show," roughly like the US "Daily Show."

Wadephul speaks at some length to young anchor Fabian Köster in an elevator in a playful interview that's nevertheless focused on entirely serious topics. It spans NATO relations and Donald Trump and Greenland, Russia's war against Ukraine, the low popularity of government he serves in, the war in Iran and Nicolas Maduro's abduction from Venezuela.

"We're not conducting some kind of foreign policy interview here," Wadephul said at one point with a chuckle after a trickier question, only for Köster to immediately reply "doch!" or roughly "oh, but we are!"

When the topic turned to the US military operation to kidnap Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, Wadephul was asked whether "international law can rub up against the boundaries of Realpolitik."

"Yes, if you're honest, yes, that's the case," Wadephul said. "But to be honest, we're familiar with this in the rule of law. If you think of yourself in road traffic, for instance, have you always kept to everything 100%?"

Köster said he liked the analogy but noted that "a stop sign is something slightly different" than the abduction of a head of state.

"In the law it's written that you can't drive faster than 50 km/h in a built-up area, but nevertheless sometimes people drive faster. And it's the same, fundamentally, in international law. And you have to deal with that. The laws are there to provide an orientation, but they are never dogmatically upheld 100%," Wadephul said.

Asked whether it was "embarrassing" for Germany to only speak up against breaches of international law if "the right countries" are offenders, Wadephul said it was important to note that there were gradations of color.

"There are differences," he said. "If you, like [Russian President Vladimir] Putin, have been waging five years of war against Ukraine and killing thousands upon thousands of people — including your own people — or if you took this one step against a person in power in Venezuela, who did not exactly keep to international law himself: There really is a difference."

Chancellor Friedrich Merz had faced criticism amid the US operations in both Venezuela and Iran for comments suggesting the situations were "complex." Wadephul expanded on this saying they were politically complex but perhaps simpler from a purely legal perspective, still without explicitly saying they were breaches of the law.

The show airs on Friday evening .

World.title: Could 'mesh networks' help overcome authoritarians' internet blocks?
World.content:
In authoritarian countries, the state is often either monitoring online communications or has the ability to shut them down in a political crisis. But there are other ways that activists can keep in touch.

Iran, January 2026: During some of the country's largest protests in decades, the Iranian government shut down the internet.

US-based internet monitor, IODA — short for Internet Outage Detection and Analysis — registered almost no data traffic at all and US internet infrastructure analyst Doug Madory described it as "one of the largest government-directed communication shutdowns in history."

During that time, the Iranian government killed and arrested thousands of people but to this day, nobody knows exactly how many. Estimates of the death toll have been anywhere between 7,000 and 40,000, though many observers suspect its closer to the higher number. The lack of clarity is partially because the internet blackout meant that communication with the outside world was all but impossible.

The Iranian government's behavior is not unusual. In Russia, Belarus, Myanmar and Sudan, particularly when governments fear resistance, the internet has become a weapon — because those who cannot communicate cannot organize.

Radio-powered networks

One solution for these sorts of communications crises could be what is known as a "LoRa mesh network."

Mobile phones may not function if the system overloads in crises or concerts; mesh networks don't overload like that Image: Laurent Zabulon/ABACA/picture alliance

LoRa, which is short for "long range," is based on a simple principle invented for industrial purposes. Small radio modules, also known as LoRa transmitters, have regularly been embedded into physical silicon chips that are used for industrial devices that connect to the internet, things such as smoke alarms, smart water or power meters and environmental sensors — basically any device that requires long battery life and long-range data transmission but only for small amounts of data.

To transmit information, these devices use license-free radio frequencies of the sort available for civilian use, the same frequencies used by weather stations and garage door openers.

To form an internet-free communications network, users first need to purchase a transmitting device that uses LoRa; these can cost anything from about €30 ($35) to €80 ($91). Then users can connect their phone to the device using special software.

The LoRa devices transmit encrypted data packets over a distance of several kilometers. Each device automatically forwards messages to the next one, like a baton being passed through a crowd. If any single device fails, the message finds the next nearby device, via a different route. This means the communications network that is formed can repair itself.

The result of all of the above is what is known as a "LoRa mesh network."

The different transmitting devices are called "nodes" in the network and because there is no central node, there's no way the communications network can be shut down. The radio modules can be kept hidden and powered either by batteries or a small solar panel.

Iran reconnects — but can everyone browse freely? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Only smaller messages, no pictures

The major disadvantage of a network like this is that, unlike the ordinary internet, users can only exchange smaller messages, with a maximum size of around 237 bytes, equivalent to a short text message.

On the other hand, the less data transmitted, the longer the distance it can travel, the less power it consumes, and the less likelihood the radio transmission could be tracked.

Two of the best-known platforms that enable this type of communication are Meshtastic and MeshCore, both of which are free to use and open source.

Both place emphasis on data protection. The transmitting devices merely forward messages and cannot read the content. Third parties, including the police or government agencies, cannot intercept the messages either.

MeshCore's motto is "your communications, your keys, your control."

That the concept works, even under extreme conditions, has been demonstrated by users in Ukraine. Meshtastic-UA offers a real-time network map that shows active nodes throughout the country; there are a lot of nodes near the front lines.

MeshCore has a similar map showing the global distribution of nodes. But there are also many other users who conceal their locations.

This MeshCore map lists the locations of mesh nodes Image: meshcore.co.uk

It's not possible to censor information sent on LoRa mesh networks. When governments halt the internet, they do things like block internet addresses and domains, scrutinize data packets and legally compel providers to cooperate.

For example, Russian security agencies require locally operating telecommunications companies to grant them direct access to communications data. Those who don't comply lose their license. This works mainly if communication takes place over the internet.

That is something that doesn't happen with LoRa mesh networks. The messages travel via radio waves, bypassing firewalls and surveillance systems.

Mesh networks imperfect

There are still risks to this kind of communication, however. For one thing, transmitters can be tracked as encryption protects the content of a message, but not the sender's location. Authorities with the right equipment can triangulate the radio signals, meaning they can physically locate the transmitter to within a certain distance.

Additionally, in some countries, operating unauthorized radio equipment is a criminal offense. In Iran or Russia, being found to be in possession of such devices can have serious legal consequences.

Starlink and the fight for Internet access in Iran To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

With any other mesh network — such as those that use mobile phones as transmitters — a LoRa mesh network can only work if enough people participate. If there are not enough nodes, then the distance messages can travel is limited. Building up a network like this takes time, something that isn't possible in crisis situations.

It is unclear whether anti-government activists in authoritarian states are using LoRa mesh networks at all. For good reason, anyone taking part in such a network would prefer not to reveal it.

However Ukraine has demonstrated that the concept can work in the real world. The hardware and required software is freely available worldwide and the technology is mature enough that even people without a lot of technical expertise can set it up themselves .

In a world where more and more governments are using the internet as an instrument of power, and where companies such as Apple are increasingly subject to government pressure, what options are left for safe communication? A network of small radio modules could be the answer for some.

This story was originally published in German.

World.title: Niger still seeking stability after 3 years of military rule
World.content:
The military government in Niger promised social, security, and economic improvements when it took power in 2023. Three years down the line, there are mixed reviews on its performance.

The military seized power in Niger on July 26, 2023. General Abdourahamane Tchiani , who became head of state, justified the coup by citing the poor security situation, which he said persisted despite international support.

In the weeks that followed, the military government announced a transitional period that was to last a maximum of three years.

However, the political promises made upon taking office have not been fulfilled. The transitional government continues to hold all the reins of power, and the security situation in the Sahel country remains fragile.

In the Tillabery region in southwestern Niger, attacks by jihadists are on the rise. Thousands of people have been forced to flee their villages, plunging the region into a severe humanitarian crisis.

Niger's military government has struggled to end an Islamist insurgency despite promises to do so Image: Ludovic Marin/AFP/Getty Images

"Today, attacks on the armed forces and the civilian population are significantly more frequent and violent than they were three years ago," Maiga, who lives in the city of Tera, which has a population of 30,000, told DW. Maiga wished to remain anonymous for security reasons.

"Life used to be better despite the insecurity; the weekly markets operated normally and supplies arrived regularly," he said, adding that at the moment entire villages had fled and schools are closed.

The independent conflict monitor ACLED has also said the the security situation has deteriorated since the 2023 coup.

According to the organization, the Tillaberi region remains the main hot spot for clashes between two rival Islamist groups, Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin and the so-called Islamic State in the Sahel Province (formerly ISGS). This rivalry has resulted in numerous casualties among soldiers and civilians.

In 2025, nearly 1,200 deaths were recorded in the region. For Heni Nsaibia, a staff member at ACLED, these figures attest to the scale of the security crisis affecting Niger.

The most recent major attack, on July 17, claimed the lives of at least 16 soldiers and 15 terrorists, according to Niger's state media, ANP.

"The situation in Niger has worsened, particularly in the Tillaberi region, where the death toll is the highest in the central Sahel," Nsaibia told DW.

Insecurity taking a toll on civilians

"We live in makeshift shelters and are defenseless against the elements; we take on small odd jobs to survive," a woman told DW.

"I used to be able to live with dignity from my work, but right now it's very difficult; even drinking water is a problem for us," added a local herder.

Young Nigeriens are torn between disappointment and optimism: In the youth assemblies, known as "Fadas," the topic continues to spark discussion. Some — like Fadila — believe that the situation is gradually stabilizing after the turmoil of the first few years.

There was much optimism in Niger after the military took over power three years ago Image: AFP/Getty Images

"For a while, it wasn't easy at all: Salaries weren't paid on time, food supplies… that wasn't easy. But for some time now, things have been going pretty well overall," Fadila told DW.

General Tchiani has emphasized that young people can once again participate in politics. "Before the coup, young people were excluded from decision-making bodies." But in the meantime, he said, an advisory commission has been established that includes young people. "So that means the concerns of young people are now being taken into account in decision-making bodies."

Just two days after the ouster of President Mohamed Bazoumin 2023, junta leader Tchiani announced plans to combat corruption and boost the economy.

But three years later, the people of Niger are no better off, noted Tahirou Garka, a close ally of Bazoum, and spokesperson for the G25, a movement advocating for a return to constitutional order in Niger.

"They have failed economically and socially," he said, referring to the military government. "People are struggling to find drinking water; there is no water, no electricity, no fuel."

What is the Alliance of Democrats for the Sahel? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

However, Hamani Oumarou of LASDEL, a social sciences research institute based in Niamey, takes a different view. According to him, the socioeconomic situation has improved for a large portion of Niger's population, especially for those who are not part of the middle class or the elite.

"Households with low incomes have more money left over to feed their families," Oumarou told DW. However, Niger is also forced to import food at certain times of the year, which leads to a sharp rise in prices.

Rebuilding ties with ECOWAS

Along with Mali and Burkina Faso, Niger is a founding member of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), formed in 2023 after all three countries withdrew from the West African regional organization ECOWAS.

The AES has distanced itself from Western partners and is seeking closer ties with Russia.

Pape Ibrahima Kane, an expert on international organizations, now hopes for a rapprochement between the AES member states and their longtime allies in West Africa.

The military leaders of the Sahel Alliance support one another militarily and economically, but still face political sanctions by the African Union Image: Mahamadou Hamidou/REUTERS

He sees a positive sign in the fact that former Guinean Prime Minister Lansana Kouyate was elected chief negotiator for ECOWAS a few days ago. According to Kane, Kouyate seems to have been accepted by the AES.

"We are at the beginning of a promising process, as both sides are truly on the same page when it comes to starting talks," he told DW.

For him, economic negotiations should also play a role. Niger depends on access to the port of Benin and on its electricity supply from Nigeria and Benin, both of which are ECOWAS member states.

Reliou Koubakin and Ali Abdou contributed to this article, which was originally written in German.

Correction, July 24, 2026: A previous version of this article stated that Lansana Kouyate is Guinea's current prime minister. This has been corrected.

World.title: Última hora de los incendios forestales, en directo | El Gobierno amplía la emergencia nacional por los incendios a Toledo
World.content:
El Poder Judicial evalúa las consecuencias de los incendios

El CGPJ contacta con las presidencias de los TSJ de Castilla y León y Madrid para evaluar la situación ante los por si hubiera que aprobar alguna de las medidas contempladas en el protocolo de actuación judicial en situaciones de emergencia y catástrofe. La Comisión Permanente del Consejo General del Poder Judicial permanece en contacto con la presidenta del Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Castilla y León, Ana del Ser; y con la presidenta en funciones del Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Madrid, Aurora de la Cueva, ante los incendios forestales que están afectando al territorio de estas dos Comunidades Autónomas.

El objetivo de estos contactos es evaluar la situación y valorar si procede adoptar algunas de las medidas contempladas en el Protocolo de actuación judicial en situaciones de emergencia y catástrofe, cuyo texto actualizado fue aprobado por el Pleno del CGPJ en su reunión del pasado miércoles. El Protocolo prevé medidas para asegurar la continuidad del servicio público de Justicia en estas circunstancias, ya que la intervención judicial resulta esencial tanto para la protección de las personas afectadas como para la investigación de los hechos y la exigencia de las responsabilidades que, en su caso, procedan.

Entre esas medidas figuran, entre otras, algunas relativas a las sedes judiciales cuando el acceso a las mismas sea imposible o su utilización suponga riesgo para la seguridad de las personas; la suspensión generalizada de los señalamientos y de las actuaciones programadas en el ámbito territorial afectado; o la utilización de medios electrónicos, actuaciones telemáticas y sistemas de comunicación remota que favorezcan la continuidad de la actividad jurisdiccional.

Tanto la presidenta del TSJ de Castilla y León como la presidenta en funciones del TSJ de Madrid han comunicado que, por el momento, los servicios de guardia funcionan con normalidad y que no es necesario adoptar ninguna de esas medidas de manera inmediata.

World.title: Los incendios de Madrid y Ávila afectan ya a 45.000 hectáreas y obligan a evacuar o confinar a más de 88.500 personas
World.content:
Las fuertes rachas de viento complican los trabajos de extinción de los fuegos, que no están controlados. La UME unifica el mando para coordinar la respuesta y el Gobierno amplía la emergencia nacional por los incendios a Toledo

Los incendios forestales que afectan ya a 45.000 hectáreas y han obligado a evacuar o confinar a más de 88.500 personas en la provincia de Ávila y la Comunidad de Madrid continúan este sábado activos y sin controlar. Durante la noche, han avanzado “muy poco y han bajado su intensidad”, pero preocupa el aumento del viento que se ha dado durante todo el día. El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, ha advertido de que la situación sigue siendo compleja: “No sabemos cuál va a ser la evolución del viento, pese a que las temperaturas hayan bajado”, ha señalado desde el puesto de mando avanzado en el municipio madrileño de Cenicientos (2.152 habitantes), que se ha desalojado de urgencia por el avance de las llamas y se traslada a Navalcarnero. Y la presidenta autonómica, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, ha apuntado que la situación es “totalmente inédita, nunca vista” y que puede “llevar a tener situaciones mucho peores en las próximas horas”.

Las labores de extinción han seguido “con intensidad” durante toda la noche y la madrugada, a las que se han sumado los medios aéreos esta mañana. Las llamas en Madrid no se han unido a las de Burgohondo (Ávila), que era y sigue siendo el principal temor. Aun así, ambos fuegos se tratan ya como uno solo, según ha informado la Unidad Militar de Emergencias (UME), para facilitar la coordinación. Y sobre las 19.15, el Gobierno ha anunciado que amplía la emergencia nacional por los incendios a Toledo. “Nuestra prioridad está en salvar vidas y defender los núcleos poblacionales”, ha señalado Sánchez esta mañana. El presidente ha indicado que este fin de semana, a pesar del viento, se abre “una ventana de oportunidad” para controlar los fuegos.

La secretaria general de Protección Civil y Emergencias, Virginia Barcones, también ha advertido de que el cambio de las condiciones meteorológicas previsto para la jornada es clave, como ya lo fue el viernes, y complica la evolución del fuego en Madrid. Se esperaban cambios en la dirección del viento, con rachas de hasta 60 kilómetros por hora, lo que ha obligado a adaptar la estrategia de extinción. La cabeza del incendio en Madrid se sitúa entre Robledo de Chavela y Fresnedillas de la Oliva, mientras que el fuego declarado en Ávila continúa moviéndose hacia el sur e inquieta su avance en el Valle del Tiétar, donde el Gobierno ha ordenado el desalojo de toda la zona. Allí se han intensificado los trabajos de extinción.

Ante la virulencia y complejidad de los fuegos, el Gobierno declaró el jueves la emergencia nacional en ambas comunidades y desde entonces ha asumido el control de la situación. Y la UME ha informado de que creaba un mando unificado para coordinar la respuesta entre Ávila y Madrid. Lo ha anunciado el jefe de la unidad, el teniente general Francisco Javier Marcos Izquierdo, desde el puesto de mando: el operativo dejará de trabajar “como dos sectores independientes” para actuar “como uno único”. “Es la mejor forma de gestionar y ganar tiempo”, ha apuntado el teniente general.

Hace 24 horas, debido al rápido avance de las llamas, España solicitó a Bruselas la activación del mecanismo europeo de respuesta, que ha movilizado dos aviones desde Grecia y dos desde Italia, que en principio llegaban este sábado a la península. También se desplazarán 100 efectivos del ejército de Portugal, ha detallado Sánchez desde el puesto de mando, junto al ministro del Interior, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, y la presidenta madrileña. Además, 10 comunidades autónomas han enviado recursos para hacer frente a los incendios.

01:38 Ayuso: "Es un momento muy crítico"

Más evacuaciones en Ávila y Madrid

En Ávila, donde el incendio de Burgohondo ya ha arrasado 21.000 hectáreas según Interior, se ha ordenado este sábado el desalojo de siete municipios más, que se suman a los cuatro evacuados hace 24 horas. Son: Sotillo de La Adrada, La Adrada, Piedralaves, Casavieja, Casillas, Santa María del Tiétar y Navahondilla.

En total, hay ya 11 municipios afectados, 38.000 evacuados y casi 8.000 confinados en la provincia. La zona más conflictiva de fuego sigue estando en la zona sur, el Valle del Tiétar, precisamente donde se han desalojado estas nuevas localidades, según ha detallado el delegado del Gobierno en Castilla y León, Nicanor Sen, desde el puesto de mando de la región, en Navaluenga. Los vecinos han recibido a lo largo de la mañana las alertas en sus teléfonos móviles para que abandonen sus pueblos y se dirijan a las zonas preparadas para acogerlos. “Son desalojos preventivos”, ha explicado Sen, que no ha descartado que las evacuaciones se amplíen.

Los esfuerzos se están centrando en frenar el avance del fuego en esta zona y en evitar que se unan los dos grandes frentes. El teniente coronel de la Unidad Militar de Emergencias (UME) Pablo Samaniego ha explicado desde el puesto de mando en Ávila que los incendios ya están influyendo mutuamente debido a las condiciones meteorológicas, aunque todavía no se han unido físicamente: “Trabajamos para que esa unión física no se produzca”.

La Guardia Civil informó el viernes de que había detenido a una persona e investigaba a una segunda como responsables del incendio forestal del municipio abulense de 1.269 habitantes. Según el cuerpo, ambas habrían utilizado maquinaria pesada en una zona donde estaba prohibido su uso, lo que provocó una chispa que originó el fuego.

En Madrid, los tres fuegos activos en la mañana del viernes terminaron fusionándose en un solo gran frente que arrasa la esquina suroeste de la región y ha calcinado 24.000 hectáreas a su paso. “Es el peor incendio de la historia de la Comunidad de Madrid”, dijo el viernes la presidenta autonómica. El delegado del Gobierno en la región, Francisco Martín, ha añadido este sábado que se “habla ya de un incendio único”. En la comunidad hay ya 12 municipios evacuados y cuatro confinados. Los últimos en sumarse a los desalojos son Rozas de Puerto Real (579 habitantes) y Cadalso de los Vidrios (3.372), ha avanzado el delegado. En total, ha detallado, hay 29.488 desalojados y 21.132 confinados en sus pueblos y es probable que en las próximas horas haya más avisos de evacuación, ha señalado desde el puesto de mando el Cenicientos.

Por el momento, solo se conocen los daños materiales en una de las primeras urbanizaciones que tuvieron que ser desalojadas en Madrid. Fue en la localidad de Encinar del Alberche, donde 43 casas han quedado destruidas y 286 dañadas. Es el primer y único balance provisional de destrozos causados por los fuegos.

Las labores de extinción han sido hasta ahora complicadas por un peligroso cóctel meteorológico: la llamada regla del 30-30-30, utilizada por bomberos, meteorólogos y expertos forestales. Hace referencia a los tres factores que aumentan el riesgo de que un incendio avance cada vez más rápido y se convierta en uno de nivel cinco, esto es, que supere la capacidad de extinción. Son: temperaturas de más de 30 grados, humedad relativa menor al 30% y vientos que superan los 30 kilómetros por hora. Este viernes se dieron las tres.

World.title: Hallado un hombre muerto en el incendio de un barranco de Manises (Valencia)
World.content:
El audio de esta noticia utiliza una voz sintética generada por Inteligencia Artificial y podría tener algunas inconsistencias.

Cinco personas han sido trasladadas al hospital por inhalación de humo y quemaduras como consecuencia del fuego, ya estabilizado

Un hombre ha fallecido este sábado en el incendio declarado en el barranco del Salt de l’Aigua en la localidad valenciana de Manises. El Ayuntamiento de la localidad ha confirmado la muerte en un mensaje en las redes sociales: “Lamentablemente, el incendio se ha cobrado la vida de 1 persona. El Ayuntamiento de Manises decreta dos días de luto oficial, mañana y lunes”.

Según varias informaciones, el fallecido, una persona de avanzada edad, había ido por la mañana a su huerto junto al barranco, cuando le ha sorprendido el fuego. Los profesionales de la extinción del fuego han hallado el cadáver de la víctima, que podría haber inhalado humo y no habría podido ponerse a salvo. También ha aparecido su coche calcinado.

El incendio ha arrasado sobre todo matorral y ha generado una intensa humareda visible desde Valencia (a 14 kilómetros). Se ha dado por estabilizado por la tarde.

Cinco personas han sido trasladadas al hospital por inhalación de humo y quemaduras como consecuencia del fuego, según ha informado el Centro de Información y Coordinación de Urgencias (CICU). Tres han recibido ya el alta y dos permanecen en observación, según las mismas fuentes.

Dos medios aéreos y nueve dotaciones de bomberos han trabajado para sofocar este fuego, declarado sobre las 12:45 horas en un área de vegetación del barranco del Salt de l’Aigua de Manises (Valencia), según el Consorcio Provincial de Bomberos de Valencia.

Al lugar del fuego se han desplazado seis dotaciones de bomberos, dos BRIFO, un sargento, un coordinador forestal y un oficial del Consorcio. Además, ha acudido también una unidad de bomberos forestales y dos medios aéreos de la Generalitat. En total, al lugar del fuego se han trasladado tres ambulancias de Soporte Vital Básico (SVB) y otras dos de Transporte Urgente, según el CICU.

World.title: ¿Cuántas hectáreas han ardido? El mapa de los incendios activos más graves
World.content:
En las últimas dos semanas se han iniciado en España {{fires_2weeks}} incendios, {{bigfires_2weeks}} de ellos han sido grandes incendios forestales de más de 500 hectáreas. Eso indican los datos provisionales del Sistema de información europeo de incendios forestales (EFFIS) que miden la extensión de los fuegos a partir de imágenes satelitales.

En el siguiente mapa mostramos dos cosas: los polígonos que actualiza EFFIS y otros estimados por EL PAÍS a partir de los puntos de calor que detectan los satélites. Usamos estos puntos para clasificar los incendios: cuando hay puntos de las últimas 24 horas sobre un incendio o sus inmediaciones se ven en rojo ( activo 24 horas ); cuando son de las últimas 48, pasan a naranja ( 48 horas ). Así, un incendio con polígono rojo y muchos puntos rojos será activo y reciente.

Cargando En el mapa se muestran los incendios activos en las últimas 48 horas y los puntos de calor recogidos por distintos satélites: 24 h 48 h. Más incendios graves Desde mayo Cargando incendios activos...

La información de puntos de calor activos la recopilan cinco satélites de la NASA que detectan focos de temperaturas anómalas mediante sensores térmicos. Para determinar el perímetro del incendio usamos los datos del programa europeo EFFIS, basado en fotografías satelitales: mide el área quemada casi tiempo real, por lo que ofrece cifras provisionales y sirve para seguir la temporada al día. Sus números suelen ser algo más altos que los del Ministerio de Transición Ecológica, que ofrece la estadística oficial más precisa a partir de los partes de incendio de las comunidades autónomas, pero con semanas o meses de retraso. Ambos deben tomarse como una estimación que se consolidará al final de la temporada.

En el mapa también puede consultar las zonas de riesgo de incendios en el territorio. Este {{date_aemet}} habría peligro extremo de incendio en {{area_riesgo_extremo}}% de la superficie peninsular, según las estimaciones de Aemet.

¿Cómo está siendo la temporada?

Según los últimos datos actualizados de EFFIS, en España se han quemado {{area_ha_year}} hectáreas desde el principio de año hasta este {{today}}, por encima de la media de los últimos 20 años a estas altura de la temporada.

Ha despuntado también el número de incendios, que se sitúa ya en {{fires_year}} –sobre la media de {{fires_mean}}–, con un incremento del {{fires_summer_inc}}% desde el inicio del verano.

¿Qué está pasando en Europa?

En el conjunto de la Unión Europea, la superficie quemada asciende a {{ue_area_year}} hectareas, {{ue_aera_over_mean}} por encima de la media.

World.title: El peligroso incendio que acecha a Madrid: de quinta generación y con la regla del 30-30-30
World.content:
La extinción de los tres incendios, fusionados desde la tarde del viernes en un solo monstruo que avanza por la esquina suroeste de la región madrileña hacia el norte, se ve dificultada por un peligroso cóctel meteorológico: la conocida como regla del 30-30-30. Utilizada por bomberos, meteorólogos y expertos forestales, resume los tres factores que disparan el riesgo de que un fuego avance a ritmo de velocista y se convierta en lo que ya es este, un incendio de nivel 5 o quinta generación, es decir, que supera la capacidad de extinción: temperaturas por encima de los 30 grados, humedad relativa por debajo del 30% y rachas de viento superiores a 30 kilómetros por hora.

Más información EDITORIAL | Cuando se apaguen las brasas

Los bomberos no luchan contra las llamas, luchan contra el tiempo. En la zona del incendio, según detalla a este diario Javier Armeteros, delegado en Madrid de la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología, confluyeron el viernes dichas condiciones, las “más adversas″ a las que se puede enfrentar un bombero: 32 grados, humedad por debajo del 30% y “viento sostenido del oeste-suroeste de 30 kilómetros por hora y rachas de 50 a 60”.

La predicción para este sábado apunta a una mejora de las condiciones de temperatura y humedad, pero no las de viento. La temperatura baja a 29 grados y la humedad, en las horas centrales del día, se quedará en torno al 30%. En cuanto al viento, muy malas noticias: durante la mañana “gira hacia el noroeste y por la tarde se intensifica, con rachas que pueden superar los 50 kilómetros por hora”.

Este cambio en las condiciones meteorológicas, menos viento, mayor humedad y menos temperatura, “ha beneficiado la lucha contra los incendios forestales”, señala a primera hora de esta mañana el Ministerio del Interior, que certifica que “los incendios durante la noche han avanzado muy poco y han bajado su intensidad”. Lo importante es que el frente de Ávila no ha cruzado a Madrid, el mayor temor de todos los expertos consultados por EL PAÍS. El frente madrileño “ha avanzado menos durante la noche” que el de Ávila y su cabeza se encuentra en Robledo de Chavela y Fresnedillas de la Oliva. Pero siguen sin estar controlados ni perimetrados.

Este es, sin lugar a dudas, “el peor incendio de la historia” de la región, como certificó la presidenta de Madrid, Isabel Díaz Ayuso: 9.940 hectáreas calcinadas y subiendo. A estas horas hay más de 37.000 personas evacuadas de Chapinería, Navas del Rey, Colmenar del Arroyo, Fresnedillas de la Oliva, Robledo de Chavela, Navalagamella, Valdemaqueda, Aldea del Fresno, Zarzalejo y Peralejo, a los que se ha sumado en las últimas horas Rozas de Puerto Real, Cadalso de los Vidrios y Cenicientos, de donde tiene que evacuarse hasta el propio puesto de mando del incendio. Otros 20.000 vecinos están confinados en San Martín de Valdeiglesias, Pelayos de la Presa y Villa del Prado.

Según advierten varios profesionales consultados, no se trata de un problema de efectivos o de medios, sino de condiciones desfavorables. “Medios no faltan, pero este incendio tiene tanta virulencia y tanta fuerza que no puedes meter ni siquiera medios a trabajar”, lamenta Israel Naveso, miembro del cuerpo madrileño y portavoz del Sindicato de Bomberos, mayoritario en la región. Porque el incendio de Madrid ya es de nivel 5, que es como llaman los técnicos a un fuego que se torna inextinguible. “Pero no lo es en todo momento, depende de la orografía. A ratos baja y se abre una ventana de oportunidad y puedes intervenir, en otros es imposible, hay que dejarlo correr”, explica. A un incendio de estas características “no se le puede meter mano de ninguna forma“, concluye el sindicalista, para explicar que lo grave es que ”está cogiendo zonas de interfaz, es decir, parte forestal y parte urbana, está atravesando municipios enteros”.

A estas horas, la máxima aspiración de los bomberos es que “se mantenga el contador a cero”, es decir, que no muera nadie. “Está siendo un milagro, la verdad. Con el incendio ya fuera de la capacidad de extinción, a nosotros se nos ha dado la orden de dejar que el monte se queme, la única prioridad son las personas, los ciudadanos y nosotros mismos”, confiesa con sufrimiento e impotencia Naveso. A partir de ahí, teniendo en cuenta que el objetivo primordial es proteger la vida, “se está haciendo lo que se está pudiendo”. Así, sobre el terreno, los efectivos están “aguantando por los flancos”, pero no pueden hacer “un ataque directo a la cabeza” porque con un fuego de quinta o incluso ya de sexta generación “es ir directo a la muerte”, explica José María Bermúdez, portavoz del Cuerpo de Agentes Forestales de Madrid del sindicato CSIF.

Para los equipos de extinción en Madrid y Ávila, supone la peor crisis a la que se han tenido que enfrentar con mucha diferencia, según las fuentes, que alertan de una posible “catástrofe” si las condiciones no cambian y si acaban uniéndose el incendio de Ávila y el de Madrid porque el primero es “el que más carga de fuego trae y el que más hectáreas se está quemando”, explica Naveso. Como ocurra, “se va a quemar media Comunidad de Madrid”.

Es tan grave la situación que “todo el mundo, mayoritariamente, está renunciando a sus vacaciones para incorporarse a trabajar, para poder dar relevos a las dotaciones”, se felicita Naveso. “Nos estamos dejando el alma porque es muy duro lo que está pasando”, dice por teléfono, con la voz entrecortada.

Para Naveso, la causa es “una tormenta perfecta de muchas circunstancias distintas en las que se han dado todas a la vez”. El primer ingrediente para amasar este desastre es la dejación de funciones de las administraciones respecto al campo: “Es muy evidente que el Gobierno madrileño no está invirtiendo lo necesario en el mantenimiento y la limpieza de sus montes”. Ayuso tildó el jueves de “verdadero problema de los españoles” la falta de limpieza de los montes como si fuera un asunto de otros y no competencia de los gobiernos regionales.

Porque la falta de limpieza de los montes tiene un doble efecto letal: deja las pistas impracticables, lo que impide el acceso al foco de las llamas, y convierte en combustible para las llamas unos pastos tan crecidos. Si a esta falta de limpieza “se suma a todo lo que ha llovido durante el invierno, que ha provocado que crezca mucho el pasto, y se junta ahora con tres olas de calor en seis semanas, que se han chupado toda la humedad que había y han secado los pastos, y si a una chispa le sumas el viento, pues se dan las condiciones perfectas para que haya varios incendios simultáneos”.

Una de las claves es la vegetación seca, que favorece la rápida expansión de las llamas. Como el calor no desciende por las noches, no da tiempo a que la madera absorba la humedad y el agua, convirtiéndola en más propensa a arder. Esa velocidad frustra a los bomberos forestales. Este cuerpo lleva años advirtiendo de que cada vez es más difícil contener los conatos de incendio, es decir, los fuegos que queman menos de una hectárea gracias a una rápida reacción. Dicen que llegan a las llamas con la misma rapidez, pero ya es demasiado tarde. “Solemos tardar 30 o 45 minutos, como siempre, pero vemos que el incendio ya se ha extendido”, dice Guillermo Ruiz, bombero forestal.

A juicio del forestal Bermúdez, estamos ante un “panorama inédito”, tanto por la confluencia de tantos grandes incendios como por la declaración de emergencia nacional. “Anoche lo vimos como una jugada exagerada y con perfil político, pero ahora, viendo los mapas, tiene una justificación técnica. Los técnicos vieron lo que venía de Ávila y se asustaron. Es un incendio de una velocidad y voracidad increíbles, se ha recorrido la sierra de Gredos en dos días”, contextualiza.

Para evitar que estas situaciones se repitan verano tras verano y sean cada vez peores son fundamentales las inversiones. ”Está bien que se hagan en medios de extinción, pero lo que estamos repitiendo todos los profesionales es que necesitamos que lleguen al sector forestal, al agente forestal, a los bomberos forestales, a las cuadrillas que limpian los montes”, reclama Bermúdez. “Todos los veranos cuando viene el lobo lo repetimos, parece que por fin se ha creado conciencia social, pero llega octubre y se acabó y en vez de haber 10 cuadrillas limpiando pistas, hay una”, reclama el agente forestal.

World.title: Datos | Pocos incendios pero grandes y rápidos: julio deja ya una de las peores quincenas en más de 40 años
World.content:
Las dos últimas semanas de julio son la cuarta peor racha en grandes incendios desde 1983. España tiene hoy la mitad de grandes incendios que hace 40 años, pero cada uno es, de media, más del doble de grande.

En las últimas dos semanas la curva de hectáreas quemadas en España ha dado un salto brusco. No lo han provocado incendios repartidos por toda la península, sino fuegos que se han expandido muy rápido y se han concentrado en zonas muy concretas.

No es una tendencia nueva, pero el final de esta semana la ha confirmado. Entre el pasado jueves y el viernes se han declarado cuatro incendios en tres provincias, todos a menos de 40 kilómetros unos de otros: Almorox (Toledo), Burgohondo (Ávila) y San Martín de Valdeiglesias y Villa del Prado (Madrid). El de Burgohondo ha quemado 8.000 hectáreas en menos de 48 horas, hasta casi unirse en un único frente con los demás.

Más información EDITORIAL | Cuando se apaguen las brasas

Que varios fuegos coincidan tan cerca los somete a las mismas condiciones —calor extremo, humedad baja y viento—, de modo que todos evolucionan de forma agresiva a la vez. “Los incendios no compiten entre sí: interactúan”, resume Ferran Dalmau, ingeniero forestal y consultor. “Por eso es recomendable que se aborden como un complejo de incendios, porque donde sí compiten es por los recursos de extinción disponibles”.

A ellos se sumaba otro fuego de estas mismas dos semanas: el de La Mierla, en Guadalajara, estabilizado hace cinco días. Fue uno solo, pero se expandió tan rápido y sobre un territorio tan amplio que, a falta de datos definitivos, todo apunta a que figurará entre los mayores registrados en España.

Estos fuegos han elevado el balance de la quincena por encima de las 72.000 hectáreas quemadas en grandes incendios forestales, los de más de 500 hectáreas. Esos catorce días, del 9 al 22 de julio, son la cuarta peor quincena desde 1983, primer año de la estadística oficial con datos comparables. Y esas 72.000 hectáreas superan por sí solas el total anual de 31 de los 43 años de los que hay datos.

Encabezan esa lista años que acabaron con cifras récord: 2025, con los incendios de agosto en el noroeste (Zamora, Ourense y León); 1994, con los de julio en el este (Valencia, Aragón y Castilla-La Mancha), y 2022, con el de la Sierra de la Culebra, en Zamora.

El siguiente gráfico muestra la rapidez con la que los fuegos de los últimos días han disparado la estadística: el salto que dibuja la línea de 2026 representa esas 72.000 hectáreas, y solo un puñado de años registra un salto tan brusco.

No es algo nuevo. El verano pasado fue extremo en la misma línea, con una gran concentración de fuego en pocos días: el 89% de todo lo que ardió en 2025 (359.771 hectáreas) se quemó en una sola quincena, del 8 al 21 de agosto (320.060 hectáreas). Esas dos semanas quemaron más que el total anual de cualquier otro año de la serie histórica, con la única excepción de 1994.

Los años con más superficie quemada se reparten por toda la serie: 2025, 1994, 2022, 1985, 1991 y 2012. Pero llegan a ser los peores por dos vías distintas: unos, como 1985, acumulando muchísimos incendios medianos; otros, como 2025, con pocos incendios pero gigantes, de más de 5.000 hectáreas de media.

Lo que distingue a los dos grupos es el tamaño de cada fuego. Así lo muestra el siguiente gráfico: el tamaño medio de los incendios ha ido aumentando a lo largo de la serie histórica, construida uniendo la estadística del Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica (1983-2022) con los datos satelitales del programa europeo Copernicus (2023-2026). La tendencia hacia incendios medios más grandes ya se aprecia con los datos del Ministerio, procedentes de las comunidades autónomas, y se confirma con los datos satelitales, más recientes y precisos.

Este patrón confirma algo que los expertos alertan desde hace una década: no tanto más incendios en total, sino fuegos más concentrados, de expansión más rápida y más explosivos. En los años ochenta y noventa ardían unos 50 grandes incendios al año; entre 2010 y 2025, unos 26. España tiene hoy la mitad de grandes incendios que hace 40 años, pero cada uno es, de media, más del doble de grande.

El fuego de La Mierla, con alrededor de 35.000 hectáreas quemadas, ha sido el que más ha disparado los registros este año. La zona afectada se extiende a lo largo de más de 40 kilómetros y abarca 20.000 hectáreas del Parque Natural de la Sierra Norte de Guadalajara.

Si su rapidez ha situado estas semanas entre las peores desde que hay registros, su extensión lo sitúa entre los incendios más grandes jamás medidos en España. Entre los de los últimos diez años, todos medidos por satélite, ocuparía el tercer puesto, a falta de datos definitivos. Comparado con toda la serie histórica, es probable que se sitúe entre los cinco primeros, por delante de las 29.000 hectáreas del incendio de Minas de Riotinto y Berrocal (Huelva y Sevilla, 2004), aunque habrá que esperar a los datos definitivos para confirmarlo.

La concentración de incendios que se vive este año fue aún más devastador el año pasado. En 2025 el fuego se concentró en una sola semana de agosto: entre el 8 y el 17, solo en la provincia de Ourense se declararon una decena de grandes incendios —Manzaneda, A Mezquita, Oímbra, A Rúa, A Veiga— que arrasaron más de 130.000 hectáreas. En toda España, pero centrado en Ourense, Zamora y León, ardieron a la vez 40 grandes incendios que sumaron 312.990 hectáreas.

Esa concentración de incendios, que este año se repite al sur de Madrid y Ávila, complica el trabajo de los efectivos que los combaten. “Si cuatro grandes incendios requieren simultáneamente decenas de aeronaves, centenares de bomberos forestales, maquinaria pesada y mandos especializados, llega un momento en que los recursos disponibles deben priorizarse”, explica el ingeniero forestal Ferran Dalmau. Funciona como el triaje sanitario: se da atención prioritaria a los núcleos de población, que a menudo carecen de defensas propias. “El Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil está diseñado para responder a este tipo de situaciones: cuando la magnitud supera la capacidad de una comunidad autónoma, pueden incorporarse medios estatales y declararse una emergencia de interés nacional para unificar la dirección”, añade.

¿Y en agosto?

Julio y agosto concentran el 70% de la superficie que arde cada año en España: son, con claridad, los dos meses clave de la temporada. Los datos de lo quemado hasta ahora apuntan a dos cosas, una negativa y otra más esperanzadora.

La primera es que este año ya se han quemado, hasta el 22 de julio, más de 93.000 hectáreas en grandes incendios, según EFFIS (más de 120.000 en total). La cifra, acumulada desde comienzos de año, es casi cuatro veces la media histórica para estas fechas y más del triple de la media de los últimos diez años.

La segunda, más esperanzadora, es que la temporada aún puede torcer hacia otro lado: hay agostos moderados. En casi la mitad de los años analizados, el área quemada en ese mes se quedó por debajo de las 10.000 hectáreas, y en 7 de los 43 años, por debajo de las 5.000. Si no hay muchos grandes fuegos en lo que queda de verano, la temporada se cerraría como un año malo, pero lejos del récord.

World.title: Blood on Her Tongue: A modern vampire tale not for the squeamish
World.content:
Johanna van Veen’s gothic horror Blood on Her Tongue offers up a classic vampire tale with some modern contemplations.

The book follows Lucy Goedhart as she is called to the ominously named Zwartwater (black water) estate, where her sister has taken ill. In 1887, there isn’t much in the way of medical treatment, but Lucy’s sister Sarah isn’t fighting off a regular illness.

Sarah has become obsessed with a body found in the bog of the vast estate and since interacting with the 300-year-old corpse she has become increasingly incoherent, struggles with taking care of herself and has developed an insatiable hunger.

As Lucy tries desperately to save her sister, she finds that her sister’s husband, her sister’s doctor and childhood friend, and several other characters who are present at the remote manor house all have their own interests and motivations – some as dangerous as whatever condition is plaguing Sarah.

The book is not for those easily bothered by gore. The title – Blood on Her Tongue – is a pretty good indication of what is to come. Van Veen does not shy away from the horror elements, including two separate scenes of eyeball gouging.

Like any good horror novel, the macabre monster is not the scariest part. The threats Lucy faces are from the men surrounding her sister. Her brother-in-law attempts to seduce Lucy while badgering her to send Sarah away to an asylum.

Sarah’s doctor expresses his own interest in Lucy, pushing his vision of the future while supposedly devoting himself to his patient. The mores of 19th-century upper-class society may be the biggest piece of villainy of all.

In the tradition of Dracula, Blood on Her Tongue tells its story through letters, journal entries and newspaper clippings. The personal correspondence adds to the claustrophobia of the work, with everyone limited to an isolated house, but the media reports remind the reader that the world outside does exist.

The work is the second book from Dutch author Johanna van Veen. It was published in 2025 in English and became a USA Today bestseller. Her first book, My Darling Dreadful Thing, was nominated for the Bram Stoker Award for best horror novel. Van Veen grew up in the Netherlands as a triplet, something that influenced her writing about the sisters Lucy and Sarah.

If horror is your thing, Blood on Her Tongue will creep you out and keep you turning the pages.

You can get your copy at the American Book Center.

World.title: Thousands cross finishing line as Nijmegen Vierdaagse ends
World.content:
The 108th edition of the Nijmegense Vierdaagse (four-day march) ended on Friday, with tens of thousands of walkers being welcomed with flowers by well-wishers.

British walker Simon Brownlee crossed the finishing line ahead of the rest of the walkers for the 27th time, local media reported. Brownlee, who completed the distance before 10am, told local broadcaster Omroep Gelderland that the walk “felt like home”. “I’m happy it is over and I can now relax,” he said.

Wheelchair participant Ronald van Dort was the very first person to finish, picking up his seventh medal for completing the event.

Over 45,000 walkers from 70 countries took part in this year’s series, which is proving increasingly popular among the young. Ten years ago, 7.5% of the walkers were aged 21 to 30, but this year their number rose to over 20%.

This year the event was marred by a fatal shooting just outside the area where the Vierdaagsefeesten, the street festivities accompanying the annual four-day marches, were taking place. One man has been arrested.

The shooting, and other crowd problems, led the organisers to cancel performances by urban scene artists such as Ronnie Flex and Lil’ Kleine because their presence was “attracting the wrong sort of people”, the AD reported.

World.title: Dozens of women forced into prostitution by Romanian gang
World.content:
Dozens of women may have been forced into working as prostitutes in Amsterdam’s red light district by a Romanian gang, Dutch police confirmed on Friday.

The statement follows a joint Dutch and Romanian campaign against human trafficking in the area earlier this month. Seven men were arrested during a string of raids on July 14 – four in the Netherlands and three in Romania. All were Romanian nationals.

Shortly after the arrests, police issued a video interview with one of the victims speaking Romanian, which has led more women to come forward and has resulted in other information reaching the police, the statement said.

Police now say they have spoken to several victims and say they believe more women have been trafficked. They too are said to be Romanian.

The women were lured to Amsterdam with the promise of high earnings but found themselves forced into working in brothels and handing over their earnings to the gang. They were also forced to pay “rent” for their rooms.

None of the men had jobs but were big spenders, buying expensive clothes and cars and gambling heavily, the statement said. The gang also treated part of the red light district as their “personal kingdom”.

Four men remain in custody in the Netherlands, one of whom was extradited from Romania. Another man may also be extradited soon, RTL said. They are all suspected of human trafficking and forming a criminal organisation.

According to the Parool, two of the suspects are half brothers aged 44 and 45 who have earlier convictions for trafficking in women in Romania.

More arrests have not been ruled out.

A year ago, Dutch and Romanian police arrested 13 people in a joint investigation into human trafficking and the forced prostitution of Romanian women, mainly in and around Amsterdam.

World.title: Singer Sophie Straat cleared of discrimination over mosh pit
World.content:
Discrimination hotlines in both the Netherlands and Belgium have concluded that Dutch singer Sophie Straat did not discriminate when she asked “all white men to step back” during two of her recent performances.

Last month at the Best Kept Secret festival in Beekse Bergen, Straat — real name Sophie Schwartz — asked for space for women, queer people and people of colour in the “mosh pit”, an area in front of the stage where fans dance chaotically.

She made the same request on Monday during a performance in Ghent, Belgium.

The Dutch discrimination hotline Discriminatie.nl said it received hundreds of complaints but maintains that Straat’s comments do not amount to discrimination against white men based on their colour or gender.

“The call only concerned one short, one-off mosh pit for these groups,” said the hotline. “Therefore, visitors were not refused entry to the concert.”

Belgian authorities reached the same conclusion after receiving some 200 complaints following her performance in Ghent.

“Although the statement may be perceived as polarizing or offensive, in this context it must be seen as a symbolic and artistic expression,” a spokesperson for the Belgian discrimination hotline Unia told the Flemish broadcaster VRT.

“According to the case law of the European Court of Human Rights, artistic and political expressions enjoy broad protection under freedom of expression, even when they provoke, shock or offend.”

Hate messages and death threats

Straat wrote on Instagram earlier this month that she has received “a wave of sexist, antisemitic hate messages and (death) threats, some more explicit and creative than others”.

She has also questioned where the left-wing media has been in all this, saying the public narrative is being controlled by the right.

The singer, who was raised in a Jewish home in Amsterdam’s de Pijp neighbourhood and is known for her protest songs, has said she never wanted to exclude anyone but rather wanted to make room for people who feel unsafe in a mosh pit.

World.title: Youngster arrested for participating in sadistic online network
World.content:
Police have arrested a young man from Noord Holland who they suspect of being part of the sadistic online Com network “764”.

The public prosecution department reported the arrest on Thursday, saying the suspect encouraged underage girls to cut themselves and write his online name on a wall with their own blood—so-called “bloodsigns”.

He also is said to have prompted them to write his name on their bodies with a marker, known as“fansigns”. Both are practices within the Com movement—short for The Community—for members to gain prestige.

The suspect himself, who was also charged with aggravated assault, exploitation of underage girls and possession of images of sexual child abuse, was a minor at the time of the alleged crimes. Because of that, no further details are being released.

The Com network consists of various chat groups where members recruit vulnerable young people and force them to commit acts including assault, sexual abuse and murder.

The members, from all corners of the globe, then share images of these acts online in private chat groups, using such platforms as Telegram and Discord.

According to NOS, at least 70 Dutch people are involved in this movement known as “nihilistic extremism” because the incitement to commit such extreme violence doesn’t have a clear ideological motive.

The phenomenon is especially attractive to young men.

World.title: Dangerous drivers face extra surveillance under points system
World.content:
The police and justice ministry officials are working on a system which would see traffic offenders being given points for dangerous driving – which will lead to persistent offenders coming under extra surveillance.

Motorists who have collected six points for using a mobile phone while driving or not wearing a seatbelt would come under the tougher regime, RTL Nieuws reported on Friday. No start date has yet been set.

The points will be awarded in addition to regular fines. The number of points will depend on the seriousness of the offences and speeding tickets recorded by camera will not be included.

The new system is being devised in an effort to tackle persistent offenders who do not change their behaviour despite being fined multiple times, RTL said. Last year, almost 30,000 people would have had at least six points if the new system had been in existence.

“Research shows that people who don’t stick to the rules are often responsible for accidents,” Achilles Damen from the public prosecution department told the broadcaster.

The privacy implications of monitoring specific individuals are still being assessed, RTL said.

World.title: Ajax beat Vojvodina in Conference League qualifier, Twente lose
World.content:
Ajax kicked off their European football campaign with a 4-1 win over Serbian club Vojvodina in the second qualification round of the Conference League competition in Novi Sad on Thursday evening.

The simple win sets the Amsterdammers up in a strong position ahead of the return match next week. If Ajax win again, they will meet either Irish side Shelbourne FC or Estonian club Nõmme Kalju in the third qualification round for the third-tier European competition.

The Amsterdam goal total included one for 16-year-old debutant Mohamed Abdalla, who became the youngest player to score for a Dutch club in Europe.

There was disappointment for FC Twente, who are hoping to qualify for the group stage of the Europa League. They lost 1-2 at home to Hungarian side Ferencváros and will have to pull out all the stops during the away leg next week to remain in the competition.

If they do lose, Twente will move down to the qualification rounds of the Conference League.

PSV Eindhoven and Feyenoord have qualified directly for the Champions League while NEC is taking part in the qualification competition. AZ, as winners of the KNVB Cup last season, will take part in the Europa League competition.

World.title: Unilever backs London for food division secondary listing
World.content:
Unilever’s food division, which is being sold to US sauce and spice producer McCormick, will have a secondary listing on the London stock exchange, despite an intensive lobbying campaign to list in Amsterdam.

Unilever itself has been based in London, and listed there, since 2020.

Unilever said in a statement that the secondary listing is separate to McCormick’s plans to establish an international headquarters in the Netherlands and maintain Unilever Food’s R&D facilities and operations in Wageningen.

This “reflects its commitment to the European market and the critical role the Netherlands will continue to play in the combined company”, the statement said.

Economic affairs minister Heleen Herbert said in a reaction to the sale when it was announced in March that the cabinet had already discussed developments with Unilever and would talk to the new owner “such as about a listing on the Amsterdam stock exchange”.

Unilever’s ice cream arm, spun off in 2024, is listed on the Amsterdam stock exchange as the Magnum Ice Cream Company and is headquartered in the Dutch capital.

The sale of the food arm means there is nothing left of the original Dutch part of Unilever, which was set up in 1930 through the merger of the Dutch Margarine Unie and British soap maker Lever Brothers. Unilever now focuses on personal care and household cleaning products.

World.title: Poland identifies remains of legendary anti-communist resistance fighter
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s state Institute of National Remembrance (IPN) has identified the remains of Mieczysław Dziemieszkiewicz (pictured above on the right), a prominent figure in the underground resistance that fought against the Soviet-installed communist authorities in the years after World War Two. Dziemieszkiewicz, who was killed by the communist security services in 1951 and dumped in an unmarked mass grave, was identified through a combination of historical detective work and genetic testing, including exhuming the remains of his deceased mother and sister to obtain DNA samples. “Once again, we can say that the communist authorities did not win. Heroes prevail,” declared Krzysztof Szwagrzyk, deputy head of the IPN. “Even in the most difficult situations, we must seek the truth, find those of whom no trace was supposed to remain, and restore their names.” While World War Two officially came to an end in 1945, tens of thousands of Poles, known as the “cursed soldiers” (żolnierze wyklęci), continued to fight against the Soviets and the communist regime they installed in Poland. While most had laid down arms by 1947, some continued fighting well beyond then, including Dziemieszkiewicz, who operated under the nom de guerre “Rój” (meaning “swarm”). Dziemieszkiewicz, who was 20 years old when the war ended, came from a family that had been part of Poland’s wartime resistance. His anti-communist views were hardened when his elder brother, Roman, was killed by Red Army soldiers in 1945. After being conscripted that year into the Soviet-backed Polish People’s Army, Dziemieszkiewicz defected and joined the underground resistance forces, where he rose to command a unit tasked with eliminating regime officials and members of the communist Polish Workers Party (PPR). Dziemieszkiewicz’s group killed around two dozen members of the communist security services and more than 20 informants, according to the IPN. In 1950, the communist authorities intensified efforts to dismantle Dziemieszkiewicz’s unit, using threats and blackmail to recruit hundreds of agents and informants in an effort to locate the resistance fighters. Eventually, one such informant gave up Dziemieszkiewicz’s location in exchange for a promise to release her parents from captivity. Dziemieszkiewicz found himself surrounded by several hundred soldiers and was killed while trying to escape. After his body had been identified by his family, Dziemieszkiewicz was buried in a section of Powązki Cemetery in Warsaw where the remains of those killed by the communist security services were placed en masse in unmarked graves. Exhumations by the IPN, which was established after the fall of communism to investigate communist and Nazi crimes in Poland, have located over 200 complete bodies at that site as well as several thousand bone fragments. During that work, one set of remains was found buried with an eagle symbol and remnants of a black cloth. IPN researchers realised that the item was similar to a beret that appeared in posthumous photographs of Dziemieszkiewicz’s body taken by the communist security services. That prompted them to carry out genetic testing on the remains and compare them to samples taken from Dziemieszkiewicz’s mother and sister, who were buried in a cemetery in the town of Maków Mazowiecki. “We have found ‘Rój’, commander of one of the longest-fighting units of the independence underground,” declared the IPN on Friday, announcing the confirmation of his identity. They described Dziemieszkiewicz as “legend in life and a symbol of the fight against communist oppression”. The identification was announced today during a press conference at @PrzystanekH. The identification is the result of many years of work carried out by the IPN. It was preceded by extensive archival and investigative research, the analysis of forensic evidence, archaeological… https://t.co/Rcf4wemJFc pic.twitter.com/XgMUAgSQc6 — Institute of National Remembrance (@ipngovpl_eng) July 24, 2026 At a conference announcing the findings, the IPN noted that Dziemieszkiewicz’s remains had been located right next to those of another prominent anti-communist resistance fighter, Zygmunt Szendzielarz, who fought under the nom de guerre “Łupaszko”. “It is an incredible situation that two great and distinguished soldiers of the Polish underground lie next to each other in this part of the Powązki Cemetery,” said Szwagrzyk. However, Szendzielarz, who was executed by the communist authorities in 1951, has a contested legacy, given evidence that his unit was involved in the massacre of dozens of Lithuanian civilians. Some other “cursed soldiers” have faced similar accusations of war crimes. While it was often IPN historians who uncovered evidence of such actions, the institution has more recently begun to honour those figures, particularly under the rule of the national-conservative Law and Justice government between 2015 and 2023. Opposition MPs walked out of parliament yesterday as the chamber commemorated an underground officer who fought against Nazi-German occupation and the imposition of communism in Poland, but has also been accused of a war crime against civilians https://t.co/MIY7krOxTw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 9, 2022 Dziemieszkiewicz himself, however, like most of the cursed soldiers, has not faced such accusations. In 2007, President Lech Kaczński posthumously awarded Dziemieszkiewicz the Commander’s Cross with Star of the Order of Polonia Restituta, one of Poland’s highest honours. In 2020, his image was featured on a commemorative silver coin issued by the National Bank of Poland. Through a combination of brutal repression and offering amnesties, the communist authorities managed to end most resistance efforts by 1947. However, the last “cursed soldier” to die in combat, Józef Franczak, was killed in 1963, 18 years after the end of the war.
